# Multi-source SI network — Plan S3-C2: stage-3 P2 si-member off consensus, code layer Implementation Plan

> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking.

> **Status (2026-10-17): draft, review in progress.** Tasks 29, 30, 31 have had their adversarial review and fixes (Track B, 2026-10-17; the review facts are at the end of Appendix B); Tasks 32, 33, 34, 35, 36 have not (32 and 34 carry the AgentConnect round-2 fix 245-5); the plan consistency pass (which also writes Appendices B and C in final form) and the cross-plan pass have not run. Do not execute this plan before those passes; `2026-10-15-multi-source-si-s3cf-status.md` lists what remains and how to finish it.

**Goal:** Build the member data plane of stage-3 P2 as code, with no consensus change and no Raft-reachable call: an `si-member` process, separate from the SNode, that follows the arbiter's published manifests along the `ParentSnapshotID` chain, keeps one incarnation-scoped `hg_replica` copy of every SI table of every peer owner (static group scope: every other SI indexer), fills it only with parts a validated manifest lists, through one install gate fed by a no-split pull from the owner's `hg_safe`, a pull from a network verifier's `hg_unsafe` and a P1 object-store restore, journals what each copy holds, audits its copies at startup and after every ClickHouse restart, and shadow-verifies every sealed block of a peer owner by replaying it from DA and byte-scanning its candidate parts pulled from the owner's `hg_unsafe`; plus the ClickHouse proof that `si_member` is confined under `table_engines_require_grant`, the sentio-node release that runs it, and the integration proofs in arbiter `chpipeline` (copies follow the owner, never hold a Rejected statement's rows, survive a kill mid-stream, and the 500-blocks-per-owner shadow soak with zero mismatches, which pull requests run short at 50 blocks per owner and a manual `workflow_dispatch` runs in full, decision D38).

**Architecture:** arbiter-core adds the typed `GetSafeWatermark`, `GetManifest` and `GetBlockVerification` client reads, the canonical `wire.BlockVerification`, `wire.TableRegistrySnapshot.ManifestOwner` (the arbiter's manifest-attribution rule) and `member/manifestfeed` (one bounded, verifying follower per watermark, demultiplexed per owner, with a bounded LRU manifest store) (Task 29); the member DDL intent set in `dataplane/ddl` (`MemberPinned`, `CopyIntent`, `ScratchIntent`, `MemberUnsafeIntent` defined for Plan S3-E1, `ListMemberTables`) and `member/copyset`, the group-scoped copy reconciler with its startup refusals (Task 30); `member/sources` (owner pull resolved by `hash_of_all_files` with a row-hash fallback, peer unsafe pull, object-store restore, `missed`/`refused`/`unreachable` as outcomes) and the member's startup posture probes (engine fence, `READ ON REMOTE` without `WRITE`) (Task 31); `member/install`, the install gate executor around Plan S3-C1's pure `member/gate`, with scratch tables named `<node_id>_<boot_nonce>_<n>`, Diverged repair by `DROP PARTITION` + `ATTACH PARTITION FROM`, arithmetic closure, the per-owner journal and its crash recovery, the startup audit and self-audit, the startup drop of the node's scratch tables and the disk budget stop (Task 32); `member/shadow`, the off-consensus shadow verifier with its durable cursor and the counters of blocks, mismatches and missed scans (Task 33); `member.Role`, which composes them, its stats, the ClickHouse confinement suite run on `26.3.37.3` in CI and Cut Release and by hand on the deployed image, and the release `CORE_TAG_P2` (Task 34). sentio-node pins `CORE_TAG_P2`, adds `sentio-node si-member --config-path` as its own process reading its own config file (`storage_integrity.member`, env-only passwords and restore keys), the member metrics collector and a ClickHouse-gated install test, and releases `SN_COMMIT_P2` / `SN_DIGEST_P2` (Task 35). arbiter pins `CORE_TAG_P2` on `main` with no release (`ARBITER_PIN_P2`), proves `ManifestOwner` equals the FSM rule, gives `chpipeline` the stage-2 activation sequence for its SNode so its manifests carry `track_frontiers`, runs a member against a second, fenced ClickHouse with a 50-block soak in every `ci.yml` run, and records the full 500-block soak from a manual `workflow_dispatch` of its new `member-soak.yml` on the merge commit (Task 36, D38). Plan S3-C3 (`2026-10-15-multi-source-si-s3c3-p2-hosts-rollout.md`) puts it to work on devnet2.

**Tech Stack:** Go 1.26; Bazel 9.1.0 + Bzlmod + gazelle (arbiter-core, sentio-node, arbiter); ClickHouse 26.3 (`clickhouse/clickhouse-server:26.3.37.3` for the new CI jobs and the release gate, `us-west1-docker.pkg.dev/sentio-352722/sentio/clickhouse-server:26.3-lts-decimal512-release-2026-09-16` for the manual deployed-image confinement run; the existing ClickHouse 25.8 CI jobs stay as they are); MinIO in CI for the `READ ON S3` restore proof (Plan S3-C1's image pin); docker for the two-server harnesses; Prometheus client_golang; cobra (sentio-node commands); `gh` for PRs and the arbiter-core Cut Release workflow.

**Spec:** housegate `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-14-multi-source-si-stage3-database-groups-design.md` (PR housegate#236, spec commit `a815dd0`, merged to `main` as `fb83a97`; as amended on the plans branch `urwt/claude/ms-si-stage3-plans-cf` by the stage-3 plans PR, decision D36) — binding for the code of P2: §8.1 (the si-member process, its own users, settings profile and databases, the free-space stop; the capacity-enforcing disk class is not code), §8.2 as amended (the `si_member` grants verbatim, including `CREATE DATABASE` on `hg_replica.*` and `hg_rstage.*`, `READ ON S3`, and on `hg_rstage.*` exactly `SELECT, INSERT, ALTER, CREATE TABLE, DROP TABLE, TRUNCATE, OPTIMIZE`, never `ALL`, so no dictionary, view, `SYSTEM` or definer right there (D36; ## Global Constraints

- **Plans S3-A, S3-B and S3-C1 apply.** Every Global Constraint and clarification of those plans applies, and through them those of Plans S1-A, S1-B, S2-A and S2-B (strict decoder, request-only signatures, signed claims, tracks, quarantine, golden files, worktrees, commits, remote actions, ledger record procedure).
- **Activation model (contract §20.1, read first):** no consensus format change: no Raft command, Raft tag, Raft-reachable field, snapshot version, header byte or feature string; `arbiter.LocalNodeFeatures()` is unchanged in `CORE_TAG_P2`; arbiter gains only a dependency pin and tests, never released by this plan; a P2 member has no consensus identity, never registers and makes only the read RPCs of contract §20.1, so every component stays rollback-able.
- **Order:** Tasks 29 → 30 → 31 → 32 → 33 → 34 on one arbiter-core branch and one PR, released once as `CORE_TAG_P2`; Tasks 35 and 36 start once `CORE_TAG_P2` and `P2_CONFINEMENT` are recorded and may run in parallel; the plan starts once `P1_END` is recorded (the conventions' execution DAG), and its code reads only `HG_TAG_P1`, `CORE_TAG_P1` and `SN_COMMIT_P1`.
- **Irreversible steps:** none on devnet2; the release tags and the `main` merges are permanent records (a tag is never moved or re-cut), and `ARBITER_PIN_P2` becomes part of the base that Plan S3-D releases as `ARBITER_TAG_P4`.
- **Member safety invariants (contract §22–§23):** the member never creates, opens or writes `hg_safe`, `hg_unsafe` or `hg_promote` on its own ClickHouse; it writes only into `hg_replica` and `hg_rstage`; it never issues `REPLACE PARTITION`, `OPTIMIZE`, `TRUNCATE` or `SYSTEM DROP REPLICA` (spec §8.2 grants `TRUNCATE` and `OPTIMIZE` on `hg_rstage.*` only, D36; the role uses neither), and creates no replicated table in P2 (`MemberUnsafeIntent` has no caller); it reaches other ClickHouses only through `NOT OVERRIDABLE` named collections, never with a host, user or password in SQL; it refuses to start unless its engine fence is live and `remote()` is read-only for its user.
- **production rule:** this plan changes no production file; every name production consumes (config keys, environment variables, container and process names, metric names, the `si_member` grants, collection names, the storage policy) is binding for Plan S3-C3 as contract §23–§24 spells it.
- **Runbook conventions:** this plan has no runbook and no live task; local evidence goes under `$si_evidence` (contract §20.4, mode 700, created fresh) and is never committed; commands handed to the user in chat are fish (`bash <script> <args>` or `bash -c '...'` wrappers allowed); Plan S3-C3's P2 runbook cites §20–§24.
- **Passwords and keys (S3-B K16):** the `si_member` password comes only from `STORAGE_INTEGRITY_MEMBER_CLICKHOUSE_PASSWORD` and the restore key only from `STORAGE_INTEGRITY_MEMBER_RESTORE_ACCESS_KEY_ID` / `STORAGE_INTEGRITY_MEMBER_RESTORE_SECRET`; a YAML key for any of them is refused; nothing prints, logs or puts them on argv (every config type redacts in `String()` and `LogValue()`); test users get passwords from `crypto/rand` inside the test; the CI ClickHouse `default` keeps the posture Plan S3-A gives it.
- **No live action.** Pushes, PRs, merges, release workflows, workflow dispatches (Task 36's `member-soak.yml`) and tags need explicit user confirmation in chat, each for its own step; no task touches devnet2, a CHI, a Secret or a consensus parameter.
- **Never edit existing golden or vector files:** everything Plans S2-A and S3-A list, plus `pre_tracks_golden.json`, the `l3_track_golden_test.go` constants and both repositories' `conformance/stage3_reads_test.go` (arbiter-proto's and arbiter-core's; decision D25 lets only Plans S3-D and S3-E1 change its count literals, and this plan changes nothing in it); this plan adds no frozen fixture.
- **Repository commands, worktrees, commits, releases:** contract §20.4 and Plan S3-A's contract §6; commits end with `Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>`, PR bodies with `🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)`; markdown is never hard-wrapped; code comments in English; TDD in each repository's test style.
- **Hunks are anchored on the base revisions.** Tasks were drafted in parallel and anchor on `origin/main` before Plans S3-A, S3-B and S3-C1; when a hunk overlaps an edit of those plans or of an earlier task here (Tasks 29–34 all edit arbiter-core's `member/` tree and `.github/workflows/ci.yml`; Plan S3-C1 Task 23 extracts `dataplane/chparts` from `snode`), apply the later intent on top of the earlier change. The contract and the named tests are binding; line anchors are guidance.
- **Ledger (S3-B decision D23, Plan S3-C1 contract §19).** Each recording task (34, 35, 36) writes its values and its run record into Appendix C of this plan file on the ledger copy with `$HOME/.cache/s3-ledger/s3-ledger.py`, in one commit through the record procedure, and checks it back before it ends; every reader takes values only from the ledger copy. The ledger copy is the one `s3-ledger.py ref <housegate> s3c2` names: the plans branch `urwt/claude/ms-si-stage3-plans-cf` until the stage-3 plans PR merges, `main` afterwards (decision D34).
- **References.** `contract §N` points to Plan S3-A's Appendix A for §0–§6, Plan S3-B's for §7–§15, Plan S3-C1's for §16–§19 and this plan's Appendix A for §20–§24; a task group's "Facts" point to Appendix B; Appendix C records the ledger values and run records as they are made.

## Plan clarifications (binding)

The spec and Plans S3-A, S3-B and S3-C1 leave these P2 code details open; each is resolved here and binding for Plans S3-C2 through S3-F.

- **K29 — Member ids (spec §8.5 line 192, §6.1 line 104).** The spec names scratch tables `<node_id>_<boot_nonce>_<n>` and requires a member's `node_id` to be unused by every SNode and verifier, but a P2 member has no consensus identity yet. Resolution: the ids are pinned now and never reused: `member-a` (host indexer-a, indexer id 0), `member-b` (host indexer-b, indexer id 1), `member-c` (host indexer-c, `INDEXER_C_ID`); none is, or ever becomes, an SNode, verifier or voter id; the P2 id is the member's P6 VERIFIER node id and its Keeper replica name. Plan S3-C3 records them as `MEMBER_IDS` in the multi-source runbook's §1.2 ledger. Code: a node id must match `^[a-z][a-z0-9-]{0,30}[a-z0-9]$`; at startup the member refuses an id that is in the arbiter's purge node set or equals an `si_indexers` entry's `snode_node_id` (`copyset.ErrNodeIDInUse`, contract §21.6). Plan S3-E1 Task 63 refines step (6) for a member with `Config.Consensus`: its own id in the purge node set (its own VERIFIER registration) is accepted; an SNode's id and an id the registry serves as another host's group member are still refused. Why: no re-keying at P6, stable scratch prefixes, and a collision would make the reconcilers of P6 treat the member's replica as another node's.
- **K30 — Process layout (spec §8.1 "separate from the SNode", §8.2 "its password is mounted only into the reconciler", §11 "authenticated local status endpoint").** Resolution: the si-member gets its own StatefulSet, never a container of the host pod; its container `si-member` runs `sentio-node si-member --config-path <file>` and connects as `si_member` only; the pod reserves a second container slot `si-member-reconciler` (the `hg_member_unsafe` reconciler as `si_member_ddl`, Plans S3-E1 and S3-F) that stays empty until §10.4 step 6; the process reads its own file through `config.LoadSIMemberConfig`, never the host's `LoadConfig` (which validates the node config and needs `PRIVATE_KEY`); the authenticated status endpoint is a Service with a bearer token, implemented by Plan S3-C4 (Tasks 45–46); the token has its own Secret `<release>-si-member-status-token`, never the Secret that holds the `si_member` password, and on the host side only the host's sentio-node mounts it (decision D29); P2's binary serves only Prometheus metrics and `GET /readyz` on `metrics_listen` and reads no token. Why: the host pod's checksum (production `charts/sentio-node/templates/node.yaml:486`) hashes the host values, so a member container there would restart the SNode, and with it the owner's track, on every member change; a separate pod keeps the member's crashes and memory away from the SNode (§8.1); deciding the reconciler slot now means Plan S3-F does not re-architect the pod.
- **K31 — The copy reconciler is a new package (spec §8.3).** The spec says the member's reconciler "takes the set of groups it belongs to … instead of the stage-1 `Owner` filter". Resolution: `member/copyset` is a new package, not a mode of `dataplane/tableset`: it keeps exactly one MergeTree copy per Pending or Active incarnation owned by an owner in its scope (P2: the static `peers` list, every enrolled SI indexer but the host), drops a copy from Retiring on, and drops every other table of `hg_replica` (Purged, Refused, unknown comment, foreign owner); it never opens a protocol database and never reports a purge. Why: tableset's three-table shape, `ensurePresent`, sweep and decommission logic (`arbiter-core:dataplane/tableset/reconciler.go:533-587`, `:672-842`) are SNode- and Keeper-specific, while a copy is regenerable local state.
- **K32 — Database creation (spec §8.2 line 171–172, amended in housegate#236).** The original grant lists gave `si_member` no `CREATE DATABASE` on `hg_replica.*` and `si_member_ddl` none on `hg_member_unsafe.*`. Resolution (spec amended): `si_member` holds `CREATE DATABASE` on `hg_replica.*` and `hg_rstage.*`, and the member creates both with `CREATE DATABASE IF NOT EXISTS` without `ENGINE` (`ddl.EnsureMemberDatabases`); `hg_member_unsafe` is never created by `si_member` (Plan S3-E1's reconciler creates it as `si_member_ddl`, whose amended grants include `CREATE DATABASE` on `hg_member_unsafe.*`); Task 34's confinement suite measures both users' grants on 26.3. Why: no admin runbook step is needed, and 26.3 checks a database `ENGINE` as `TABLE ENGINE ON <engine>`, which `GRANT` cannot name.
- **K33 — The restore right (spec §8.2, §8.6, amended in housegate#236).** The object-store restore source needs a source right the original §8.2 list omitted. Resolution (spec amended): `si_member` holds `READ ON S3`; the restore source runs as `si_member` with the per-statement `S3()` keys of Plan S3-C1's K23, read from the member's environment; Task 34's `TestConfinement_SIMemberRestoreNeedsReadOnS3` proves on 26.3 against MinIO that the restore succeeds with the grant and is refused (497) without it. Why: restore is the bootstrap and large-gap source of §8.6 and must work under the fenced user, not an admin.
- **K34 — Shadow semantics (spec §16 row P2: "shadow verification that replays from DA and scans each candidate part after pulling it from the owner's `hg_unsafe`").** The spec does not say what a mismatch is, nor how to treat QuorumFailed or Rejected blocks and evidence recorded after the latch. Resolution: the shadow never re-derives check flags or the verdict (FSM logic, `arbiter:fsm/threeway.go:35-179`); it compares bodies: its own receipt's `Hash()` with every recorded attestation's `receipt_hash` (kind `receipt`), and its own scan of each candidate part with the scanned hash every recorded byte-side scan reports for that part (kind `scan`), for evaluated evidence and evidence recorded after the latch alike ("compared as recorded"); the verdict is read only from evaluated evidence, and a block whose quorum passed while the shadow scans one of its candidate parts to a hash other than the claimed one is kind `claim`. A QuorumFailed or Rejected block therefore must reproduce the honest verifiers' receipts and scans and counts no mismatch when it does. A candidate part already cleaned from the owner's `hg_unsafe` is a missed scan, counted apart, never a mismatch; a block whose verdict is not evaluated within `VerdictWait` is compared against the evidence recorded so far and counted `unverdicted`. Why: the receipt is replica-independent (`housegate:pkg/replay/types.go:335-353`), so equality with every honest verifier is exact, and porting the three checks would duplicate consensus logic outside the FSM.
- **K35 — Bounds on pulls and on the member disk (spec §8.1 "installs stop when the member disk crosses a free-space threshold", §8.6).** A no-split pull materialises a whole part in one insert block, and `si_member`'s grants (§8.2) include no system table that reports free space. Resolution: the `si_member` profile's `max_memory_usage` bounds the largest pullable part; a pull refused by ClickHouse (`MEMORY_LIMIT_EXCEEDED` 241, `TOO_MANY_SIMULTANEOUS_QUERIES` 202, `TIMEOUT_EXCEEDED` 159) is outcome `refused` and the installer moves to the next source, never retrying a source within one pass; a part that every source refused, missed or could not reach is deferred with a backoff from 1 m doubling to 30 m (`install.ErrNoSourceSucceeded`). The free-space threshold is a member disk budget: `disk_budget_bytes` and `stop_installs_ratio` (default 0.8) over the summed `bytes_on_disk` of every part, active or not, of `hg_replica` and `hg_rstage` in `system.parts`; above it installs pause (`install.ErrInstallsPaused`) while audits and the shadow continue. On devnet2, Plan S3-C3 sets `disk_budget_bytes` to the member disk's total and `stop_installs_ratio` to 0.5, the P2 exit's 50 % (decision D28); the code default stays 0.8. The node SSD itself is bounded by ClickHouse's `keep_free_space_bytes` (Plan S3-C3) and watched by its alerts. Why: a refused pull must fall back to restore and never loop, and a budget needs no grant beyond §8.2 on devnet2, whose member disk is a directory on the data volume (Plan S3-C3 K40).
- **K36 — Journal recovery and Foreign (spec §8.5 steps 4–7, §8.7).** A crash between `ATTACH PARTITION FROM` and the journal write leaves an unjournaled part, and the spec says a Foreign scratch quarantines "the table locally". Resolution: at startup and after every ClickHouse restart the installer reconciles the journal with `system.parts`: a part present locally but not journaled is scanned by name (`chexec.ScanParts`) and adopted only if its row hash is one the journaled target manifest still needs for that partition; anything else is Diverged and repaired; nothing is scanned in full outside the rate-limited self-audit. Foreign quarantines the whole table: the copy stops installing (and, from P3, is never served), its scratch is kept for forensics, the journal marks it, metrics count it; only an operator clears it, offline, with `sentio-node si-member clear-foreign --table <db.table>`, after which the copy is dropped and rebuilt. Why: arithmetic closure needs exact knowledge of what a partition holds, and a transport that delivered foreign bytes once is not trusted for the rest of that table until a human has looked.
- **K37 — Feed shape (spec §8.4).** The spec asks for a `ParentSnapshotID` walk, never `GetManifestByBlock`, and a full fetch only when an owner's entry changed. Resolution: one `manifestfeed.Follower` per process follows the watermark and demultiplexes per owner: each accepted manifest yields every owner's `replay.OwnerEntry` and the owners whose entry changed; the walk from the watermark back to the last accepted manifest is bounded (`DefaultMaxWalk` 64 hops) and beyond it the follower accepts the verified watermark manifest alone (a full fetch, counted); the follower refuses a watermark manifest without `track_frontiers` (its manifest store still serves a pre-tracks manifest as a replay base), so the member has no pre-tracks mode, and arbiter `chpipeline` (pre-registry and pre-tracks at its base) runs the registry, signed-claims and tracks activations for its one SNode before a member starts (Task 36), leaving more owners to Plan S3-E4 Task 78; manifests are cached in a bounded LRU (`DefaultCacheEntries` 16) that also serves the shadow's replays. Why: three owners share one watermark, so one follower is cheaper than three; the walk bound caps the leader barriers a stale journal costs; and an owner entry exists only in track-aware manifests.

Plan S3-C3 consumes all six produced names (K38 reads `P2_INTEGRATION_SOAK`'s run record as the 500-blocks-per-owner exit criterion).

## Review Focus

1. **A manifest that lies, or a feed that falls far behind.** Expected: the follower accepts a manifest only when its `snapshot_id` is the requested id and its own recomputed root, every partition root equals the sum of its listed parts, and it descends from the last accepted manifest; it refuses a watermark manifest without `track_frontiers` and any owner entry that goes back; nothing is installed from a refused manifest; a gap of more than 64 publications ends in a full fetch of the verified watermark manifest, counted; `GetManifestByBlock` is never called; the replay store still serves a pre-tracks base manifest. Tests: Task 29 `TestVerifyAcceptsOnlyTheRequestedIDThatIsItsOwnRoot`, `TestVerifyRefusesPartitionRootsThatDoNotSumToTheirParts`, `TestFollowerRefusesAWatermarkThatDoesNotDescend`, `TestFollowerRefusesAnOwnerEntryThatGoesBack`, `TestFollowerRefusesAManifestWithoutTrackFrontiers`, `TestFollowerFallsBackToAFullFetchBeyondMaxWalk`, `TestFollowerNeverCallsGetManifestByBlock`, `TestStoreKeepsOnlyVerifiedManifests`, `TestStoreServesAPreTracksManifest`.
2. **A partition the gate cannot simply append to.** A local copy that is not a sub-multiset of the manifest, a scratch that holds a split, a doubled insert, a zero-row rename race or a foreign part, a pull refused by the memory limit, an owner that is unreachable or already cleaned the part, an owner that rebuilt its parts in a partition behind more than eight other partitions (or among more than eight parts) of the same row count, a bootstrapping owner, a full member disk. Expected: Diverged is rebuilt in a fresh scratch and repaired with `DROP PARTITION` then `ATTACH PARTITION … FROM`, never `REPLACE PARTITION`, and the repair holds across a ClickHouse reload inside the outdated-part window; a split moves to the next source; a rename race or a doubled insert is retried once from a clean scratch; Foreign quarantines the whole table locally, keeps the scratch and is cleared only offline; a closure or partition-set mismatch installs nothing; a refused, missed or unreachable source moves to the next one and a part no source delivers is deferred with a backoff, never retried in a loop; the row-hash fallback lists only the needed partition (ClickHouse's `partition_id`, computed on the member's server) before its bound and continues after its last candidate on the next fetch (review fix 245-3); while an owner has no journaled entry each copy's first fetch tries the restore before the owner pull, once per copy and process (review fix 245-4); installs pause above the disk budget while audits and the shadow continue. Tests: Task 32 `TestInstallDivergedPartitionIsRebuiltWithDropAndAttach`, `TestInstallDivergedRepairSurvivesAReloadInsideTheOutdatedWindow`, `TestInstallNeverIssuesReplacePartition`, `TestInstallForeignScratchQuarantinesTheTableAndKeepsTheScratch`, `TestInstallSplitFallsBackToTheNextSource`, `TestInstallRenameRaceRetriesOnceFromACleanScratch`, `TestInstallDoubledRetryIsDroppedAndRetriedOnce`, `TestInstallClosureFailureInstallsNothing`, `TestInstallPartitionSetMismatchInstallsNothing`, `TestInstallRefusedPullFallsBackToRestoreAndDefers`, `TestInstallBootstrapProbesTheRestoreOncePerCopy`, `TestInstallsPauseAboveTheDiskBudget`; Task 31 `TestOwnerPullMemoryLimitIsRefusedNotRetried`, `TestUnsafePullOfACleanedPartIsMissed`, `TestPullFromAnUnreachableOwnerIsUnreachable`, `TestOwnerPullFallsBackToTheRowHashWhenTheOwnerRebuiltItsParts`, `TestOwnerPullFallbackScopesTheNeededPartition`, `TestOwnerPullFallbackListsAfterItsCursor`.
3. **A crash, a kill or a ClickHouse restart in the middle of an install.** Expected: a part attached but not journaled is adopted only if the journaled target still needs its row hash, else its partition is Diverged and repaired; equal-hash twins (same row hash and `hash_of_all_files`) keep the journaled name and the others are dropped with `DROP PART`; the audit reruns when the ClickHouse uptime regresses and gates readiness until clean; the startup audit runs after the first copyset pass, and a copy the copyset makes ready later (one it created again empty while the journal is at the watermark) is audited before any pass may skip it as current (review fix 245-1); a Diverged partition or unjournaled part an audit records is repaired by re-applying the newest offered update, without waiting for a new manifest (review fix 245-2); after a pass that committed some owners and failed for another, the retry is that newest update and an owner's journal entry never goes back, so the owners that committed keep their parts (review fix 245-5); startup drops exactly this node's `hg_rstage` tables; a second process on the same state directory is refused; a member killed mid-stream converges to the latest manifest on restart. Tests: Task 32 `TestInstallRecoversAPartAttachedBeforeTheJournalWrite`, `TestStartupAuditDropsEqualHashTwinsWithDropPart`, `TestStartupAuditMarksAnyOtherMismatchDiverged`, `TestAStartWithACurrentJournalAuditsTheCopiesItFindsLater`, `TestAnAuditThatFindsDamageAsksForAPass`, `TestAuditRerunsWhenClickHouseUptimeRegresses`, `TestStartupDropsOnlyThisNodesStageTables`, `TestApplyNeverTakesAnOwnerBackAfterAPartialPass`; Task 34 `TestRoleRefusesASecondProcessOnTheStateDir`, `TestRoleIsReadyOnlyAfterACleanAuditAndAManifest`, `TestRoleAuditsTheCopiesTheFirstCopysetPassMadeReady`, `TestRoleRepairsWhatAnAuditFoundWithoutANewManifest`, `TestRoleRetriesTheNewestOfferedUpdateAfterAPartialPass`; Task 36 `TestPipeline_MemberKilledMidStreamResumesFromItsJournal`.
4. **A member that could write where it must not.** Expected: the member refuses to start when its server accepts an ungranted engine (the fence is off), when `remote()` is writable for its user, when its node id is an SNode's or in the purge node set, when its databases intersect the protocol databases, when a peer is not enrolled or is the host, when a YAML password or restore key is present or no username is set; as `si_member` on `26.3.37.3` and on the deployed image, each of the eight `Replicated*MergeTree` engines and `Buffer`/`Distributed`/`Merge`/`Alias` in `hg_rstage` and `hg_replica`, a `Replicated` database, `ATTACH PARTITION FROM` / `MOVE PARTITION TO TABLE` / a materialized view into `hg_member_unsafe`, a dictionary, a view with another definer or with `SQL SECURITY NONE`, and a `SYSTEM` command in `hg_rstage` or `hg_replica` (the explicit `hg_rstage` list, never `ALL`, decision D36; plain views there stay possible through 26.3's implicit `CREATE VIEW`, which the suite measures and records), a write through `remote()`, a collection override and `SYSTEM DROP REPLICA` are refused with 497 while every right the role needs works; `si_member_ddl`'s profile refuses a replica created with merges allowed; the role calls only the read RPCs of contract §20.1. Tests: Task 34 `TestConfinement_SIMemberCreatesNoReplicatedEngine`, `TestConfinement_SIMemberCreatesNoBufferDistributedMergeOrAlias`, `TestConfinement_SIMemberCreatesNoReplicatedDatabase`, `TestConfinement_SIMemberCannotMoveDataIntoMemberUnsafe`, `TestConfinement_SIMemberCannotWriteThroughRemote`, `TestConfinement_SIMemberCannotOverrideACollection`, `TestConfinement_SIMemberCannotDropAReplica`, `TestConfinement_SIMemberHasNoDictionarySystemOrDefinerRight`, `TestConfinement_SIMemberHoldsEveryRightItsRoleNeeds`, `TestConfinement_SIMemberDDLProfileRefusesAMergesAllowedReplica`, `TestRoleRefusesToStartWithoutTheEngineFence`, `TestRoleRefusesAWritableRemote`, `TestRoleRefusesANodeIDInUse`, `TestRoleRefusesAPeerThatIsNotEnrolled`, `TestRoleCallsOnlyReadRPCs`; Task 30 `TestCopysetRefusesMemberDatabasesThatIntersectTheSNodes`, `TestCheckNodeIDUnusedRefusesAnSNodeOrVerifierID`; Task 35 `TestSIMemberConfigRefusesAClickhousePasswordKey`, `TestSIMemberConfigRefusesRestoreKeysInYAML`, `TestSIMemberConfigRequiresAUsername`, `TestSIMemberConfigNeverPrintsASecret`.
5. **Shadow verification of a fraud block, a cleaned candidate or a verdict that never comes.** Expected: a Rejected block (a lying candidate part hash or partition sum) reproduces every honest verifier's receipt and scans and counts zero mismatches; a `claim` mismatch arises only on a block whose quorum passed; evidence recorded after the latch is compared by its recorded body; a candidate already cleaned from the owner's `hg_unsafe` is a missed scan, never a mismatch; a block without a verdict after `VerdictWait` is compared and counted `unverdicted`; blocks of the host, of other owners and transition blocks are skipped; the cursor survives a restart and the shadow never submits; in `chpipeline` at least 500 blocks of the owner are shadow-verified with zero mismatches in the dispatched full soak (50 in every `ci.yml` run, decision D38) and the copies never hold a Rejected statement's rows. Tests: Task 33 `TestShadowReproducesARejectedBlocksReceipts`, `TestShadowClaimMismatchOnlyForAQuorumPassBlock`, `TestShadowComparesEvidenceRecordedAfterTheLatchAsRecorded`, `TestShadowCountsACleanedCandidateAsAMissedScan`, `TestShadowCountsAnUnverdictedBlockAfterVerdictWait`, `TestShadowSkipsBlocksOfItsHostOtherOwnersAndTransitions`, `TestShadowCursorSurvivesARestart`, `TestShadowNeverSubmitsAnything`; Task 36 `TestPipeline_MemberCopiesNeverHoldRowsOfARejectedStatement`, `TestPipeline_MemberShadowSoak`.

Plan S3-C1 complete (`HG_TAG_P1`, `CORE_TAG_P1`, `SN_COMMIT_P1` / `SN_DIGEST_P1` released and `P1_END` recorded in its Appendix C) → 29 → 30 → 31 → 32 → 33 → 34 (arbiter-core, one branch `urwt/claude/multi-source-s3c2`, one PR, `CORE_TAG_P2`, then the deployed-image confinement run and `P2_CONFINEMENT`) → 35 (sentio-node, `SN_COMMIT_P2` / `SN_DIGEST_P2`) and 36 (arbiter, `ARBITER_PIN_P2`, `P2_INTEGRATION_SOAK`; it records only after its merge and the dispatched `member-soak.yml` run on that merge commit, decision D38) in parallel. Tasks 31–33 may be drafted in parallel with 29–30 against contract §21–§22, but they apply on top of them (the hunk rule): 31 uses Task 30's `ScratchIntent`; 32 uses 29's `Update`, 30's `copyset` and 31's `sources`; 33 uses 29's reads and store, 31's `NewOwnerUnsafePull` and 32's `ScratchPrefix`; 34 composes all of them. Task 35's ClickHouse test and Task 36's harness both need `CORE_TAG_P2`. A task that reads a ledger value starts only once the recording task's record has passed its R4 check. Notes:
- **Reads only, no consensus change (contract §20.1).** The three methods call existing `SafeState` RPCs (`GetBlockVerification` since `PROTO_TAG`); nothing here is Raft-reachable, no golden or `conformance` file changes, and `arbiter.LocalNodeFeatures()` is untouched. `GetManifestByBlock` is never called: `Source` has no by-block method, and `TestFollowerNeverCallsGetManifestByBlock` runs the follower through a real `dataplane.Client` against a server whose interceptor records every method and whose `GetManifestByBlock` fails the test.
- **Refusals are not retried.** `WithLeaderRetry` follows NotLeader and retries only Unavailable, DeadlineExceeded, Canceled and Unknown (`retryableStatus`), so NotFound and Unimplemented come back at once; the tests time it. `GetBlockVerification` reuses Plan S3-A's `stage3ReadError`, so an arbiter older than `ARBITER_TAG` answers `ErrStage3ReadsUnavailable` exactly like `GetPartitionStates` does; `GetSafeWatermark` and `GetManifest` exist on every arbiter: `GetManifest` maps NotFound to `ErrManifestNotFound`, and both pass every other refusal through unchanged.
- **Why a snapshot id must be its own root.** Every manifest the arbiter publishes is sealed with an empty `SnapshotID` (`arbiter:orchestrator/promotion.go:262-270` at `fb42260`, `:288-296` at `526a721`, Plan S3-A's merge now on `origin/main`; the snapshot-query abort child `arbiter:fsm/apply_snapshot_query_abort.go:88-92`; housegate `payloadexec.(*Executor).GenesisSnapshot`), and `Seal` then sets `SnapshotID = ManifestRoot`; `Validate` does not check that equality (it excludes the id from the root's preimage), so `Verify` does. A sealed manifest validates whatever its partition roots are, which is why `VerifyLedger` comes last: `TestVerifyRefusesPartitionRootsThatDoNotSumToTheirParts` reseals a manifest with a wrong root and with an orphan part, and only the ledger refuses them.
- **Walk arithmetic.** From the watermark manifest W, hop k reads W's k-th ancestor id; the walk succeeds when that id is the last accepted one, refuses when it is empty, and after `MaxWalk` hops without reaching it accepts W alone (`FullFetch`, `Walked == MaxWalk`). A walk of d ≤ `MaxWalk` hops fetches d manifests (W and the d − 1 between, never the last accepted one), a full fetch at most `MaxWalk`; every fetch goes through the `Store`, so each is verified once and the recent ones stay cached for the shadow's replays. The owner-entry check compares W's entries with the last accepted ones (an owner missing from W counts as (0, 0)), in both cases. Only the watermark manifest must carry `track_frontiers`: a manifest without them is refused while it is the watermark (the follower stays put and counts it), and a walk from a later track-aware watermark crosses it, since `Verify` does not require frontiers (`TestFollowerRefusesAManifestWithoutTrackFrontiers`).
- **An entry that goes back (the rule Tasks 32 and 34 cite, review fix 245-5).** An owner's entry in the watermark manifest W goes back when its `SafeBlockSeq` or its `AppliedPromotionSeq` is below the last accepted entry's, compared component by component: (9, 4) → (9, 3) and (10, 5) → (9, 7) both go back; an equal entry has not moved; an owner the last accepted entries list but W does not counts as (0, 0), so it goes back unless it was (0, 0); an owner W lists for the first time never does. On one chain the arbiter never publishes such an entry: a track's entry is Carried verbatim, Initialised once, or Advanced to (its prefix, the global `PromotionSeq`), and both grow (`arbiter:fsm/reads_manifest.go:212-292`, `trackManifestInputsLocked`). The follower refuses such a watermark (`manifestfeed: owner %d entry went back …`, counted in `Refused`) and offers nothing from it, so every update `Run` offers descends from the last accepted manifest along `ParentSnapshotID` or, after a full fetch, is a newer watermark none of whose entries is behind; along an honest chain the manifests' `SafeBlockSeq` (the global safe prefix) never decreases, which is the order Task 34's repair target takes (`>=`, so of two manifests with one `SafeBlockSeq` the later offered wins). Task 32's `ownerAhead` applies the same rule to an owner's journaled entry before `Apply` touches its copies. `TestFollowerRefusesAnOwnerEntryThatGoesBack` pins each case, after a walk, after a full fetch and on a first fetch checked against a journal's entries.
- **Spec §8.4's "full manifest only when `track_frontiers[O]` differs".** The arbiter serves no header-only manifest read (`GetManifest` answers the whole manifest, `arbiter:server/safestate.go:39-48`), so every hop of the walk is one `GetManifest`, verified once and kept in the `Store`; the per-owner saving is `Update.Changed`, which names the owners whose entry moved so that a consumer can leave the others alone (K37). `FullFetch` keeps the contract's meaning: a watermark manifest accepted without a chain back to the last accepted one.
- **Accepting an update.** `Poll` accepts what it returns (tests and one-shot callers); `Run` accepts an update only after `onUpdate` returns nil, so a failing installer leaves the follower where it was and the next poll walks from the same manifest again (contract §21.4, "the installer's journal stays the source of truth"); `FollowerStats.UpdateFailures` counts those failures. `NewFollower` with `last` "" and a journal's `lastEntries` makes the first poll a full fetch checked against those entries; Task 34 decides which form its restart passes. In steady state a poll costs one leader barrier (the watermark read) and no fetch.
- **`Store` is not `dataplane.ManifestStore`.** The existing store is unbounded and only runs `Validate`; the member needs a bound (K37: 16 entries by default) and the full acceptance rule, so `ManifestStore` stays unchanged and unused by the member (contract §21.1).
- **`TestBlockVerificationFromPBReadsEveryField` fails when a proto field is added.** It builds the message through protoreflect with one `case` per field name of `pb.BlockVerification`, `pb.StatementCandidates` and `pb.VerifierEvidence`, and fails on an unknown field; of `pb.L3BlockHeader` it names the seven fields the view reads and the anchor, sets every other string field to a value the view must not read, and fails on an unknown field of any other kind. Plan S3-E1 (fields 14–22, its contract §39 and the `BlockVerification` extension of its §41) extends the Go type and the cases together. The fixture gives each bool its own pattern across the statements, the three evidence entries and three flag rows, so a converter that swaps two fields or reads the transition flag from the track fails too (checked in drafting by mutating each converter line).
- **The FSM equality proof is Task 36's** (`TestManifestTableOwnerMatchesWireManifestOwner`, contract §24.8); here the four tests pin the ported rule, including that Refused is skipped before origin and add block are looked at, as the FSM does.
- **No PR here.** Tasks 29–34 share the branch `urwt/claude/multi-source-s3c2`; Task 34 opens the one PR and releases `CORE_TAG_P2`. This task records nothing in the ledger.
- **Commit identity (user rule).** This task creates the worktree Tasks 30–34 commit in, so Step 1 gives it its own identity `poetry <chen@sentio.xyz>` before the first commit (the global `uranuswch@gmail.com` must never author or co-author a commit: GitHub would add it as a co-author of the squash merge); every commit block prints the author, Step 14 checks every commit of the branch, and Task 34 checks them again before the squash merge.
- **Verified** (adversarial review, 2026-10-17) on a `git archive` of arbiter-core `origin/main` `cfd4f42` with Plan S3-C1 Tasks 23–24's reviewed text applied (the `CORE_TAG_P1` stand-in, its BUILD files by gazelle), against housegate `origin/main` `ed24705` with Plan S3-C1 Task 22's reviewed text applied as the `HG_TAG_P1` stand-in (through `replace` for `go test` and `--override_module` for Bazel): Step 3's checks printed what they expect; the hunks of this task, applied verbatim step by step by a script, failed to build at Steps 4, 6, 8, 10 and 12 with exactly the `undefined` lists stated (under `go test` and under Bazel 9.1.0 offline) and passed at Steps 5, 7, 9, 11 and 13; gazelle wrote exactly the BUILD changes stated (Step 9's grep printed `2`, Step 10's file held the test target alone, Step 13's file is byte-equal to its block); Step 14 passed (public boundary, gofmt, no BUILD diff after gazelle, `bazel build //...`, `bazel test //...` 21 of 21, the race run of the three targets); `go vet` clean and `go test -race -count=3` of the three packages passed; mutations of the go-back rule (either component alone, `&&` for `||`, ignoring an owner that disappears), of `Run`'s accept-after-callback and of the walk each failed a named test; the arbiter's `GetBlockVerification` server (`arbiter:server/safestate_stage3.go:71-88`, `:133-188`) fills exactly the fields the converter reads; the identity lines of Step 1 and the author checks ran in a scratch worktree and printed `poetry <chen@sentio.xyz>`.

```go
func appendMessages[M proto.Message](r protoreflect.Message, fd protoreflect.FieldDescriptor, ms []M) {
	list := r.Mutable(fd).List()
	for _, m := range ms {
		list.Append(protoreflect.ValueOfMessage(m.ProtoReflect()))
	}
}

func appendStrings(r protoreflect.Message, fd protoreflect.FieldDescriptor, ss []string) {
	list := r.Mutable(fd).List()
	for _, s := range ss {
		list.Append(protoreflect.ValueOfString(s))
	}
}

// headerThroughReflection sets every pb.L3BlockHeader field: those of the view
// from v, every other one to a value the view must not read.
func headerThroughReflection(t *testing.T, v BlockHeaderView) *pb.L3BlockHeader {
	t.Helper()
	m := &pb.L3BlockHeader{}
	r := m.ProtoReflect()
	fields := r.Descriptor().Fields()
	for i := 0; i < fields.Len(); i++ {
		fd := fields.Get(i)
		switch fd.Name() {
		case "l3_block_seq":
			r.Set(fd, protoreflect.ValueOfUint64(v.L3BlockSeq))
		case "statement_seq_start":
			r.Set(fd, protoreflect.ValueOfUint64(v.StatementSeqStart))
		case "statement_count":
			r.Set(fd, protoreflect.ValueOfUint32(v.StatementCount))
		case "prev_safe_snapshot_id":
			r.Set(fd, protoreflect.ValueOfString(v.PrevSafeSnapshotID))
		case "prev_state_root":
			r.Set(fd, protoreflect.ValueOfString(v.PrevStateRoot))
		case "table_set_transition":
			if v.IsTableSetTransition {
				r.Set(fd, protoreflect.ValueOfMessage((&pb.TableSetTransition{Retires: []string{"db.old"}, NewSchemaRoot: "0xschema-next"}).ProtoReflect()))
			}
		case "track":
			if v.TrackIndexerID != nil {
				r.Set(fd, protoreflect.ValueOfMessage((&pb.L3BlockTrack{IndexerId: *v.TrackIndexerID}).ProtoReflect()))
			}
		case "l2_anchor_ref":
			r.Set(fd, protoreflect.ValueOfMessage(AnchorRefToPB(arbiter.AnchorRef{L3BlockHash: "0xnot-read", StateRoot: "0xnot-read"}).ProtoReflect()))
		default:
			if fd.Kind() != protoreflect.StringKind {
				t.Fatalf("%s has no case: decide whether BlockHeaderView reads it", fd.FullName())
			}
			r.Set(fd, protoreflect.ValueOfString("not-read-"+string(fd.Name())))
		}
	}
	return m
}

func statementThroughReflection(t *testing.T, v StatementCandidates) *pb.StatementCandidates {
	t.Helper()
	m := &pb.StatementCandidates{}
	r := m.ProtoReflect()
	fields := r.Descriptor().Fields()
	for i := 0; i < fields.Len(); i++ {
		fd := fields.Get(i)
		switch fd.Name() {
		case "statement_seq":
			r.Set(fd, protoreflect.ValueOfUint64(v.StatementSeq))
		case "statement_id":
			r.Set(fd, protoreflect.ValueOfString(v.StatementID))
		case "status":
			r.Set(fd, protoreflect.ValueOfString(v.Status))
		case "source_node":
			r.Set(fd, protoreflect.ValueOfString(v.SourceNode))
		case "rc_bound":
			r.Set(fd, protoreflect.ValueOfBool(v.RCBound))
		case "source_claim_root":
			r.Set(fd, protoreflect.ValueOfString(v.SourceClaimRoot))
		case "candidate_parts":
			appendMessages(r, fd, mapSlice(v.CandidateParts, CandidatePartToPB))
		case "partition_new_part_sums":
			appendMessages(r, fd, mapSlice(v.PartitionNewPartSums, PartitionLtHashSumToPB))
		case "unpromoted_part_row_lthashes":
			appendStrings(r, fd, v.UnpromotedPartRowLtHashes)
		default:
			t.Fatalf("%s has no case: StatementCandidates and this test must carry it", fd.FullName())
		}
	}
	return m
}

// blockVerificationThroughReflection builds v's message field by field
// through protoreflect, never through BlockVerificationToPB. Every field of
// pb.BlockVerification, pb.StatementCandidates and pb.VerifierEvidence needs a
// case, so a field added to the proto fails here until the Go type carries it.
func blockVerificationThroughReflection(t *testing.T, v BlockVerification) *pb.BlockVerification {
	t.Helper()
	m := &pb.BlockVerification{}
	r := m.ProtoReflect()
	fields := r.Descriptor().Fields()
	for i := 0; i < fields.Len(); i++ {
		fd := fields.Get(i)
		switch fd.Name() {
		case "header":
			r.Set(fd, protoreflect.ValueOfMessage(headerThroughReflection(t, v.Header).ProtoReflect()))
		case "chain_hash":
			r.Set(fd, protoreflect.ValueOfString(v.ChainHash))
		case "replay_job":
			r.Set(fd, protoreflect.ValueOfMessage(ReplayJobToPB(v.ReplayJob).ProtoReflect()))
		case "statements":
			list := r.Mutable(fd).List()
			for _, s := range v.Statements {
				list.Append(protoreflect.ValueOfMessage(statementThroughReflection(t, s).ProtoReflect()))
			}
		case "scan_parts":
			appendMessages(r, fd, mapSlice(v.ScanParts, partRefToPB))
		case "source_nodes":
			appendStrings(r, fd, v.SourceNodes)
		case "verifier_set":
			appendStrings(r, fd, v.VerifierSet)
		case "evidence":
			list := r.Mutable(fd).List()
			for _, e := range v.Evidence {
				list.Append(protoreflect.ValueOfMessage(evidenceThroughReflection(t, e).ProtoReflect()))
			}
		case "verdict_evaluated":
			r.Set(fd, protoreflect.ValueOfBool(v.VerdictEvaluated))
		case "quorum":
			r.Set(fd, protoreflect.ValueOfBool(v.Quorum))
		case "anchor":
			r.Set(fd, protoreflect.ValueOfMessage(AnchorRefToPB(*v.Anchor).ProtoReflect()))
		case "finality":
			r.Set(fd, protoreflect.ValueOfBool(v.Finality))
		case "last_mergeable":
			r.Set(fd, protoreflect.ValueOfBool(v.LastMergeable))
		default:
			t.Fatalf("%s has no case: BlockVerification and this test must carry it", fd.FullName())
		}
	}
	return m
}

// TestBlockVerificationFromPBReadsEveryField: every field of
// pb.BlockVerification, pb.StatementCandidates and pb.VerifierEvidence is set
// through protoreflect and read back, and of the header exactly the fields of
// BlockHeaderView are read (plan S3-C2 contract §21.2). The four top-level
// bools and the transition flag take three patterns, so a swap of any two of
// them, or a flag read from the track, is caught.
func TestBlockVerificationFromPBReadsEveryField(t *testing.T) {
	if n := reflect.TypeOf(BlockHeaderView{}).NumField(); n != len(blockHeaderViewFields) {
		t.Fatalf("BlockHeaderView has %d fields, the test names %d header fields", n, len(blockHeaderViewFields))
	}
	for _, flags := range [][5]bool{{true, false, false, true, true}, {false, true, false, true, false}, {false, false, true, false, true}} {
		want := blockVerificationFixture()
		want.VerdictEvaluated, want.Quorum, want.Finality, want.LastMergeable = flags[0], flags[1], flags[2], flags[3]
		want.Header.IsTableSetTransition = flags[4]

		got, err := BlockVerificationFromPB(blockVerificationThroughReflection(t, want))

		if err != nil {
			t.Fatalf("BlockVerificationFromPB: %v", err)
		}
		if !reflect.DeepEqual(got, want) {
			t.Fatalf("flags %v: read back\n got %+v\nwant %+v", flags, got, want)
		}
	}
	back := BlockVerificationToPB(blockVerificationFixture()).GetHeader().ProtoReflect()
	fields := back.Descriptor().Fields()
	for i := 0; i < fields.Len(); i++ {
		if fd := fields.Get(i); !blockHeaderViewFields[fd.Name()] && back.Has(fd) {
			t.Errorf("BlockVerificationToPB set header field %s, which BlockHeaderView does not carry", fd.FullName())
		}
	}
}

// TestBlockVerificationRoundTrip: ToPB then FromPB, also through
// proto.Marshal, gives the value back, with every optional message absent as
// well as present.
func TestBlockVerificationRoundTrip(t *testing.T) {
	sparse := blockVerificationFixture()
	sparse.Header.IsTableSetTransition, sparse.Header.TrackIndexerID = false, nil
	sparse.Anchor = nil
	sparse.ScanParts, sparse.SourceNodes = nil, nil
	sparse.Evidence = []VerifierEvidence{{ReplicaID: "verifier-1"}, {ReplicaID: "verifier-2", Evaluated: true}}
	sparse.Statements = []StatementCandidates{{StatementSeq: 300, StatementID: "stmt-300", Status: "pending"}}
	for name, want := range map[string]BlockVerification{"every field": blockVerificationFixture(), "absent messages and lists": sparse, "header only": {Header: BlockHeaderView{L3BlockSeq: 1}}} {
		t.Run(name, func(t *testing.T) {
			raw, err := proto.Marshal(BlockVerificationToPB(want))
			if err != nil {
				t.Fatal(err)
			}
			var m pb.BlockVerification
			if err := proto.Unmarshal(raw, &m); err != nil {
				t.Fatal(err)
			}
			for via, msg := range map[string]*pb.BlockVerification{"direct": BlockVerificationToPB(want), "marshalled": &m} {
				got, err := BlockVerificationFromPB(msg)
				if err != nil {
					t.Fatalf("%s: %v", via, err)
				}
				if !reflect.DeepEqual(got, want) {
					t.Fatalf("%s round trip\n got %+v\nwant %+v", via, got, want)
				}
			}
		})
	}
}

// TestBlockVerificationWithoutAHeaderIsRefused: an answer that names no block
// is refused, never read as block 0.
func TestBlockVerificationWithoutAHeaderIsRefused(t *testing.T) {
	for name, m := range map[string]*pb.BlockVerification{"nil": nil, "no header": {ChainHash: "0xchain", Quorum: true}} {
		if _, err := BlockVerificationFromPB(m); err == nil || err.Error() != "wire: block verification has no header" {
			t.Fatalf("%s: BlockVerificationFromPB = %v, want the no-header refusal", name, err)
		}
	}
}

// TestBlockVerificationTrackKeepsIndexerZeroDistinctFromAbsent: a block of
// indexer 0's track has a present track with indexer_id 0, a block sealed
// before the tracks activation has none, and both survive the wire.
func TestBlockVerificationTrackKeepsIndexerZeroDistinctFromAbsent(t *testing.T) {
	zero := uint64(0)
	for name, track := range map[string]*uint64{"absent": nil, "indexer 0": &zero} {
		t.Run(name, func(t *testing.T) {
			raw, err := proto.Marshal(BlockVerificationToPB(BlockVerification{Header: BlockHeaderView{L3BlockSeq: 5, TrackIndexerID: track}}))
			if err != nil {
				t.Fatal(err)
			}
			var m pb.BlockVerification
			if err := proto.Unmarshal(raw, &m); err != nil {
				t.Fatal(err)
			}
			if (m.GetHeader().GetTrack() != nil) != (track != nil) {
				t.Fatalf("wire track present = %v, want %v", m.GetHeader().GetTrack() != nil, track != nil)
			}
			got, err := BlockVerificationFromPB(&m)
			if err != nil {
				t.Fatal(err)
			}
			switch {
			case track == nil && got.Header.TrackIndexerID != nil:
				t.Fatalf("absent track read as indexer %d", *got.Header.TrackIndexerID)
			case track != nil && (got.Header.TrackIndexerID == nil || *got.Header.TrackIndexerID != 0):
				t.Fatalf("indexer 0's track read as %v", got.Header.TrackIndexerID)
			case got.Header.IsTableSetTransition:
				t.Fatal("a block with a track and no table_set_transition read as a transition block")
			}
		})
	}
}
```

- [ ] **Step 5: Implement `wire.BlockVerification` and its converters**

Create `wire/block_verification.go`:

```go
package wire

import (
	"errors"

	pb "github.com/sentioxyz/arbiter-proto/gen/pb"

	"github.com/housegate/housegate/pkg/replay"

	"github.com/sentioxyz/arbiter-core"
)

// BlockHeaderView is the part of a sealed block's header that a block
// verification read is used for (plan S3-C2 contract §21.2): which block, which
// statements, which base manifest, whether it is a table-set transition and
// whose track it is. The other header fields (hashes, roots, the L2 anchor)
// stay with GetL3Block, which serves the whole header for auditing.
type BlockHeaderView struct {
	L3BlockSeq         uint64
	StatementSeqStart  uint64
	StatementCount     uint32
	PrevSafeSnapshotID string
	PrevStateRoot      string
	// IsTableSetTransition reports that header.table_set_transition is present.
	IsTableSetTransition bool
	// TrackIndexerID is header.track; nil on a block sealed before the tracks
	// activation. Indexer 0 is a value, distinct from absent.
	TrackIndexerID *uint64
}

// StatementCandidates mirrors pb.StatementCandidates: one statement of the
// block with the candidate parts and partition sums its source claimed.
type StatementCandidates struct {
	StatementSeq              uint64
	StatementID               string
	Status                    string
	SourceNode                string
	RCBound                   bool
	SourceClaimRoot           string
	CandidateParts            []arbiter.CandidatePart
	PartitionNewPartSums      []arbiter.PartitionLtHashSum
	UnpromotedPartRowLtHashes []string
}

// VerifierEvidence mirrors pb.VerifierEvidence: what one verifier of the
// block's verifier set recorded, and the FSM's checks of it. Evaluated is
// false for evidence recorded after the quorum latched (plan S3-A contract
// §4); its checks are then not part of the verdict.
type VerifierEvidence struct {
	ReplicaID            string
	Attestation          *replay.ReplayAttestation // nil when not recorded
	ByteSideScan         *arbiter.ByteSideScanMsg  // nil when not recorded
	Evaluated            bool
	Check1RootMatch      bool
	Check2PartitionMatch bool
	Check3ByteSideMatch  bool
	Pass                 bool
}

// BlockVerification is the canonical Go form of SafeState.GetBlockVerification
// (plan S3-A contract §1; plan S3-C2 contract §21.2). It is a read reply, not
// a signing form, so it carries no JSON tags.
type BlockVerification struct {
	Header           BlockHeaderView
	ChainHash        string
	ReplayJob        replay.ReplayJob
	Statements       []StatementCandidates
	ScanParts        []arbiter.PartRef
	SourceNodes      []string
	VerifierSet      []string
	Evidence         []VerifierEvidence
	VerdictEvaluated bool
	Quorum           bool
	Anchor           *arbiter.AnchorRef // nil when the block has no anchor
	Finality         bool
	LastMergeable    bool
}

// BlockVerificationFromPB converts a GetBlockVerification answer. A message
// without a header names no block and is refused; repeated fields decode empty
// to nil and absent messages to nil pointers.
func BlockVerificationFromPB(m *pb.BlockVerification) (BlockVerification, error) {
	h := m.GetHeader()
	if h == nil {
		return BlockVerification{}, errors.New("wire: block verification has no header")
	}
	out := BlockVerification{
		Header:           blockHeaderViewFromPB(h),
		ChainHash:        m.GetChainHash(),
		ReplayJob:        ReplayJobFromPB(m.GetReplayJob()),
		Statements:       mapSlice(m.GetStatements(), statementCandidatesFromPB),
		ScanParts:        PartRefsFromPB(m.GetScanParts()),
		SourceNodes:      mapSlice(m.GetSourceNodes(), func(s string) string { return s }),
		VerifierSet:      mapSlice(m.GetVerifierSet(), func(s string) string { return s }),
		Evidence:         mapSlice(m.GetEvidence(), verifierEvidenceFromPB),
		VerdictEvaluated: m.GetVerdictEvaluated(),
		Quorum:           m.GetQuorum(),
		Finality:         m.GetFinality(),
		LastMergeable:    m.GetLastMergeable(),
	}
	if a := m.GetAnchor(); a != nil {
		anchor := AnchorRefFromPB(a)
		out.Anchor = &anchor
	}
	return out, nil
}

// BlockVerificationToPB is BlockVerificationFromPB's inverse, for fake arbiter
// servers and tests. The header fields outside BlockHeaderView stay empty, and
// a transition block's table_set_transition is an empty, present message.
func BlockVerificationToPB(v BlockVerification) *pb.BlockVerification {
	h := &pb.L3BlockHeader{
		L3BlockSeq:         v.Header.L3BlockSeq,
		StatementSeqStart:  v.Header.StatementSeqStart,
		StatementCount:     v.Header.StatementCount,
		PrevSafeSnapshotId: v.Header.PrevSafeSnapshotID,
		PrevStateRoot:      v.Header.PrevStateRoot,
	}
	if v.Header.IsTableSetTransition {
		h.TableSetTransition = &pb.TableSetTransition{}
	}
	if v.Header.TrackIndexerID != nil {
		h.Track = &pb.L3BlockTrack{IndexerId: *v.Header.TrackIndexerID}
	}
	out := &pb.BlockVerification{
		Header:           h,
		ChainHash:        v.ChainHash,
		ReplayJob:        ReplayJobToPB(v.ReplayJob),
		Statements:       mapSlice(v.Statements, statementCandidatesToPB),
		ScanParts:        mapSlice(v.ScanParts, partRefToPB),
		SourceNodes:      mapSlice(v.SourceNodes, func(s string) string { return s }),
		VerifierSet:      mapSlice(v.VerifierSet, func(s string) string { return s }),
		Evidence:         mapSlice(v.Evidence, verifierEvidenceToPB),
		VerdictEvaluated: v.VerdictEvaluated,
		Quorum:           v.Quorum,
		Finality:         v.Finality,
		LastMergeable:    v.LastMergeable,
	}
	if v.Anchor != nil {
		out.Anchor = AnchorRefToPB(*v.Anchor)
	}
	return out
}

func blockHeaderViewFromPB(h *pb.L3BlockHeader) BlockHeaderView {
	v := BlockHeaderView{
		L3BlockSeq:           h.GetL3BlockSeq(),
		StatementSeqStart:    h.GetStatementSeqStart(),
		StatementCount:       h.GetStatementCount(),
		PrevSafeSnapshotID:   h.GetPrevSafeSnapshotId(),
		PrevStateRoot:        h.GetPrevStateRoot(),
		IsTableSetTransition: h.GetTableSetTransition() != nil,
	}
	if track := h.GetTrack(); track != nil {
		id := track.GetIndexerId()
		v.TrackIndexerID = &id
	}
	return v
}

func statementCandidatesFromPB(m *pb.StatementCandidates) StatementCandidates {
	return StatementCandidates{
		StatementSeq:              m.GetStatementSeq(),
		StatementID:               m.GetStatementId(),
		Status:                    m.GetStatus(),
		SourceNode:                m.GetSourceNode(),
		RCBound:                   m.GetRcBound(),
		SourceClaimRoot:           m.GetSourceClaimRoot(),
		CandidateParts:            mapSlice(m.GetCandidateParts(), candidatePartFromPB),
		PartitionNewPartSums:      mapSlice(m.GetPartitionNewPartSums(), partitionSumFromPB),
		UnpromotedPartRowLtHashes: mapSlice(m.GetUnpromotedPartRowLthashes(), func(s string) string { return s }),
	}
}

func statementCandidatesToPB(v StatementCandidates) *pb.StatementCandidates {
	return &pb.StatementCandidates{
		StatementSeq:              v.StatementSeq,
		StatementId:               v.StatementID,
		Status:                    v.Status,
		SourceNode:                v.SourceNode,
		RcBound:                   v.RCBound,
		SourceClaimRoot:           v.SourceClaimRoot,
		CandidateParts:            mapSlice(v.CandidateParts, CandidatePartToPB),
		PartitionNewPartSums:      mapSlice(v.PartitionNewPartSums, PartitionLtHashSumToPB),
		UnpromotedPartRowLthashes: mapSlice(v.UnpromotedPartRowLtHashes, func(s string) string { return s }),
	}
}

func verifierEvidenceFromPB(m *pb.VerifierEvidence) VerifierEvidence {
	out := VerifierEvidence{
		ReplicaID:            m.GetReplicaId(),
		Evaluated:            m.GetEvaluated(),
		Check1RootMatch:      m.GetCheck1RootMatch(),
		Check2PartitionMatch: m.GetCheck2PartitionMatch(),
		Check3ByteSideMatch:  m.GetCheck3ByteSideMatch(),
		Pass:                 m.GetPass(),
	}
	if a := m.GetAttestation(); a != nil {
		att := AttestationFromPB(a)
		out.Attestation = &att
	}
	if s := m.GetByteSideScan(); s != nil {
		scan := ScanFromPB(s)
		out.ByteSideScan = &scan
	}
	return out
}

func verifierEvidenceToPB(v VerifierEvidence) *pb.VerifierEvidence {
	out := &pb.VerifierEvidence{
		ReplicaId:            v.ReplicaID,
		Evaluated:            v.Evaluated,
		Check1RootMatch:      v.Check1RootMatch,
		Check2PartitionMatch: v.Check2PartitionMatch,
		Check3ByteSideMatch:  v.Check3ByteSideMatch,
		Pass:                 v.Pass,
	}
	if v.Attestation != nil {
		out.Attestation = AttestationToPB(*v.Attestation)
	}
	if v.ByteSideScan != nil {
		out.ByteSideScan = ScanToPB(*v.ByteSideScan)
	}
	return out
}
```

- [ ] **Step 7: Implement `ManifestOwner`**

In `wire/table_registry_snapshot.go`, after `Owner` (`:178-186`, the closing `}` of `func (s TableRegistrySnapshot) Owner(inc TableIncarnation) uint64`), add:

```go
// ManifestOwner is the SI indexer a published manifest attributes tableKey to:
// the port of arbiter's fsm.manifestTableOwnerLocked (fsm/reads_manifest.go).
// Scanning the incarnations from the newest, the first of tableKey that is not
// Refused and ever entered a table set (a genesis one, or one whose add
// transition was sealed: AddBlockSeq non-zero) gives Owner(inc); ok is false
// when there is none. A Pending incarnation never added is skipped, so a key
// keeps the owner of the incarnation a manifest can hold. Callers pass a
// snapshot of an enabled registry (RegistryView.View true); arbiter's
// TestManifestTableOwnerMatchesWireManifestOwner proves both rules agree.
func (s TableRegistrySnapshot) ManifestOwner(tableKey string) (uint64, bool) {
	for i := len(s.Incarnations) - 1; i >= 0; i-- {
		inc := s.Incarnations[i]
		if inc.Key() != tableKey || inc.Status == TableStatusRefused {
			continue
		}
		if inc.Origin == TableOriginGenesis || inc.AddBlockSeq != 0 {
			return s.Owner(inc), true
		}
	}
	return 0, false
}
```

```go
package dataplane

import (
	"context"
	"errors"
	"reflect"
	"sync"
	"testing"
	"time"

	pb "github.com/sentioxyz/arbiter-proto/gen/pb"
	"google.golang.org/grpc"
	"google.golang.org/grpc/codes"
	"google.golang.org/grpc/status"

	"github.com/sentioxyz/arbiter-core"
	"github.com/sentioxyz/arbiter-core/wire"
)

// memberReadsSafeState serves the three reads a P2 member makes and records
// every method it is asked. A peer with hint answers NotLeader naming it, one
// with err refuses with it, and otherwise it answers from its maps with the
// arbiter's NotFound texts (server/safestate.go, plan S3-A contract §4).
type memberReadsSafeState struct {
	pb.UnimplementedSafeStateServer

	mu        sync.Mutex
	hint      string
	err       error
	watermark *pb.SafeWatermark
	manifests map[string]*pb.SafeSnapshotManifest
	blocks    map[uint64]*pb.BlockVerification
	calls     []string
}

func (s *memberReadsSafeState) refusal(method string) error {
	s.calls = append(s.calls, method)
	if s.hint != "" {
		st, err := status.New(codes.FailedPrecondition, "not leader").WithDetails(&pb.NotLeader{LeaderAddr: s.hint})
		if err != nil {
			return status.Error(codes.Internal, err.Error())
		}
		return st.Err()
	}
	return s.err
}

func (s *memberReadsSafeState) GetSafeWatermark(context.Context, *pb.GetSafeWatermarkRequest) (*pb.SafeWatermark, error) {
	s.mu.Lock()
	defer s.mu.Unlock()
	if err := s.refusal("GetSafeWatermark"); err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	return s.watermark, nil
}

func (s *memberReadsSafeState) GetManifest(_ context.Context, ref *pb.SnapshotRef) (*pb.SafeSnapshotManifest, error) {
	s.mu.Lock()
	defer s.mu.Unlock()
	if err := s.refusal("GetManifest"); err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	m, ok := s.manifests[ref.GetSnapshotId()]
	if !ok {
		return nil, status.Error(codes.NotFound, "unknown snapshot id")
	}
	return m, nil
}

func (s *memberReadsSafeState) GetBlockVerification(_ context.Context, ref *pb.L3BlockRef) (*pb.BlockVerification, error) {
	s.mu.Lock()
	defer s.mu.Unlock()
	if err := s.refusal("GetBlockVerification"); err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	b, ok := s.blocks[ref.GetL3BlockSeq()]
	if !ok {
		return nil, status.Error(codes.NotFound, "no sealed block at that seq")
	}
	return b, nil
}

func (s *memberReadsSafeState) methods() []string {
	s.mu.Lock()
	defer s.mu.Unlock()
	return append([]string(nil), s.calls...)
}

func startMemberReadsPeer(t *testing.T, s *memberReadsSafeState) string {
	t.Helper()
	srv := grpc.NewServer()
	pb.RegisterSafeStateServer(srv, s)
	return serveGRPCForDataplaneTest(t, srv)
}

func memberBlockFixture(seq uint64) wire.BlockVerification {
	owner := uint64(0)
	return wire.BlockVerification{
		Header:      wire.BlockHeaderView{L3BlockSeq: seq, StatementSeqStart: 10, StatementCount: 1, PrevSafeSnapshotID: "0xprev", PrevStateRoot: "0xstate", TrackIndexerID: &owner},
		ChainHash:   "0xchain",
		VerifierSet: []string{"verifier-1", "verifier-2", "verifier-3"},
		Evidence:    []wire.VerifierEvidence{{ReplicaID: "verifier-1", Evaluated: true, Check1RootMatch: true, Pass: true}},
		Quorum:      true, VerdictEvaluated: true,
	}
}

// TestGetSafeWatermarkFollowsTheLeader: the read is leader-barriered, so a
// follower answers NotLeader and the client asks the leader it names, and the
// leader first the next time (plan S3-C2 contract §21.1).
func TestGetSafeWatermarkFollowsTheLeader(t *testing.T) {
	follower := &memberReadsSafeState{hint: "n2"}
	leader := &memberReadsSafeState{watermark: &pb.SafeWatermark{SnapshotId: "0xsnap", SafeBlockSeq: 7, ManifestRoot: "0xsnap"}}
	c := newTestClient(t, Peer{ID: "n1", GRPCAddr: startMemberReadsPeer(t, follower)}, Peer{ID: "n2", GRPCAddr: startMemberReadsPeer(t, leader)})
	ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 5*time.Second)
	defer cancel()

	got, err := c.GetSafeWatermark(ctx)

	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("GetSafeWatermark: %v", err)
	}
	if want := (arbiter.SafeWatermark{SnapshotID: "0xsnap", SafeBlockSeq: 7, ManifestRoot: "0xsnap"}); got != want {
		t.Fatalf("watermark = %+v, want %+v", got, want)
	}
	if _, err := c.GetSafeWatermark(ctx); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("second read: %v", err)
	}
	if f, l := follower.methods(), leader.methods(); len(f) != 1 || len(l) != 2 {
		t.Fatalf("calls: follower %v, leader %v; want the follower once and the leader twice", f, l)
	}
}

// TestGetManifestUnknownSnapshotIsErrManifestNotFound: a known id is
// answered, and the leader's NotFound is ErrManifestNotFound naming the id,
// returned at once (NotFound is not retried).
func TestGetManifestUnknownSnapshotIsErrManifestNotFound(t *testing.T) {
	manifest := sealedDataplaneManifest(t)
	peer := &memberReadsSafeState{manifests: map[string]*pb.SafeSnapshotManifest{manifest.SnapshotID: wire.ManifestToPB(manifest)}}
	c := newTestClient(t, Peer{ID: "n1", GRPCAddr: startMemberReadsPeer(t, peer)})
	ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 5*time.Second)
	defer cancel()

	got, err := c.GetManifest(ctx, manifest.SnapshotID)
	if err != nil || !reflect.DeepEqual(got, manifest) {
		t.Fatalf("GetManifest(known) = %+v, %v; want the manifest", got, err)
	}
	began := time.Now()
	_, err = c.GetManifest(ctx, "0xmissing")

	if !errors.Is(err, ErrManifestNotFound) || err.Error() != "dataplane: the arbiter has no manifest with that snapshot id: 0xmissing" {
		t.Fatalf("GetManifest(unknown) = %v, want ErrManifestNotFound naming 0xmissing", err)
	}
	if elapsed, calls := time.Since(began), len(peer.methods()); elapsed > 2*time.Second || calls != 2 {
		t.Fatalf("NotFound must not be retried: %d calls in %v", calls, elapsed)
	}
}

// TestGetManifestReturnsTheAnswerUnvalidated: the client converts and returns
// what the arbiter sent; accepting it is the member feed's job.
func TestGetManifestReturnsTheAnswerUnvalidated(t *testing.T) {
	tampered := sealedDataplaneManifest(t)
	tampered.ManifestRoot = "0xnot-the-root"

	c := newTestClient(t, Peer{ID: "n1", GRPCAddr: startMemberReadsPeer(t, peer)})
	ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 5*time.Second)
	defer cancel()

	got, err := c.GetManifest(ctx, tampered.SnapshotID)

	if err != nil || !reflect.DeepEqual(got, tampered) {
		t.Fatalf("GetManifest = %+v, %v; want the tampered manifest as sent", got, err)
	}
}

// TestGetManifestRefusesAnEmptyID: an empty id is refused before any call.
func TestGetManifestRefusesAnEmptyID(t *testing.T) {
	peer := &memberReadsSafeState{}
	c := newTestClient(t, Peer{ID: "n1", GRPCAddr: startMemberReadsPeer(t, peer)})

// TestGetBlockVerificationRefusesSeqZero: block seqs start at 1, so 0 is

func TestGetBlockVerificationRefusesSeqZero(t *testing.T) {
	peer := &memberReadsSafeState{}

// TestGetBlockVerificationRefusesAnAnswerForAnotherBlock: the requested block
// is answered as the canonical type; an answer whose header names another
// block, or no block, is refused.
func TestGetBlockVerificationRefusesAnAnswerForAnotherBlock(t *testing.T) {
	want := memberBlockFixture(42)
	peer := &memberReadsSafeState{blocks: map[uint64]*pb.BlockVerification{
		42: wire.BlockVerificationToPB(want),

	if err != nil || !reflect.DeepEqual(got, want) {
		t.Fatalf("GetBlockVerification(42) = %+v, %v; want %+v", got, err, want)
	}
	for seq, refusal := range map[uint64]string{
		43: "dataplane: GetBlockVerification(43) answered block 44",
		45: "dataplane: GetBlockVerification(45): wire: block verification has no header",
	} {
		if _, err := c.GetBlockVerification(ctx, seq); err == nil || err.Error() != refusal {
			t.Fatalf("GetBlockVerification(%d) = %v, want %q", seq, err, refusal)
		}
	}
}

// TestGetBlockVerificationUnimplementedIsErrStage3ReadsUnavailable: an
// arbiter v0.12.0 serves SafeState without the read; Unimplemented is
// ErrStage3ReadsUnavailable at once, never a retry.
func TestGetBlockVerificationUnimplementedIsErrStage3ReadsUnavailable(t *testing.T) {
	c := newTestClient(t, Peer{ID: "n1", GRPCAddr: startSafeStatePeer(t, &fakeSafeState{code: codes.OK, snapshot: "safe"})})
	ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 5*time.Second)
	defer cancel()
	began := time.Now()

	_, err := c.GetBlockVerification(ctx, 42)

	if !errors.Is(err, ErrStage3ReadsUnavailable) || errors.Is(err, ErrBlockNotSealed) {
		t.Fatalf("GetBlockVerification = %v, want ErrStage3ReadsUnavailable", err)
	}
	if elapsed := time.Since(began); elapsed > 2*time.Second {
		t.Fatalf("Unimplemented must not be retried: %v", elapsed)
	}
}
```

```go
package dataplane

import (
	"context"
	"errors"
	"fmt"

	pb "github.com/sentioxyz/arbiter-proto/gen/pb"
	"google.golang.org/grpc"
	"google.golang.org/grpc/codes"
	"google.golang.org/grpc/status"

	"github.com/housegate/housegate/pkg/replay"

	"github.com/sentioxyz/arbiter-core"
	"github.com/sentioxyz/arbiter-core/wire"
)

// ErrManifestNotFound is the leader's NotFound for GetManifest: no published
// manifest has that snapshot id.
var ErrManifestNotFound = errors.New("dataplane: the arbiter has no manifest with that snapshot id")

// ErrBlockNotSealed is the leader's NotFound for GetBlockVerification: no
// block with that seq is sealed yet.
var ErrBlockNotSealed = errors.New("dataplane: no sealed block at that seq")

// GetSafeWatermark reads the published safe-state tip from the leader, behind
// one leader read barrier (plan S3-C2 contract §21.1). A follower's NotLeader
// is followed; any other refusal is returned unchanged.
func (c *Client) GetSafeWatermark(ctx context.Context) (arbiter.SafeWatermark, error) {
	var out arbiter.SafeWatermark
	err := c.WithLeaderRetry(ctx, func(ctx context.Context, conn *grpc.ClientConn) error {
		m, err := pb.NewSafeStateClient(conn).GetSafeWatermark(ctx, &pb.GetSafeWatermarkRequest{})
		if err != nil {
			return err
		}
		out = arbiter.SafeWatermark{SnapshotID: m.GetSnapshotId(), SafeBlockSeq: m.GetSafeBlockSeq(), ManifestRoot: m.GetManifestRoot()}
		return nil
	})
	if err != nil {
		return arbiter.SafeWatermark{}, err
	}
	return out, nil
}

// GetManifest reads one published manifest by snapshot id from the leader. It
// returns the manifest as the arbiter sent it, unvalidated: the member's feed
// (member/manifestfeed.Verify) decides whether to accept it. NotFound becomes
// an error wrapping ErrManifestNotFound that names the id.
func (c *Client) GetManifest(ctx context.Context, snapshotID string) (replay.SafeSnapshotManifest, error) {
	if snapshotID == "" {
		return replay.SafeSnapshotManifest{}, errors.New("dataplane: GetManifest needs a snapshot id")
	}
	var out replay.SafeSnapshotManifest
	err := c.WithLeaderRetry(ctx, func(ctx context.Context, conn *grpc.ClientConn) error {
		m, err := pb.NewSafeStateClient(conn).GetManifest(ctx, &pb.SnapshotRef{SnapshotId: snapshotID})
		if err != nil {
			return err
		}
		out = wire.ManifestFromPB(m)
		return nil
	})
	switch {
	case status.Code(err) == codes.NotFound:
		return replay.SafeSnapshotManifest{}, fmt.Errorf("%w: %s", ErrManifestNotFound, snapshotID)
	case err != nil:
		return replay.SafeSnapshotManifest{}, err
	}
	return out, nil
}

// GetBlockVerification reads one sealed block's verification state from the
// leader: its header, replay job, candidates, verifier set, evidence and
// verdict (plan S3-A contract §1, §4). NotFound becomes ErrBlockNotSealed, an
// arbiter without the read answers ErrStage3ReadsUnavailable, and an answer
// for another block is refused, because SafeState reads are unauthenticated.
func (c *Client) GetBlockVerification(ctx context.Context, blockSeq uint64) (wire.BlockVerification, error) {
	if blockSeq == 0 {
		return wire.BlockVerification{}, errors.New("dataplane: GetBlockVerification needs a block seq")
	}
	var msg *pb.BlockVerification
	err := c.WithLeaderRetry(ctx, func(ctx context.Context, conn *grpc.ClientConn) error {
		m, err := pb.NewSafeStateClient(conn).GetBlockVerification(ctx, &pb.L3BlockRef{L3BlockSeq: blockSeq})
		if err != nil {
			return err
		}
		msg = m
		return nil
	})
	switch {
	case status.Code(err) == codes.NotFound:
		return wire.BlockVerification{}, fmt.Errorf("%w: %d", ErrBlockNotSealed, blockSeq)
	case err != nil:
		return wire.BlockVerification{}, stage3ReadError("GetBlockVerification", err)
	}
	v, err := wire.BlockVerificationFromPB(msg)
	if err != nil {
		return wire.BlockVerification{}, fmt.Errorf("dataplane: GetBlockVerification(%d): %w", blockSeq, err)
	}
	if v.Header.L3BlockSeq != blockSeq {
		return wire.BlockVerification{}, fmt.Errorf("dataplane: GetBlockVerification(%d) answered block %d", blockSeq, v.Header.L3BlockSeq)
	}
	return v, nil
}
```

```go
package manifestfeed

import (
	"context"
	"encoding/hex"
	"fmt"
	"sync"
	"testing"

	"github.com/housegate/housegate/pkg/lthash"
	"github.com/housegate/housegate/pkg/replay"
	"github.com/housegate/housegate/pkg/replay/payloadexec"

	"github.com/sentioxyz/arbiter-core"
	"github.com/sentioxyz/arbiter-core/dataplane"
)

// *dataplane.Client is the production Source (plan S3-C2 contract §21.4).
var _ Source = (*dataplane.Client)(nil)

// rowHash is the row LtHash of a part holding one row.
func rowHash(row string) string {
	return "0x" + hex.EncodeToString(lthash.ElementHash([]byte(row)).Bytes())
}

func frontier(owner, safeBlockSeq, appliedPromotionSeq uint64) replay.TrackFrontier {
	return replay.TrackFrontier{IndexerID: owner, SafeBlockSeq: safeBlockSeq, AppliedPromotionSeq: appliedPromotionSeq}
}

// sealManifest seals the manifest of block seq on parent: table db.t, whose
// partition all holds one one-row part per row with the partition root their
// sum (a consistent ledger), and the given track frontiers (nil: a pre-tracks
// manifest).
func sealManifest(t *testing.T, parent string, seq uint64, frontiers []replay.TrackFrontier, rows ...string) replay.SafeSnapshotManifest {
	t.Helper()
	parts := make([]replay.PartManifestEntry, 0, len(rows))
	hashes := make([]string, 0, len(rows))
	for i, row := range rows {
		h := rowHash(row)
		hashes = append(hashes, h)
		parts = append(parts, replay.PartManifestEntry{TableID: "db.t", PartitionID: "all", PartName: fmt.Sprintf("all_%d_%d_0", i+1, i+1),
			PartPhysHash: "0xphys-" + row, PartRowLtHash: h, RowCount: 1, Bytes: 100})
	}
	root, err := payloadexec.SumPartRowLtHashes(hashes)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("partition root: %v", err)
	}
	m, err := (replay.SafeSnapshotManifest{
		ParentSnapshotID:  parent,
		SafeBlockSeq:      seq,
		SchemaSnapshotID:  "schema-genesis",
		SchemaRoot:        "0xschema-root",
		ExecutorProfileID: "housegate-replay-mvp-v0",
		Tables: []replay.TableManifest{{TableID: "db.t", SchemaHash: "0xtable-schema",
			PartitionRoots: []replay.PartitionCommitment{{TableID: "db.t", PartitionID: "all", Root: root}}, ActiveParts: parts}},
		TrackFrontiers: frontiers,
	}).Seal()
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("seal manifest %d: %v", seq, err)
	}
	return m
}

// trackChain seals n track-aware manifests, each the child of the one before
// (the first on parent): manifest i has block seq first+i, owner 0's entry
// advances at every manifest, owner 1's at every second one, and owner 2's
// never.
func trackChain(t *testing.T, parent string, first uint64, n int) []replay.SafeSnapshotManifest {
	t.Helper()
	out := make([]replay.SafeSnapshotManifest, 0, n)
	for i := 0; i < n; i++ {
		seq := first + uint64(i)
		frontiers := []replay.TrackFrontier{frontier(0, seq, seq), frontier(1, 10+seq/2, seq/2), frontier(2, 10, 0)}
		m := sealManifest(t, parent, seq, frontiers, fmt.Sprintf("row-%d", seq))
		out = append(out, m)
		parent = m.SnapshotID
	}
	return out
}

func entriesOf(m replay.SafeSnapshotManifest) map[uint64]replay.TrackFrontier {
	out := make(map[uint64]replay.TrackFrontier, len(m.TrackFrontiers))
	for _, tf := range m.TrackFrontiers {
		out[tf.IndexerID] = tf
	}
	return out
}

// fakeSource is an arbiter that serves a watermark and manifests by id and
// records every manifest id it is asked for.
type fakeSource struct {
	mu        sync.Mutex
	watermark arbiter.SafeWatermark
	manifests map[string]replay.SafeSnapshotManifest
	fetched   []string
}

func newFakeSource(ms ...replay.SafeSnapshotManifest) *fakeSource {
	s := &fakeSource{manifests: make(map[string]replay.SafeSnapshotManifest)}
	s.add(ms...)
	return s
}

func (s *fakeSource) add(ms ...replay.SafeSnapshotManifest) {
	s.mu.Lock()
	defer s.mu.Unlock()
	for _, m := range ms {
		s.manifests[m.SnapshotID] = m
	}
}

// publish makes m the watermark, as the arbiter does once it applies m.
func (s *fakeSource) publish(m replay.SafeSnapshotManifest) {
	s.add(m)
	s.mu.Lock()
	defer s.mu.Unlock()
	s.watermark = arbiter.SafeWatermark{SnapshotID: m.SnapshotID, SafeBlockSeq: m.SafeBlockSeq, ManifestRoot: m.ManifestRoot}
}

func (s *fakeSource) GetSafeWatermark(context.Context) (arbiter.SafeWatermark, error) {
	s.mu.Lock()
	defer s.mu.Unlock()
	return s.watermark, nil
}

func (s *fakeSource) GetManifest(_ context.Context, id string) (replay.SafeSnapshotManifest, error) {
	s.mu.Lock()
	defer s.mu.Unlock()
	s.fetched = append(s.fetched, id)
	m, ok := s.manifests[id]
	if !ok {
		return replay.SafeSnapshotManifest{}, fmt.Errorf("%w: %s", dataplane.ErrManifestNotFound, id)
	}
	return m, nil
}

// takeFetched returns the ids fetched since the last call.
func (s *fakeSource) takeFetched() []string {
	s.mu.Lock()
	defer s.mu.Unlock()
	out := s.fetched
	s.fetched = nil
	return out
}

func idsOf(ms ...replay.SafeSnapshotManifest) []string {
	out := make([]string, 0, len(ms))
	for _, m := range ms {
		out = append(out, m.SnapshotID)
	}
	return out
}
```
