```go
package sources

import (
	"context"
	"fmt"
	"reflect"
	"strings"
	"sync"

	clickhouse "github.com/ClickHouse/clickhouse-go/v2"
	"github.com/ClickHouse/clickhouse-go/v2/lib/driver"
)

// statementLog records the statements a connection was given, in order.
type statementLog struct {
	mu         sync.Mutex
	statements []string
}

func (l *statementLog) record(kind, query string) {
	l.mu.Lock()
	defer l.mu.Unlock()
	l.statements = append(l.statements, kind+" "+query)
}

func (l *statementLog) all() []string {
	l.mu.Lock()
	defer l.mu.Unlock()
	return append([]string(nil), l.statements...)
}

// matching returns the recorded statements that start with prefix.
func (l *statementLog) matching(prefix string) []string {
	var out []string
	for _, s := range l.all() {
		if strings.HasPrefix(s, prefix) {
			out = append(out, s)
		}
	}
	return out
}

// fakeConn is a clickhouse.Conn whose Query answers from rows and whose Exec
// answers from exec; it records every statement as "query <sql>" or
// "exec <sql>". Any other method is unimplemented (the embedded nil Conn
// panics).
type fakeConn struct {
	clickhouse.Conn
	statementLog
	rows func(query string, args []any) ([][]any, error)
	exec func(query string) error
}

func (c *fakeConn) Query(_ context.Context, query string, args ...any) (driver.Rows, error) {
	c.record("query", query)
	if c.rows == nil {
		return &fakeRows{}, nil
	}
	data, err := c.rows(query, args)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	return &fakeRows{data: data}, nil
}

func (c *fakeConn) Exec(_ context.Context, query string, _ ...any) error {
	c.record("exec", query)
	if c.exec == nil {
		return nil
	}
	return c.exec(query)
}

// fakeRows serves data row by row; Scan assigns each value to the matching
// destination pointer.
type fakeRows struct {
	driver.Rows
	data [][]any
	next int
}

func (r *fakeRows) Next() bool {
	if r.next >= len(r.data) {
		return false
	}
	r.next++
	return true
}

func (r *fakeRows) Scan(dest ...any) error {
	row := r.data[r.next-1]
	if len(dest) != len(row) {
		return fmt.Errorf("fakeRows: scan into %d destinations, row has %d values", len(dest), len(row))
	}
	for i, d := range dest {
		target := reflect.ValueOf(d).Elem()
		value := reflect.ValueOf(row[i])
		if !value.Type().AssignableTo(target.Type()) {
			return fmt.Errorf("fakeRows: column %d is %T, destination is %T", i, row[i], d)
		}
		target.Set(value)
	}
	return nil
}

func (r *fakeRows) Err() error   { return nil }
func (r *fakeRows) Close() error { return nil }

// recordingConn records every Exec and Query of a real connection.
type recordingConn struct {
	clickhouse.Conn
	statementLog
}

func (c *recordingConn) Exec(ctx context.Context, query string, args ...any) error {
	c.record("exec", query)
	return c.Conn.Exec(ctx, query, args...)
}

func (c *recordingConn) Query(ctx context.Context, query string, args ...any) (driver.Rows, error) {
	c.record("query", query)
	return c.Conn.Query(ctx, query, args...)
}

func (c *recordingConn) QueryRow(ctx context.Context, query string, args ...any) driver.Row {
	c.record("query", query)
	return c.Conn.QueryRow(ctx, query, args...)
}
```

Create `member/sources/ch_test.go`:

```go
package sources

import (
	"context"
	"crypto/rand"
	"encoding/hex"
	"errors"
	"fmt"
	"net"
	"os"
	"strconv"
	"strings"
	"testing"

	clickhouse "github.com/ClickHouse/clickhouse-go/v2"

	"github.com/housegate/housegate/pkg/lthash"
	"github.com/housegate/housegate/pkg/replay/chexec"
	"github.com/housegate/housegate/pkg/replay/payloadexec"

	"github.com/sentioxyz/arbiter-core/dataplane/chtest"
	"github.com/sentioxyz/arbiter-core/dataplane/ddl"
)

// The ClickHouse-gated tests of this package use the environment of the
// member confinement suite (contract §23.3): CH_ADDR is the member's
// ClickHouse, CH_PEER_ADDR a second server (the owner, or a network
// verifier) as this test reaches it, and CH_PEER_ADDR_FROM_SERVER the same
// server as CH_ADDR's server reaches it; S3_ENDPOINT, S3_BUCKET,
// S3_ACCESS_KEY_ID and S3_SECRET name an S3 bucket that both servers reach
// with a key that may write it (the restore test makes a backup first). The
// test's admin user is chtest's (CH_USER, CH_PASSWORD); it must manage users
// and named collections. Every user, collection, database and table a test
// makes is its own and is dropped when it ends.
const (
	envIntegration        = "ARBITER_CH_INTEGRATION"
	envAddr               = "CH_ADDR"
	envPeerAddr           = "CH_PEER_ADDR"
	envPeerAddrFromServer = "CH_PEER_ADDR_FROM_SERVER"
	envS3Endpoint         = "S3_ENDPOINT"
	envS3Bucket           = "S3_BUCKET"
	envS3AccessKeyID      = "S3_ACCESS_KEY_ID"
	envS3Secret           = "S3_SECRET"
)

// memberServer opens the member's ClickHouse (CH_ADDR) as the admin user.
func memberServer(t *testing.T) (clickhouse.Conn, string) {
	t.Helper()
	if os.Getenv(envIntegration) != "1" {
		t.Skipf("set %s=1 and %s to run the ClickHouse-gated member source tests", envIntegration, envAddr)
	}
	addr := os.Getenv(envAddr)
	if addr == "" {
		addr = "127.0.0.1:9000"
	}
	return chtest.Open(t, addr), addr
}

// pair is the member's ClickHouse and a second server it reaches through
// remote().
type pair struct {
	Member     clickhouse.Conn
	MemberAddr string
	Peer       clickhouse.Conn
	PeerAddr   string
	PeerHost   string // as the member's server reaches the peer
	PeerPort   uint64
}

func requirePair(t *testing.T) pair {
	t.Helper()
	member, memberAddr := memberServer(t)
	peerAddr, fromServer := os.Getenv(envPeerAddr), os.Getenv(envPeerAddrFromServer)
	if peerAddr == "" || fromServer == "" {
		t.Skipf("set %s (the second ClickHouse as this test reaches it) and %s (the same server as %s's server reaches it) to run the two-server source tests", envPeerAddr, envPeerAddrFromServer, envAddr)
	}
	host, portText, err := net.SplitHostPort(fromServer)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("%s %q: %v", envPeerAddrFromServer, fromServer, err)
	}
	port, err := strconv.ParseUint(portText, 10, 16)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("%s %q port: %v", envPeerAddrFromServer, fromServer, err)
	}
	return pair{Member: member, MemberAddr: memberAddr, Peer: chtest.Open(t, peerAddr), PeerAddr: peerAddr, PeerHost: host, PeerPort: port}
}

func randomHex(t *testing.T, n int) string {
	t.Helper()
	b := make([]byte, n)
	if _, err := rand.Read(b); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	return hex.EncodeToString(b)
}

// suffix is unique per test run, so objects never collide on a shared server
// or with an earlier run.
func suffix(t *testing.T) string {
	t.Helper()
	return randomHex(t, 4)
}

func mustExec(t *testing.T, conn clickhouse.Conn, query string) {
	t.Helper()
	if err := conn.Exec(context.Background(), query); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("%s: %v", query, err)
	}
}

// cleanup runs query on a fresh admin connection to addr when the test ends.
func cleanup(t *testing.T, addr, query string) {
	t.Helper()
	t.Cleanup(func() {
		conn, err := clickhouse.Open(chtest.Options(addr))
		if err != nil {
			t.Logf("cleanup %s: %v", query, err)
			return
		}
		defer func() { _ = conn.Close() }()
		if err := conn.Exec(context.Background(), query); err != nil {
			t.Logf("cleanup %s: %v", query, err)
		}
	})
}

// testSchema is a partitioned SI table schema whose logical database is
// unique to the test.
func testSchema(database string) payloadexec.TableSchema {
	return payloadexec.TableSchema{
		TableID: database + ".t", PartitionBy: "p",
		Columns: []lthash.Column{{Name: "p", Type: "String"}, {Name: "v", Type: "UInt64"}},
	}
}

// sourceDatabase creates database db on conn; a database of the test's own
// (not the shared hg_safe or hg_unsafe) is dropped when the test ends.
func sourceDatabase(t *testing.T, conn clickhouse.Conn, addr, db string) {
	t.Helper()
	mustExec(t, conn, "CREATE DATABASE IF NOT EXISTS "+ident(db))
	if db != "hg_safe" && db != "hg_unsafe" {
		cleanup(t, addr, "DROP DATABASE IF EXISTS "+ident(db)+" SYNC")
	}
}

// createSourceTable creates, on conn, schema's protocol MergeTree table in
// database db (the owner's hg_safe structure; the source engine does not
// matter to a pull) and drops it when the test ends; it returns the physical
// table name.
func createSourceTable(t *testing.T, conn clickhouse.Conn, addr, db string, schema payloadexec.TableSchema) string {
	t.Helper()
	_, safe, _, err := ddl.Intents(ddl.Pinned{UnsafeDB: db + "_u", SafeDB: db, PromoteDB: db + "_p", NodeID: "sources-test"}, schema)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	sourceDatabase(t, conn, addr, db)
	cleanup(t, addr, "DROP TABLE IF EXISTS "+ident(db)+"."+ident(safe.Table)+" SYNC")
	mustExec(t, conn, safe.SQL())
	return safe.Table
}

// insertPart writes n rows with row ids first..first+n-1 into partition p of
// db.table as one part.
func insertPart(t *testing.T, conn clickhouse.Conn, db, table, p string, first, n uint64) {
	t.Helper()
	ctx := clickhouse.Context(context.Background(), clickhouse.WithSettings(NoSplitSettings(n)))
	query := fmt.Sprintf("INSERT INTO %s.%s (%s, `p`, `v`) SELECT toFixedString(leftPad(lower(hex(number)), 32, '0'), 32), %s, number FROM numbers(%d, %d)",
		ident(db), ident(table), ident(ddl.RowIDColumn), literal(p), first, n)
	if err := conn.Exec(ctx, query); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("%s: %v", query, err)
	}
}

type partRow struct {
	Name, PartitionID, Hash string
	Rows                    uint64
}

// partsOf lists the active parts of db.table, by name.
func partsOf(t *testing.T, conn clickhouse.Conn, db, table string) []partRow {
	t.Helper()
	rows, err := conn.Query(context.Background(),
		"SELECT name, partition_id, hash_of_all_files, rows FROM system.parts WHERE database = ? AND table = ? AND active ORDER BY name", db, table)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	defer rows.Close()
	var out []partRow
	for rows.Next() {
		var p partRow
		if err := rows.Scan(&p.Name, &p.PartitionID, &p.Hash, &p.Rows); err != nil {
			t.Fatal(err)
		}
		out = append(out, p)
	}
	if err := rows.Err(); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	return out
}

// scanOf is the row LtHash of every active part of db.table.
func scanOf(t *testing.T, conn clickhouse.Conn, db, table string, schema payloadexec.TableSchema) map[string]chexec.PartScanResult {
	t.Helper()
	scans, err := chexec.ScanAllParts(context.Background(), conn, db+"."+table, schema)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	out := make(map[string]chexec.PartScanResult, len(scans))
	for _, s := range scans {
		out[s.PartName] = s
	}
	return out
}

// createUser creates a password user (crypto/rand password) on conn with
// grants (each with one %s for the quoted user) and drops it when the test
// ends. settings is "" or a SETTINGS clause.
func createUser(t *testing.T, conn clickhouse.Conn, addr, name, settings string, grants ...string) string {
	t.Helper()
	password := randomHex(t, 16)
	cleanup(t, addr, "DROP USER IF EXISTS "+ident(name))
	mustExec(t, conn, fmt.Sprintf("CREATE USER %s IDENTIFIED WITH sha256_password BY %s %s", ident(name), literal(password), settings))
	for _, g := range grants {
		mustExec(t, conn, fmt.Sprintf(g, ident(name)))
	}
	return password
}

// createReader creates, on the peer, a reader with spec §8.6's reader grants
// on db: SELECT on the database and SHOW COLUMNS plus si_reader's seven
// columns on system.parts. remote() describes system.parts before it reads
// it, which needs SHOW COLUMNS (measured; plan S3-C2 Appendix B).
func createReader(t *testing.T, p pair, db string) (string, string) {
	t.Helper()
	user := "src_reader_" + suffix(t)
	password := createUser(t, p.Peer, p.PeerAddr, user, "",
		"GRANT SELECT ON "+ident(db)+".* TO %s",
		"GRANT SHOW COLUMNS ON system.parts TO %s",
		"GRANT SELECT(database, table, name, active, rows, partition_id, hash_of_all_files) ON system.parts TO %s")
	return user, password
}

// createCollection creates, on the member's ClickHouse, a named collection
// reaching host:port as user, every key NOT OVERRIDABLE (contract §23.2), and
// drops it when the test ends.
func createCollection(t *testing.T, p pair, name, host string, port uint64, user, password string) {
	t.Helper()
	cleanup(t, p.MemberAddr, "DROP NAMED COLLECTION IF EXISTS "+ident(name))
	mustExec(t, p.Member, fmt.Sprintf("CREATE NAMED COLLECTION %s AS host = %s NOT OVERRIDABLE, port = %d NOT OVERRIDABLE, user = %s NOT OVERRIDABLE, password = %s NOT OVERRIDABLE",
		ident(name), literal(host), port, literal(user), literal(password)))
}

// ownerCollection creates a reader for db on the peer and a collection to it
// on the member's ClickHouse, and returns the collection's name.
func ownerCollection(t *testing.T, p pair, prefix, db string) string {
	t.Helper()
	user, password := createReader(t, p, db)
	name := prefix + suffix(t)
	createCollection(t, p, name, p.PeerHost, p.PeerPort, user, password)
	return name
}

// memberUser creates, on the member's ClickHouse, a user holding the slice of
// contract §23.2's SI_MEMBER_GRANTS that the sources use, with stage as its
// hg_rstage, plus extra grants, and returns a connection as it.
func memberUser(t *testing.T, p pair, stage, settings string, collections []string, extra ...string) clickhouse.Conn {
	t.Helper()
	mustExec(t, p.Member, "CREATE DATABASE IF NOT EXISTS "+ident(stage))
	cleanup(t, p.MemberAddr, "DROP DATABASE IF EXISTS "+ident(stage)+" SYNC")
	grants := []string{
		"GRANT SELECT, INSERT, ALTER, CREATE TABLE, DROP TABLE ON " + ident(stage) + ".* TO %s",
		"GRANT TABLE ENGINE ON MergeTree TO %s",
		"GRANT SELECT ON system.parts TO %s",
		"GRANT READ ON REMOTE TO %s",
		"GRANT CREATE TEMPORARY TABLE ON *.* TO %s",
	}
	for _, c := range collections {
		grants = append(grants, "GRANT NAMED COLLECTION ON "+ident(c)+" TO %s")
	}
	user := "src_member_" + suffix(t)
	password := createUser(t, p.Member, p.MemberAddr, user, settings, append(grants, extra...)...)
	return chtest.OpenAs(t, p.MemberAddr, user, password)
}

// newScratch creates scratch table name in stage as conn's user, with
// ddl.ScratchIntent's structure.
func newScratch(t *testing.T, conn clickhouse.Conn, stage, name string, schema payloadexec.TableSchema) Scratch {
	t.Helper()
	intent, err := ddl.ScratchIntent(ddl.MemberPinned{
		MemberUnsafeDB: "hg_member_unsafe", ReplicaDB: "hg_replica", StageDB: stage, NodeID: "member-test",
	}, schema, name)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	mustExec(t, conn, intent.SQL())
	return Scratch{Database: stage, Table: name}
}

// tablesIn lists the tables of db.
func tablesIn(t *testing.T, conn clickhouse.Conn, db string) []string {
	t.Helper()
	rows, err := conn.Query(context.Background(), "SELECT name FROM system.tables WHERE database = ? ORDER BY name", db)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	defer rows.Close()
	var out []string
	for rows.Next() {
		var n string
		if err := rows.Scan(&n); err != nil {
			t.Fatal(err)
		}
		out = append(out, n)
	}
	return out
}

// clickHouseCode is the ClickHouse error code of err, or 0.
func clickHouseCode(err error) int32 {
	var exception *clickhouse.Exception
	if !errors.As(err, &exception) {
		return 0
	}
	return exception.Code
}

// queryLog reads the finished queries of user from system.query_log after a
// flush.
func queryLog(t *testing.T, conn clickhouse.Conn, user string) []string {
	t.Helper()
	mustExec(t, conn, "SYSTEM FLUSH LOGS")
	rows, err := conn.Query(context.Background(), "SELECT query FROM system.query_log WHERE user = ? AND type IN ('QueryFinish', 'ExceptionBeforeStart', 'ExceptionWhileProcessing') ORDER BY event_time_microseconds", user)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	defer rows.Close()
	var out []string
	for rows.Next() {
		var q string
		if err := rows.Scan(&q); err != nil {
			t.Fatal(err)
		}
		out = append(out, strings.TrimSpace(q))
	}
	return out
}
```

```go
func TestNeedsOfManifestAndCandidateParts(t *testing.T) {
	want := Need{

		PartRowLtHash: "0x01", RowCount: 3, Bytes: 400,

	}
	if got := NeedOfCandidatePart(arbiter.CandidatePart{

		PartRowLtHash: "0x01", RowCount: 3, Bytes: 400,
	}); got != want {

	}

		t.Fatalf("SourceNames = %v", got)
	}
	if got := Outcomes(); fmt.Sprint(got) != "[fetched missed refused unreachable]" {
		t.Fatalf("Outcomes = %v", got)

// TestOutcomeOfClickHouseErrors pins plan S3-C2 K35's mapping: a memory
// limit, too many simultaneous queries or a timeout is refused; a network
// error, a socket timeout, failed connection tries or a remote table whose
// structure cannot be fetched is unreachable; anything else is refused.
func TestOutcomeOfClickHouseErrors(t *testing.T) {
	for _, tc := range []struct {
		err  error
		want Outcome
	}{
		{&clickhouse.Exception{Code: 241, Message: "Query memory limit exceeded"}, OutcomeRefused},
		{&clickhouse.Exception{Code: 202, Message: "Too many simultaneous queries"}, OutcomeRefused},
		{&clickhouse.Exception{Code: 159, Message: "Timeout exceeded"}, OutcomeRefused},
		{&clickhouse.Exception{Code: 210, Message: "Connection refused"}, OutcomeUnreachable},
		{&clickhouse.Exception{Code: 209, Message: "Timeout exceeded while reading from socket"}, OutcomeUnreachable},
		{&clickhouse.Exception{Code: 279, Message: "All connection tries failed"}, OutcomeUnreachable},
		{&clickhouse.Exception{Code: 519, Message: "All attempts to get table structure failed"}, OutcomeUnreachable},
		{fmt.Errorf("pull: %w", &clickhouse.Exception{Code: 279}), OutcomeUnreachable},
		{&clickhouse.Exception{Code: 497, Message: "Not enough privileges"}, OutcomeRefused},
		{&clickhouse.Exception{Code: 60, Message: "Unknown table"}, OutcomeRefused},
		{errors.New("read tcp 127.0.0.1:9000: i/o timeout"), OutcomeRefused},
	} {
		if got := outcomeOf(tc.err); got != tc.want {
			t.Errorf("outcomeOf(%v) = %s, want %s", tc.err, got, tc.want)
		}
	}
}
```

```go
package sources

import (
	"context"
	"regexp"
	"slices"
	"strings"
	"testing"

	"github.com/housegate/housegate/pkg/lthash"
	"github.com/housegate/housegate/pkg/replay/payloadexec"

// readerPartsColumns are the system.parts columns si_reader may read
// (contract §20.2).
var readerPartsColumns = []string{"database", "table", "name", "active", "rows", "partition_id", "hash_of_all_files"}

func pullSchema() payloadexec.TableSchema {
	return payloadexec.TableSchema{
		TableID: "dex.swaps", PartitionBy: "p",
		Columns: []lthash.Column{{Name: "p", Type: "String"}, {Name: "v", Type: "UInt64"}},
	}
}

// TestOwnerPullFiltersOnPartOnly pins the owner pull's statements (housegate
// spec 2026-10-14 §8.6): the name is resolved on the owner by
// hash_of_all_files, the pull filters on _part only (never on the manifest's
// logical partition id, which is not ClickHouse's partition id), the
// collection is the only way to the owner (no host, user or password in
// SQL), only si_reader's system.parts columns are named, and a miss falls
// back to the parts of the needed partition (ClickHouse's partition_id,
// computed on the member's own server by a query that reads no table) and
// row count with the bound; the unsafe pulls never fall back.
func TestOwnerPullFiltersOnPartOnly(t *testing.T) {
	need := Need{
		TableKey: "dex.swaps", Table: "dex__swaps", PartitionID: "p_2026", PartName: "d589_1_1_0",
		PartPhysHash: "4adff322bb8fd41ea3d90f10b04424fb", PartRowLtHash: "0x01", RowCount: 3,
	}
	scratch := Scratch{Database: "hg_rstage", Table: "member-a_0011aabb_7"}
	resolve := "SELECT name, rows FROM remote(`si_owner_0`, database = 'system', table = 'parts') WHERE database = 'hg_safe' AND table = 'dex__swaps' AND active AND hash_of_all_files = '4adff322bb8fd41ea3d90f10b04424fb'"
	// partitionId('2026') is 3897267c32bd78b1a745b8b101ea06f3 on 25.8 and 26.3
	// (measured), the partition_id of every part whose partition value is 2026.
	partitionID := "SELECT partitionId('2026')"
	fallback := "SELECT name FROM remote(`si_owner_0`, database = 'system', table = 'parts') WHERE database = 'hg_safe' AND table = 'dex__swaps' AND active AND partition_id = '3897267c32bd78b1a745b8b101ea06f3' AND rows = 3 ORDER BY name LIMIT 8"
	pull := "INSERT INTO `hg_rstage`.`member-a_0011aabb_7` SELECT * FROM remote(`si_owner_0`, database = 'hg_safe', table = 'dex__swaps') WHERE _part = 'd589_4_4_0'"

	t.Run("resolved_by_hash", func(t *testing.T) {
		conn := &fakeConn{rows: func(query string, args []any) ([][]any, error) {
			switch query {
			case resolve:
				return [][]any{{"d589_9_9_0", uint64(3)}, {"d589_4_4_0", uint64(3)}}, nil
			case scratchPartsQuery:
				if !slices.Equal(args, []any{"hg_rstage", "member-a_0011aabb_7"}) {
					t.Errorf("scratch listing args %v", args)
				}
				return [][]any{{"d589_1_1_0"}}, nil
			}
			t.Fatalf("unexpected query %s", query)
			return nil, nil
		}}
		res := NewOwnerPull(conn, "si_owner_0", "").Fetch(context.Background(), need, pullSchema(), scratch)
		if res.Source != "owner_pull" || res.Outcome != OutcomeFetched || res.Err != nil || !slices.Equal(res.Parts, []string{"d589_1_1_0"}) {
			t.Fatalf("Fetch = %+v, want fetched [d589_1_1_0] from owner_pull", res)
		}
		want := []string{"query " + resolve, "exec " + pull, "query " + scratchPartsQuery}
		if got := conn.all(); !slices.Equal(got, want) {
			t.Fatalf("statements:\n%s\nwant:\n%s", strings.Join(got, "\n"), strings.Join(want, "\n"))
		}
	})
	t.Run("missed_then_bounded_fallback", func(t *testing.T) {
		conn := &fakeConn{rows: func(query string, _ []any) ([][]any, error) {
			if query == partitionID {
				return [][]any{{"3897267c32bd78b1a745b8b101ea06f3"}}, nil
			}
			return nil, nil
		}}
		res := NewOwnerPull(conn, "si_owner_0", "hg_safe").Fetch(context.Background(), need, pullSchema(), scratch)
		if res.Outcome != OutcomeMissed || res.Err != nil || len(res.Parts) != 0 {
			t.Fatalf("Fetch = %+v, want missed", res)
		}
		if got, want := conn.all(), []string{"query " + resolve, "query " + partitionID, "query " + fallback}; !slices.Equal(got, want) {
			t.Fatalf("statements %q, want %q", got, want)
		}
	})
	t.Run("unpartitioned_fallback_reads_partition_all", func(t *testing.T) {
		conn := &fakeConn{}
		flat := pullSchema()
		flat.PartitionBy = ""
		unpartitioned := need
		unpartitioned.PartitionID = "all"
		res := NewOwnerPull(conn, "si_owner_0", "").Fetch(context.Background(), unpartitioned, flat, scratch)
		want := []string{"query " + resolve, "query " + strings.Replace(fallback, "'3897267c32bd78b1a745b8b101ea06f3'", "'all'", 1)}
		if res.Outcome != OutcomeMissed || !slices.Equal(conn.all(), want) {
			t.Fatalf("Fetch = %+v after %q, want missed after %q", res, conn.all(), want)
		}
	})
	t.Run("unsafe_pulls_never_fall_back", func(t *testing.T) {
		for _, p := range []*RemotePull{NewOwnerUnsafePull(&fakeConn{}, "si_owner_0", "hg_unsafe_x"), NewPeerUnsafePull(&fakeConn{}, "si_peer_verifier_1")} {
			res := p.Fetch(context.Background(), need, pullSchema(), scratch)
			statements := p.Conn.(*fakeConn).all()
			if res.Outcome != OutcomeMissed || len(statements) != 1 || !strings.Contains(statements[0], "hash_of_all_files") {
				t.Fatalf("%s: Fetch = %+v after %q, want missed after the hash lookup alone", p.Name(), res, statements)
			}
		}
	})
	t.Run("statement_shape", func(t *testing.T) {
		if strings.Contains(pull, need.PartitionID) || strings.Contains(pull, "_partition") || strings.Contains(pull, "PARTITION") {
			t.Fatalf("the pull names a partition: %s", pull)
		}
		word := regexp.MustCompile(`[a-z_]+`)
		for _, q := range []string{resolve, fallback} {
			where := q[strings.Index(q, " WHERE "):]
			selected := strings.TrimPrefix(q[:strings.Index(q, " FROM ")], "SELECT ")
			// Keywords are upper case, so every lower-case word is a column.
			for _, w := range append(word.FindAllString(stripLiterals(where), -1), word.FindAllString(selected, -1)...) {
				if !slices.Contains(readerPartsColumns, w) {
					t.Fatalf("%s names system.parts column %q outside si_reader's grant", q, w)
				}
			}
		}
		for _, q := range []string{resolve, fallback, pull} {
			for _, forbidden := range []string{"user", "password", "host", "port"} {
				if strings.Contains(strings.ToLower(stripLiterals(q)), forbidden+" =") {
					t.Fatalf("%s overrides %s", q, forbidden)
				}
			}
		}
		if strings.Contains(partitionID, " FROM ") || strings.Contains(partitionID, "remote(") {
			t.Fatalf("the partition id query reads a table: %s", partitionID)
		}
	})
	t.Run("refuses_a_collection_that_is_not_one_identifier", func(t *testing.T) {
		conn := &fakeConn{}
		res := NewOwnerPull(conn, "si_owner_0, user = 'default'", "").Fetch(context.Background(), need, pullSchema(), scratch)
		if res.Outcome != OutcomeRefused || res.Err == nil || !strings.Contains(res.Err.Error(), "must be one ClickHouse identifier") || len(conn.all()) != 0 {
			t.Fatalf("Fetch = %+v after %q, want refused before any statement", res, conn.all())
		}
	})
}

// TestOwnerPullFallbackListsAfterItsCursor pins how the row-hash fallback
// makes progress across fetches of one need (Plan S3-C2 Appendix B, review
// fix 245-3): a window of MaxFallbackCandidates that kept nothing leaves its
// last name as the need's cursor, the next listing starts after it (name >
// '<last>'), a short window (the partition's end) or a kept part clears the
// cursor so the next listing starts from the first candidate again, and
// each need, keyed by table, partition id, row hash and row count, keeps its
// own cursor.
func TestOwnerPullFallbackListsAfterItsCursor(t *testing.T) {
	pull := NewOwnerPull(&fakeConn{}, "si_owner_0", "")
	need := Need{TableKey: "dex.swaps", Table: "dex__swaps", PartitionID: "p_2026", PartRowLtHash: "0x01", RowCount: 3}
	from := "SELECT name FROM remote(`si_owner_0`, database = 'system', table = 'parts') WHERE database = 'hg_safe' AND table = 'dex__swaps' AND active AND partition_id = 'abc' AND rows = 3"
	if got, want := pull.fallbackQuery(need, "abc", "", 2), from+" ORDER BY name LIMIT 2"; got != want {
		t.Fatalf("first listing = %s, want %s", got, want)
	}
	if got, want := pull.fallbackQuery(need, "abc", "abc_4_4_0", 2), from+" AND name > 'abc_4_4_0' ORDER BY name LIMIT 2"; got != want {
		t.Fatalf("listing after the cursor = %s, want %s", got, want)
	}
	for _, tc := range []struct {
		listed []string
		limit  int
		want   string
	}{
		{[]string{"abc_1_1_0", "abc_4_4_0"}, 2, "abc_4_4_0"},
		{[]string{"abc_7_7_0"}, 2, ""},
		{nil, 2, ""},
	} {
		if got := nextFallbackCursor(tc.listed, tc.limit); got != tc.want {
			t.Fatalf("nextFallbackCursor(%v, %d) = %q, want %q", tc.listed, tc.limit, got, tc.want)
		}
	}
	key, other := fallbackKey(need, "abc"), fallbackKey(Need{Table: "dex__swaps", PartRowLtHash: "0x02", RowCount: 3}, "abc")
	pull.setCursor(key, "abc_4_4_0")
	if got := pull.cursor(key); got != "abc_4_4_0" {
		t.Fatalf("cursor = %q after a full window, want abc_4_4_0", got)
	}
	if got := pull.cursor(other); got != "" {
		t.Fatalf("another need's cursor = %q, want none", got)
	}
	pull.setCursor(key, "")
	if got := pull.cursor(key); got != "" {
		t.Fatalf("cursor = %q after the listing ended, want none", got)
	}
}

// stripLiterals removes single-quoted literals from a statement.
func stripLiterals(q string) string {
	return regexp.MustCompile(`'(?:[^'\\]|\\.)*'`).ReplaceAllString(q, "''")
}
```

```go
// siMemberGrantRows are system.grants' rows for a user holding contract
// §23.2's SI_MEMBER_GRANTS with one collection, as ClickHouse 26.3 renders

// TestCheckRemoteGrantsNeedsReadAndNoWrite reads READ and WRITE ON REMOTE
// from system.grants rows as 25.8 and 26.3 render source grants: directly,
// through ON *, through the legacy REMOTE and SOURCES privileges, through
// ALL, and minus a partial revoke.
func TestCheckRemoteGrantsNeedsReadAndNoWrite(t *testing.T) {
	const (
		noRead = "sources: system.grants shows no READ ON REMOTE for this user"
		write  = "sources: system.grants shows WRITE ON REMOTE for this user"
	)
	without := func(rows []Grant, drop Grant) []Grant {
		var out []Grant
		for _, g := range rows {
			if g != drop {
				out = append(out, g)
			}
		}
		return out
	}
	for _, tc := range []struct {
		name   string
		grants []Grant
		want   string
	}{
		{"si_member", siMemberGrantRows, ""},
		{"si_member_without_read_on_remote", without(siMemberGrantRows, Grant{AccessType: "READ", AccessObject: "REMOTE"}), noRead},
		{"read_on_s3_is_not_read_on_remote", []Grant{{AccessType: "READ", AccessObject: "S3"}}, noRead},
		{"nothing", nil, noRead},
		{"write_on_remote", append([]Grant{{AccessType: "WRITE", AccessObject: "REMOTE"}}, siMemberGrantRows...), write},
		{"write_on_remote_alone", []Grant{{AccessType: "WRITE", AccessObject: "REMOTE"}}, write},
		{"legacy_remote_on_all", []Grant{{AccessType: "READ", AccessObject: "REMOTE"}, {AccessType: "WRITE", AccessObject: "REMOTE"}}, write},
		{"read_on_all_sources", []Grant{{AccessType: "READ"}}, ""},
		{"sources_on_all", []Grant{{AccessType: "READ"}, {AccessType: "WRITE"}}, write},
		{"all", []Grant{{AccessType: "ALL"}}, write},
		{"write_on_all_minus_remote", []Grant{{AccessType: "READ"}, {AccessType: "WRITE"}, {AccessType: "WRITE", AccessObject: "REMOTE", PartialRevoke: true}}, ""},
		{"read_on_all_minus_remote", []Grant{{AccessType: "READ"}, {AccessType: "READ", AccessObject: "REMOTE", PartialRevoke: true}}, noRead},
		{"write_on_s3_only", []Grant{{AccessType: "READ", AccessObject: "REMOTE"}, {AccessType: "WRITE", AccessObject: "S3"}}, ""},
	} {
		t.Run(tc.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			err := CheckRemoteGrants(tc.grants)
			switch {
			case tc.want == "" && err != nil:
				t.Fatalf("CheckRemoteGrants = %v, want nil", err)
			case tc.want != "" && (err == nil || err.Error() != tc.want):
				t.Fatalf("CheckRemoteGrants = %v, want %q", err, tc.want)
			}
		})
	}
}
```

```go
package sources

import (
	"bytes"
	"context"
	"errors"
	"fmt"
	"log/slog"
	"strings"
	"testing"

	clickhouse "github.com/ClickHouse/clickhouse-go/v2"

// TestRestoreConfigNeverPrintsItsKeys: neither the access key id nor the
// secret of the member's restore key appears in any rendering of the config
// or of the source (fmt verbs, slog text and JSON), nor in the error of a
// failed restore, also when the server's message echoes the statement that
// carried the key (S3-B K16: keys only through the environment, never
// printed or logged).
func TestRestoreConfigNeverPrintsItsKeys(t *testing.T) {
	const id, secret = "AKIDMEMBERRESTORE0001", "member-restore-secret-0001"
	cfg := RestoreConfig{Endpoint: "http://si-minio:9000", Bucket: "si-replica", AccessKeyID: id, Secret: secret}
	source := NewRestore(nil, cfg, 7)
	var rendered []string
	for _, verb := range []string{"%v", "%+v", "%#v", "%s"} {
		rendered = append(rendered,
			fmt.Sprintf(verb, cfg), fmt.Sprintf(verb, &cfg), fmt.Sprintf(verb, source),
			fmt.Sprintf(verb, []any{cfg}), fmt.Sprintf(verb, struct{ R RestoreConfig }{cfg}))
	}
	for _, handler := range []func(*bytes.Buffer) slog.Handler{
		func(b *bytes.Buffer) slog.Handler { return slog.NewTextHandler(b, nil) },
		func(b *bytes.Buffer) slog.Handler { return slog.NewJSONHandler(b, nil) },
	} {
		var b bytes.Buffer
		slog.New(handler(&b)).Info("restore", "config", cfg, "source", source)
		rendered = append(rendered, b.String())
	}
	// A failed restore: the endpoint has no scheme, so the bucket is refused
	// before any statement; the error names the bucket and never the keys.
	bad := NewRestore(nil, RestoreConfig{Endpoint: "si-minio:9000", Bucket: "si-replica", AccessKeyID: id, Secret: secret}, 7)
	res := bad.Fetch(context.Background(), Need{TableKey: "dex.swaps", Table: "dex__swaps", PartitionID: "p_2026", PartPhysHash: "4adff322bb8fd41ea3d90f10b04424fb", RowCount: 3},
		pullSchema(), Scratch{Database: "hg_rstage", Table: "member-a_0011aabb_8"})
	if res.Outcome != OutcomeRefused || res.Err == nil || !strings.Contains(res.Err.Error(), "si-minio:9000/si-replica") {
		t.Fatalf("Fetch with a bad endpoint = %+v, want refused naming the bucket", res)
	}
	rendered = append(rendered, res.Err.Error(), fmt.Sprintf("%+v", res))
	// A server message that echoes the statement (as a syntax error does):
	// the index read and then the RESTORE fail with the statement in their
	// text, and the error carries neither part of the key. The index row is
	// what s3() answers: _file is the object's base name.
	echo := func(query string) error {
		return &clickhouse.Exception{Code: 62, Name: "SYNTAX_ERROR", Message: "Syntax error: failed at position 1 (" + query + ")"}
	}
	index := `{"format":"si-backup-index-v1","owner_indexer_id":7,"name":"20261015T000000Z-full","kind":"full","chain_length":1,` +
		`"tables":[{"physical_table":"dex__swaps","incarnation_seq":0,"parts":[{"name":"p_1_1_0","partition_id":"p_2026","phys_hash":"4adff322bb8fd41ea3d90f10b04424fb","rows":3}]}]}`
	for _, conn := range []*fakeConn{
		{rows: func(query string, _ []any) ([][]any, error) { return nil, echo(query) }},
		{
			rows: func(string, []any) ([][]any, error) {
				return [][]any{{"20261015T000000Z-full.index.json", index}}, nil
			},
			exec: func(query string) error {
				if strings.HasPrefix(query, "RESTORE ") {
					return echo(query)
				}
				return nil
			},
		},
	} {
		echoed := NewRestore(conn, cfg, 7).Fetch(context.Background(), Need{TableKey: "dex.swaps", Table: "dex__swaps", PartitionID: "p_2026", PartPhysHash: "4adff322bb8fd41ea3d90f10b04424fb", RowCount: 3},
			pullSchema(), Scratch{Database: "hg_rstage", Table: "member-a_0011aabb_9"})
		if echoed.Outcome != OutcomeRefused || echoed.Err == nil || !strings.Contains(echoed.Err.Error(), "Syntax error") {
			t.Fatalf("Fetch with an echoing server = %+v, want refused with the server's message", echoed)
		}
		var exception *clickhouse.Exception
		if errors.As(echoed.Err, &exception) {
			t.Fatalf("the scrubbed error still unwraps to the server's message: %v", exception)
		}
		rendered = append(rendered, echoed.Err.Error(), fmt.Sprintf("%+v", echoed))
		if !strings.Contains(echoed.Err.Error(), "'[redacted]'") {
			t.Fatalf("the scrubbed error %q shows no [redacted] key", echoed.Err)
		}
	}
	for _, r := range rendered {
		if strings.Contains(r, id) || strings.Contains(r, secret) {
			t.Fatalf("a rendering leaks the restore key: %s", r)
		}
	}
	if !strings.Contains(rendered[0], "si-minio:9000") || !strings.Contains(rendered[0], "si-replica") {
		t.Fatalf("the config renders as %q, want the endpoint and the bucket", rendered[0])
	}
	if source.Name() != "restore" {
		t.Fatalf("Name = %q, want restore", source.Name())
	}
}
```

```go
package sources

import (
	"context"

	clickhouse "github.com/ClickHouse/clickhouse-go/v2"

	"github.com/housegate/housegate/pkg/replay/payloadexec"
)

// largeRows is above the default min_insert_block_size_rows (1,048,449), so
// an INSERT ... SELECT with default settings splits a part this large.
const largeRows = 1_200_000

// requireOnePart asserts that scratch holds exactly one part, of rows rows
// whose row LtHash under schema is rowHash ("" skips the scan), and that res
// names it.
func requireOnePart(t *testing.T, conn clickhouse.Conn, res Result, scratch Scratch, schema payloadexec.TableSchema, rowHash string, rows uint64) {
	t.Helper()
	parts := partsOf(t, conn, scratch.Database, scratch.Table)
	if len(parts) != 1 || parts[0].Rows != rows {
		t.Fatalf("scratch holds %+v, want one part of %d rows", parts, rows)
	}
	if !slices.Equal(res.Parts, []string{parts[0].Name}) {
		t.Fatalf("Result.Parts = %v, scratch holds %s", res.Parts, parts[0].Name)
	}
	if rowHash == "" {
		return
	}
	scan := scanOf(t, conn, scratch.Database, scratch.Table, schema)
	if got := scan[parts[0].Name].RowLtHash; got != rowHash {
		t.Fatalf("the scratch part's row LtHash is %s, want %s", got, rowHash)
	}
}

// TestOwnerPullResolvesTheCurrentNameByHashOfAllFiles: the owner's REPLACE

func TestOwnerPullResolvesTheCurrentNameByHashOfAllFiles(t *testing.T) {

			manifest = part
		}

	// ATTACH PARTITION FROM, and REPLACE brings it back under new names.
	shadow := table + "_shadow"
	mustExec(t, p.Peer, "CREATE TABLE "+ident(db)+"."+ident(shadow)+" AS "+ident(db)+"."+ident(table))
	mustExec(t, p.Peer, "ALTER TABLE "+ident(db)+"."+ident(shadow)+" ATTACH PARTITION 'a' FROM "+ident(db)+"."+ident(table))
	mustExec(t, p.Peer, "ALTER TABLE "+ident(db)+"."+ident(table)+" REPLACE PARTITION 'a' FROM "+ident(db)+"."+ident(shadow))

			renamed = part
		}
	}

}

// TestOwnerPullFallsBackToTheRowHashWhenTheOwnerRebuiltItsParts: no active
// part has the manifest's hash_of_all_files (the owner rebuilt its parts), so
// the pull lists the parts of the needed partition and row count, pulls each
// into its own fresh <scratch>_c<k>, keeps the one whose scan is the needed
// row hash and drops every candidate table; the decoy of another partition,
// whose part sorts before the needed one, is never pulled; a bound below that
// candidate's position misses, and the next fetch of the same need continues
// after the last candidate it pulled.
func TestOwnerPullFallsBackToTheRowHashWhenTheOwnerRebuiltItsParts(t *testing.T) {
	p := requirePair(t)
	sfx := suffix(t)
	db, schema := "src_"+sfx, testSchema("dex_"+sfx)
	table := createSourceTable(t, p.Peer, p.PeerAddr, db, schema)
	insertPart(t, p.Peer, db, table, "a", 200, 3) // a decoy of the same row count, an earlier name
	insertPart(t, p.Peer, db, table, "a", 0, 3)   // the needed rows
	// A decoy of the row count in partition c, whose partition_id sorts before
	// a's (partitionId('c') = 0b8b7d0f…, partitionId('a') = 51fbadfb…,
	// measured), so a listing not scoped to the partition would pull it first.
	insertPart(t, p.Peer, db, table, "c", 300, 3)
	scans := scanOf(t, p.Peer, db, table, schema)
	parts := partsOf(t, p.Peer, db, table)
	needed := parts[0]
	for _, part := range parts {
		if strings.HasSuffix(part.Name, "_2_2_0") {
			needed = part
		}
	}
	// The candidates are the needed partition's parts of the row count, in
	// name order; the decoy of partition c is none of them.
	var candidates []partRow
	var decoy partRow
	for _, part := range parts {
		if part.PartitionID == needed.PartitionID {
			candidates = append(candidates, part)
		} else {
			decoy = part
		}
	}
	position := slices.IndexFunc(candidates, func(r partRow) bool { return r.Name == needed.Name })
	if position < 1 || decoy.Name == "" || decoy.Name > needed.Name {
		t.Fatalf("the needed part %s is first among its partition's %+v, or partition c holds no part that sorts before it (%+v); both decoys must sort before it", needed.Name, candidates, parts)
	}
	need := Need{
		TableKey: schema.TableID, Table: table, PartitionID: "p_a", PartName: needed.Name,
		PartPhysHash: strings.Repeat("0", 32), PartRowLtHash: scans[needed.Name].RowLtHash, RowCount: 3,
	}
	collection := ownerCollection(t, p, "si_owner_", db)
	stage := "hg_rstage_" + sfx
	member := memberUser(t, p, stage, "", []string{collection})

	t.Run("keeps_the_candidate_with_the_row_hash", func(t *testing.T) {
		scratch := newScratch(t, member, stage, "member-test_"+sfx+"_1", schema)
		rec := &recordingConn{Conn: member}
		res := NewOwnerPull(rec, collection, db).Fetch(context.Background(), need, schema, scratch)
		if res.Outcome != OutcomeFetched || res.Err != nil {
			t.Fatalf("Fetch = %+v, want fetched", res)
		}
		requireOnePart(t, member, res, scratch, schema, need.PartRowLtHash, 3)
		pulls := rec.matching("exec INSERT INTO")
		if len(pulls) != position+1 {
			t.Fatalf("%d candidate pulls %q, want %d (every candidate up to the needed one)", len(pulls), pulls, position+1)
		}
		for k, pull := range pulls {
			if want := fmt.Sprintf("exec INSERT INTO %s.%s ", ident(stage), ident(fmt.Sprintf("%s_c%d", scratch.Table, k+1))); !strings.HasPrefix(pull, want) {
				t.Fatalf("candidate pull %d is %s, want its own scratch (%s...)", k+1, pull, want)
			}
			if strings.Contains(pull, decoy.Name) {
				t.Fatalf("candidate pull %d reads %s of another partition: %s", k+1, decoy.Name, pull)
			}
		}
		if got := tablesIn(t, p.Member, stage); !slices.Equal(got, []string{scratch.Table}) {
			t.Fatalf("%s holds %v after the fetch, want only the scratch", stage, got)
		}
	})
	t.Run("a_bound_below_the_candidate_misses_and_the_next_fetch_continues", func(t *testing.T) {
		scratch := newScratch(t, member, stage, "member-test_"+sfx+"_2", schema)
		rec := &recordingConn{Conn: member}
		pull := NewOwnerPull(rec, collection, db)
		pull.MaxFallbackCandidates = position
		res := pull.Fetch(context.Background(), need, schema, scratch)
		if res.Outcome != OutcomeMissed || res.Err != nil {
			t.Fatalf("Fetch with %d candidates = %+v, want missed", position, res)
		}
		if parts := partsOf(t, member, stage, scratch.Table); len(parts) != 0 {
			t.Fatalf("a missed fetch wrote %+v", parts)
		}
		before := len(rec.matching("exec INSERT INTO"))
		next := newScratch(t, member, stage, "member-test_"+sfx+"_3", schema)
		res = pull.Fetch(context.Background(), need, schema, next)
		if res.Outcome != OutcomeFetched || res.Err != nil {
			t.Fatalf("the next Fetch of the same need = %+v, want fetched after the cursor", res)
		}
		requireOnePart(t, member, res, next, schema, need.PartRowLtHash, 3)
		if got := len(rec.matching("exec INSERT INTO")) - before; got != 1 {
			t.Fatalf("the next Fetch pulled %d candidates, want 1: it lists after the last candidate the first one pulled", got)
		}
	})
}

// TestOwnerPullFallbackScopesTheNeededPartition: nine other partitions each
// hold one part of the needed row count whose name sorts before the needed
// one, so a listing bounded before it is scoped would never reach the needed
// part (housegate spec 2026-10-14 §8.6: candidates of the same partition and
// row count; Plan S3-C2 review fix 245-3). The member's server computes
// ClickHouse's partition_id of every partition as the owner's server assigns
// it, and the fallback lists the needed partition alone and pulls its part
// first.
func TestOwnerPullFallbackScopesTheNeededPartition(t *testing.T) {
	p := requirePair(t)
	sfx := suffix(t)
	db, schema := "src_"+sfx, testSchema("dex_"+sfx)
	table := createSourceTable(t, p.Peer, p.PeerAddr, db, schema)
	values := []string{"p0", "p1", "p2", "p3", "p4", "p5", "p6", "p7", "p8", "p9"}
	ids := map[string]string{}
	for k, v := range values {
		insertPart(t, p.Peer, db, table, v, uint64(100*k), 3)
		var id string
		if err := p.Member.QueryRow(context.Background(), partitionIDQuery(literal(v))).Scan(&id); err != nil {
			t.Fatal(err)
		}
		ids[v] = id
	}
	parts := partsOf(t, p.Peer, db, table)
	for _, v := range values {
		if !slices.ContainsFunc(parts, func(r partRow) bool { return r.PartitionID == ids[v] }) {
			t.Fatalf("partitionId(%q) is %s on the member's server, and no part of the owner has it: %+v", v, ids[v], parts)
		}
	}
	// The needed partition is the one whose id sorts last, so the part of
	// every other partition sorts before its part.
	needed := slices.MaxFunc(values, func(a, b string) int { return strings.Compare(ids[a], ids[b]) })
	position := slices.IndexFunc(parts, func(r partRow) bool { return r.PartitionID == ids[needed] })
	if position < DefaultMaxFallbackCandidates {
		t.Fatalf("the needed partition's part sorts at %d of %+v, want at least %d", position, parts, DefaultMaxFallbackCandidates)
	}
	target := parts[position]
	scans := scanOf(t, p.Peer, db, table, schema)
	need := Need{
		TableKey: schema.TableID, Table: table, PartitionID: "p_" + needed, PartName: target.Name,
		PartPhysHash: strings.Repeat("0", 32), PartRowLtHash: scans[target.Name].RowLtHash, RowCount: 3,
	}
	collection := ownerCollection(t, p, "si_owner_", db)
	stage := "hg_rstage_" + sfx
	member := memberUser(t, p, stage, "", []string{collection})
	scratch := newScratch(t, member, stage, "member-test_"+sfx+"_1", schema)
	rec := &recordingConn{Conn: member}
	res := NewOwnerPull(rec, collection, db).Fetch(context.Background(), need, schema, scratch)
	if res.Outcome != OutcomeFetched || res.Err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("Fetch = %+v, want fetched from the needed partition", res)
	}
	requireOnePart(t, member, res, scratch, schema, need.PartRowLtHash, 3)
	if pulls := rec.matching("exec INSERT INTO"); len(pulls) != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("%d candidate pulls %q, want 1: the listing holds the needed partition only", len(pulls), pulls)
	}
	t.Logf("needed partition %s (partition_id %s) sorts at %d of %d parts of 3 rows", needed, ids[needed], position, len(parts))
}

// TestOwnerPullUsesTheNoSplitSettings: the pull runs under NoSplitSettings of
// the resolved part's row count (system.query_log records the query's
// settings).
func TestOwnerPullUsesTheNoSplitSettings(t *testing.T) {
	want := clickhouse.Settings{"min_insert_block_size_rows": uint64(3), "min_insert_block_size_bytes": 0, "max_threads": 1, "max_insert_threads": 1}
	if got := NoSplitSettings(3); fmt.Sprint(got) != fmt.Sprint(want) {
		t.Fatalf("NoSplitSettings(3) = %v, want %v", got, want)
	}
	if got := NoSplitSettings(0)["min_insert_block_size_rows"]; got != uint64(1) {
		t.Fatalf("NoSplitSettings(0) min_insert_block_size_rows = %v, want 1", got)
	}
	p := requirePair(t)
	sfx := suffix(t)
	db, schema := "src_"+sfx, testSchema("dex_"+sfx)
	table := createSourceTable(t, p.Peer, p.PeerAddr, db, schema)
	insertPart(t, p.Peer, db, table, "a", 0, 3)
	part := partsOf(t, p.Peer, db, table)[0]
	collection := ownerCollection(t, p, "si_owner_", db)
	stage := "hg_rstage_" + sfx
	member := memberUser(t, p, stage, "", []string{collection})
	scratch := newScratch(t, member, stage, "member-test_"+sfx+"_1", schema)
	need := Need{TableKey: schema.TableID, Table: table, PartitionID: "p_a", PartName: part.Name, PartPhysHash: part.Hash, RowCount: 3}
	if res := NewOwnerPull(member, collection, db).Fetch(context.Background(), need, schema, scratch); res.Outcome != OutcomeFetched {
		t.Fatalf("Fetch = %+v, want fetched", res)
	}
	mustExec(t, p.Member, "SYSTEM FLUSH LOGS")
	var rows, bytes, threads, insertThreads string
	if err := p.Member.QueryRow(context.Background(), `
		SELECT Settings['min_insert_block_size_rows'], Settings['min_insert_block_size_bytes'], Settings['max_threads'], Settings['max_insert_threads']
		FROM system.query_log
		WHERE type = 'QueryFinish' AND startsWith(query, ?)
		ORDER BY event_time_microseconds DESC LIMIT 1`, "INSERT INTO "+scratch.qualified()+" ").Scan(&rows, &bytes, &threads, &insertThreads); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("the pull's query_log row: %v", err)
	}
	if rows != "3" || bytes != "0" || threads != "1" || insertThreads != "1" {
		t.Fatalf("the pull ran with min_insert_block_size_rows=%q min_insert_block_size_bytes=%q max_threads=%q max_insert_threads=%q, want 3 0 1 1", rows, bytes, threads, insertThreads)
	}
}

// TestOwnerPullOfALargePartYieldsOnePart: a part above the default insert
// block size arrives as one part with the same rows (mechanics M6 for the

	need := Need{TableKey: schema.TableID, Table: table, PartitionID: "p_a", PartName: parts[0].Name, PartPhysHash: parts[0].Hash, RowCount: largeRows}
	res := NewOwnerPull(member, collection, db).Fetch(context.Background(), need, schema, scratch)

	checksum := func(conn clickhouse.Conn, db, table string) string {
		var n, sum uint64

	}
	if got, want := checksum(member, stage, scratch.Table), checksum(p.Peer, db, table); got != want {
		t.Fatalf("the pulled part's rows %s differ from the source's %s", got, want)
	}
}

// TestOwnerPullMemoryLimitIsRefusedNotRetried: the member profile's
// max_memory_usage bounds the largest pullable part (K35); a no-split pull
// above it is refused (MEMORY_LIMIT_EXCEEDED, 241), issued once, and leaves
// the scratch empty.
func TestOwnerPullMemoryLimitIsRefusedNotRetried(t *testing.T) {
	p := requirePair(t)
	sfx := suffix(t)
	db, schema := "src_"+sfx, testSchema("dex_"+sfx)
	table := createSourceTable(t, p.Peer, p.PeerAddr, db, schema)
	insertPart(t, p.Peer, db, table, "a", 0, largeRows)
	part := partsOf(t, p.Peer, db, table)[0]
	collection := ownerCollection(t, p, "si_owner_", db)
	stage := "hg_rstage_" + sfx
	member := memberUser(t, p, stage, "SETTINGS max_memory_usage = 10000000", []string{collection})
	scratch := newScratch(t, member, stage, "member-test_"+sfx+"_1", schema)
	rec := &recordingConn{Conn: member}
	need := Need{TableKey: schema.TableID, Table: table, PartitionID: "p_a", PartName: part.Name, PartPhysHash: part.Hash, PartRowLtHash: "0x00", RowCount: largeRows}
	res := NewOwnerPull(rec, collection, db).Fetch(context.Background(), need, schema, scratch)
	if res.Outcome != OutcomeRefused || clickHouseCode(res.Err) != 241 {
		t.Fatalf("Fetch = %+v, want refused with MEMORY_LIMIT_EXCEEDED (241)", res)
	}

		t.Fatalf("a refused pull wrote %+v", parts)
	}

}

// TestUnsafePullOfACleanedPartIsMissed: the owner's cleanup dropped the
// candidate part from hg_unsafe; the unsafe pull misses it after one lookup,
// pulls nothing (no fallback over the other part of the same row count) and
// leaves the scratch empty.
func TestUnsafePullOfACleanedPartIsMissed(t *testing.T) {
	p := requirePair(t)
	sfx := suffix(t)
	db, schema := "unsafe_"+sfx, testSchema("dex_"+sfx)
	table := createSourceTable(t, p.Peer, p.PeerAddr, db, schema)
	insertPart(t, p.Peer, db, table, "a", 0, 3)
	insertPart(t, p.Peer, db, table, "a", 100, 3)
	parts := partsOf(t, p.Peer, db, table)
	scans := scanOf(t, p.Peer, db, table, schema)
	cleaned := parts[0]
	mustExec(t, p.Peer, "ALTER TABLE "+ident(db)+"."+ident(table)+" DROP PART "+literal(cleaned.Name))
	collection := ownerCollection(t, p, "si_owner_", db)
	stage := "hg_rstage_" + sfx
	member := memberUser(t, p, stage, "", []string{collection})
	scratch := newScratch(t, member, stage, "member-test_"+sfx+"_1", schema)
	rec := &recordingConn{Conn: member}
	need := Need{TableKey: schema.TableID, Table: table, PartitionID: "p_a", PartName: cleaned.Name, PartPhysHash: cleaned.Hash, PartRowLtHash: scans[cleaned.Name].RowLtHash, RowCount: 3}
	res := NewOwnerUnsafePull(rec, collection, db).Fetch(context.Background(), need, schema, scratch)
	if res.Outcome != OutcomeMissed || res.Err != nil || res.Source != SourceOwnerUnsafePull {
		t.Fatalf("Fetch = %+v, want missed from owner_unsafe_pull", res)
	}
	if got := rec.all(); len(got) != 1 || !strings.Contains(got[0], "hash_of_all_files") {
		t.Fatalf("statements %q, want the hash lookup alone", got)
	}
	if got := tablesIn(t, p.Member, stage); !slices.Equal(got, []string{scratch.Table}) || len(partsOf(t, p.Member, stage, scratch.Table)) != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("%s holds %v (scratch parts %+v), want the empty scratch alone", stage, got, partsOf(t, p.Member, stage, scratch.Table))
	}
}

// TestPullFromAnUnreachableOwnerIsUnreachable: a collection whose server
// refuses connections makes every pull unreachable (remote() answers 519
// around 279 and 210), with nothing written.
func TestPullFromAnUnreachableOwnerIsUnreachable(t *testing.T) {
	p := requirePair(t)
	sfx := suffix(t)
	schema := testSchema("dex_" + sfx)
	collection := "si_owner_" + sfx
	createCollection(t, p, collection, p.PeerHost, 1, "si_reader", randomHex(t, 16))
	stage := "hg_rstage_" + sfx
	member := memberUser(t, p, stage, "", []string{collection})
	for i, source := range []*RemotePull{NewOwnerPull(member, collection, "hg_safe"), NewPeerUnsafePull(member, collection)} {
		scratch := newScratch(t, member, stage, fmt.Sprintf("member-test_%s_%d", sfx, i+1), schema)
		need := Need{TableKey: schema.TableID, Table: "dex_" + sfx + "__t", PartitionID: "p_a", PartName: "x_1_1_0", PartPhysHash: strings.Repeat("a", 32), PartRowLtHash: "0x00", RowCount: 3}
		res := source.Fetch(context.Background(), need, schema, scratch)
		code := clickHouseCode(res.Err)
		if res.Outcome != OutcomeUnreachable || (code != 519 && code != 279 && code != 210 && code != 209) {
			t.Fatalf("%s: Fetch = %+v (code %d), want unreachable", source.Name(), res, code)
		}
		if parts := partsOf(t, p.Member, stage, scratch.Table); len(parts) != 0 {
			t.Fatalf("%s: an unreachable pull wrote %+v", source.Name(), parts)
		}
		t.Logf("%s unreachable: code %d", source.Name(), code)
	}
}

// TestPeerUnsafePullReadsTheNamedPoolCollection: the peer unsafe pull reads a
// network verifier's hg_unsafe through its pool collection
// (si_peer_verifier_<n>, contract §23.2).
func TestPeerUnsafePullReadsTheNamedPoolCollection(t *testing.T) {
	p := requirePair(t)
	sfx := suffix(t)
	schema := testSchema("pool_" + sfx)
	table := createSourceTable(t, p.Peer, p.PeerAddr, "hg_unsafe", schema)
	insertPart(t, p.Peer, "hg_unsafe", table, "a", 0, 3)
	part := partsOf(t, p.Peer, "hg_unsafe", table)[0]
	scans := scanOf(t, p.Peer, "hg_unsafe", table, schema)
	user, password := createReader(t, p, "hg_unsafe")
	n, err := strconv.ParseUint(sfx, 16, 64)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	collection := fmt.Sprintf("si_peer_verifier_%d", n)
	createCollection(t, p, collection, p.PeerHost, p.PeerPort, user, password)
	stage := "hg_rstage_" + sfx
	member := memberUser(t, p, stage, "", []string{collection})
	scratch := newScratch(t, member, stage, "member-test_"+sfx+"_1", schema)
	source := NewPeerUnsafePull(member, collection)
	if source.Name() != SourcePeerUnsafePull || source.Database != "hg_unsafe" {
		t.Fatalf("NewPeerUnsafePull = %+v, want peer_unsafe_pull on hg_unsafe", source)
	}
	need := Need{TableKey: schema.TableID, Table: table, PartitionID: "p_a", PartName: part.Name, PartPhysHash: part.Hash, PartRowLtHash: scans[part.Name].RowLtHash, RowCount: 3}
	res := source.Fetch(context.Background(), need, schema, scratch)
	if res.Outcome != OutcomeFetched || res.Err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("Fetch = %+v, want fetched", res)
	}
	requireOnePart(t, member, res, scratch, schema, need.PartRowLtHash, 3)
}
```

```go
package sources

import (

// TestCheckRemoteIsReadOnlyRefusesWriteOnRemote: a READ ON REMOTE user's
// probe is refused locally for WRITE ON REMOTE, before any connection (the
// collection's server is down), so the check passes; a user with WRITE ON
// REMOTE, or the legacy REMOTE, is writable. One server suffices.
func TestCheckRemoteIsReadOnlyRefusesWriteOnRemote(t *testing.T) {
	admin, addr := memberServer(t)
	sfx := suffix(t)
	collection := "si_owner_" + sfx
	cleanup(t, addr, "DROP NAMED COLLECTION IF EXISTS "+ident(collection))
	mustExec(t, admin, "CREATE NAMED COLLECTION "+ident(collection)+" AS host = '127.0.0.1' NOT OVERRIDABLE, port = 1 NOT OVERRIDABLE, user = 'si_reader' NOT OVERRIDABLE, password = "+literal(randomHex(t, 16))+" NOT OVERRIDABLE")
	user := func(name string, grants ...string) clickhouse.Conn {
		password := createUser(t, admin, addr, name+sfx, "", append([]string{
			"GRANT NAMED COLLECTION ON " + ident(collection) + " TO %s",
			"GRANT CREATE TEMPORARY TABLE ON *.* TO %s",
		}, grants...)...)
		return chtest.OpenAs(t, addr, name+sfx, password)
	}
	if err := CheckRemoteIsReadOnly(context.Background(), user("src_read_", "GRANT READ ON REMOTE TO %s"), collection); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("CheckRemoteIsReadOnly as a READ ON REMOTE user: %v", err)
	}
	for _, tc := range []struct{ name, grant string }{
		{"src_write_", "GRANT READ, WRITE ON REMOTE TO %s"},
		{"src_legacy_", "GRANT REMOTE ON *.* TO %s"},
	} {
		err := CheckRemoteIsReadOnly(context.Background(), user(tc.name, tc.grant), collection)
		if !errors.Is(err, ErrRemoteWritable) || !strings.HasPrefix(err.Error(), "sources: INSERT INTO FUNCTION remote("+collection+") was not refused with ACCESS_DENIED (got ") || !strings.HasSuffix(err.Error(), "): WRITE ON REMOTE must be absent") {
			t.Fatalf("CheckRemoteIsReadOnly with %q = %v, want ErrRemoteWritable", tc.grant, err)
		}
		t.Logf("%s: %v", tc.grant, err)
	}
	if err := CheckRemoteIsReadOnly(context.Background(), admin, collection+", user = 'default'"); err == nil || errors.Is(err, ErrRemoteWritable) {
		t.Fatalf("CheckRemoteIsReadOnly of a collection that is not one identifier = %v, want a refusal before any statement", err)
	}
}

// TestCheckEngineFenceRefusesAServerWithoutTheFence: on a ClickHouse without
// access_control_improvements.table_engines_require_grant a user granted only
// TABLE ENGINE ON MergeTree creates ENGINE = Log, so CheckEngineFence
// reports ErrEngineFenceOff and drops its probe; on a fenced server it
// passes. Each server in CH_ADDR and CH_PEER_ADDR is classified first by a
// control user without any engine grant; at least one of them must lack the
// fence (the peer of the confinement suite and both CI servers do).
func TestCheckEngineFenceRefusesAServerWithoutTheFence(t *testing.T) {
	_, memberAddr := memberServer(t)
	addrs := []string{memberAddr}
	if peer := os.Getenv(envPeerAddr); peer != "" {
		addrs = append(addrs, peer)
	}
	unfenced := 0
	for _, addr := range addrs {
		admin := chtest.Open(t, addr)
		sfx := suffix(t)
		db := "fence_" + sfx
		mustExec(t, admin, "CREATE DATABASE IF NOT EXISTS "+ident(db))
		cleanup(t, addr, "DROP DATABASE IF EXISTS "+ident(db)+" SYNC")
		controlPassword := createUser(t, admin, addr, "src_control_"+sfx, "", "GRANT CREATE TABLE, DROP TABLE ON "+ident(db)+".* TO %s")
		err := chtest.OpenAs(t, addr, "src_control_"+sfx, controlPassword).Exec(context.Background(), "CREATE TABLE "+ident(db)+".`control` (x UInt8) ENGINE = MergeTree ORDER BY x")
		fenced := refusedFor(err, "TABLE ENGINE ON MergeTree")
		if err != nil && !fenced {
			t.Fatalf("%s: the control CREATE TABLE failed without the engine refusal: %v", addr, err)
		}
		proberPassword := createUser(t, admin, addr, "src_prober_"+sfx, "",
			"GRANT CREATE TABLE, DROP TABLE ON "+ident(db)+".* TO %s", "GRANT TABLE ENGINE ON MergeTree TO %s")
		probeTable := "member-test_engine_probe"
		err = CheckEngineFence(context.Background(), chtest.OpenAs(t, addr, "src_prober_"+sfx, proberPassword), db, probeTable)
		switch {
		case fenced && err != nil:
			t.Fatalf("%s is fenced, CheckEngineFence = %v, want nil", addr, err)
		case !fenced && (!errors.Is(err, ErrEngineFenceOff) || err.Error() != "sources: ClickHouse accepted ENGINE = Log for this user: access_control_improvements.table_engines_require_grant is off or the user holds every engine"):
			t.Fatalf("%s is not fenced, CheckEngineFence = %v, want ErrEngineFenceOff", addr, err)
		}
		if slices.Contains(tablesIn(t, admin, db), probeTable) {
			t.Fatalf("%s: the probe table %s.%s is left behind", addr, db, probeTable)
		}
		if !fenced {
			unfenced++
		}
		t.Logf("%s: fenced %v, CheckEngineFence = %v", addr, fenced, err)
	}
	if unfenced == 0 {
		t.Fatalf("every server of %v enforces the engine fence; set %s to a server without it", addrs, envPeerAddr)
	}
}

// TestReadOwnGrantsNeverRunsShowGrants: ReadOwnGrants reads its own rows of
// system.grants with one SELECT (never SHOW GRANTS); a user without SELECT on
// system.grants gets ErrGrantsUnreadable (the stock server configuration
// requires that grant); a user with it sees READ ON REMOTE as (READ, REMOTE)
// and, once granted, WRITE ON REMOTE, which CheckRemoteGrants refuses.
func TestReadOwnGrantsNeverRunsShowGrants(t *testing.T) {
	fake := &fakeConn{rows: func(query string, _ []any) ([][]any, error) {
		return [][]any{
			{"READ", (*string)(nil), (*string)(nil), "REMOTE", uint8(0)},
			{"SELECT", ptr("system"), ptr("parts"), "", uint8(0)},
		}, nil
	}}
	grants, err := ReadOwnGrants(context.Background(), fake)
	if err != nil || !slices.Equal(grants, []Grant{{AccessType: "READ", AccessObject: "REMOTE"}, {AccessType: "SELECT", Database: "system", Table: "parts"}}) {
		t.Fatalf("ReadOwnGrants = %+v, %v", grants, err)
	}
	if got := fake.all(); !slices.Equal(got, []string{"query " + readOwnGrantsQuery}) {
		t.Fatalf("statements %q, want the one system.grants SELECT", got)
	}
	denied := &fakeConn{rows: func(string, []any) ([][]any, error) {
		return nil, &clickhouse.Exception{Code: 497, Message: "si_member: Not enough privileges. To execute this query, it's necessary to have the grant SELECT ON system.grants"}
	}}
	if _, err := ReadOwnGrants(context.Background(), denied); !errors.Is(err, ErrGrantsUnreadable) {
		t.Fatalf("ReadOwnGrants refused with 497 = %v, want ErrGrantsUnreadable", err)
	}

	admin, addr := memberServer(t)
	sfx := suffix(t)
	plain, reader := "src_plain_"+sfx, "src_grants_"+sfx
	plainConn := chtest.OpenAs(t, addr, plain, createUser(t, admin, addr, plain, "", "GRANT READ ON REMOTE TO %s"))
	readerConn := chtest.OpenAs(t, addr, reader, createUser(t, admin, addr, reader, "", "GRANT READ ON REMOTE TO %s", "GRANT SELECT ON system.grants TO %s"))
	if _, err := ReadOwnGrants(context.Background(), plainConn); !errors.Is(err, ErrGrantsUnreadable) {
		t.Fatalf("ReadOwnGrants without SELECT on system.grants = %v, want ErrGrantsUnreadable", err)
	}
	grants, err = ReadOwnGrants(context.Background(), readerConn)
	if err != nil || !slices.Contains(grants, Grant{AccessType: "READ", AccessObject: "REMOTE"}) {
		t.Fatalf("ReadOwnGrants = %+v, %v; want a (READ, REMOTE) row", grants, err)
	}
	if err := CheckRemoteGrants(grants); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("CheckRemoteGrants of a READ ON REMOTE user: %v", err)
	}
	mustExec(t, admin, "GRANT WRITE ON REMOTE TO "+ident(reader))
	grants, err = ReadOwnGrants(context.Background(), readerConn)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if err := CheckRemoteGrants(grants); err == nil || err.Error() != "sources: system.grants shows WRITE ON REMOTE for this user" {
		t.Fatalf("CheckRemoteGrants after GRANT WRITE ON REMOTE = %v (rows %+v)", err, grants)
	}
	for _, user := range []string{plain, reader} {
		queries := queryLog(t, admin, user)
		if !slices.Contains(queries, readOwnGrantsQuery) {
			t.Fatalf("%s ran %q, want the system.grants SELECT", user, queries)
		}
		for _, q := range queries {
			if strings.HasPrefix(strings.ToUpper(q), "SHOW GRANTS") {
				t.Fatalf("%s ran %q", user, q)
			}
		}
	}
}
```

```go
package sources

import (

// s3Env is the bucket of the restore test (contract §23.3's names).
type s3Env struct {
	Endpoint, Bucket, AccessKeyID, Secret string
}

func requireS3(t *testing.T) s3Env {
	t.Helper()
	env := s3Env{Endpoint: os.Getenv(envS3Endpoint), Bucket: os.Getenv(envS3Bucket), AccessKeyID: os.Getenv(envS3AccessKeyID), Secret: os.Getenv(envS3Secret)}
	if env.Endpoint == "" {
		t.Skipf("set %s, %s, %s and %s (a bucket both servers reach, with a key that may write it) to run the restore test", envS3Endpoint, envS3Bucket, envS3AccessKeyID, envS3Secret)
	}
	if env.Bucket == "" || env.AccessKeyID == "" || env.Secret == "" {
		t.Fatalf("%s is set, so %s, %s and %s are required", envS3Endpoint, envS3Bucket, envS3AccessKeyID, envS3Secret)
	}
	return env
}

// TestRestoreSourceKeepsOnlyTheNeededPart: the owner's backup (Plan S3-C1's
// BACKUP DATABASE hg_safe TO S3, with its index object) holds a partition of
// two parts and another partition; restoring the need copies exactly the
// needed part into the scratch (with its row hash, under the scratch's own
// structure), drops <scratch>_r, and leaves every other part out; a need the
// index does not list is missed; an endpoint that refuses connections is a
// refused fetch at the index read's deadline, with no part of the key in its
// error and nothing in the scratch.
func TestRestoreSourceKeepsOnlyTheNeededPart(t *testing.T) {
	p := requirePair(t)
	s3 := requireS3(t)
	sfx := suffix(t)
	schema := testSchema("rst_" + sfx)
	table := createSourceTable(t, p.Peer, p.PeerAddr, "hg_safe", schema)
	insertPart(t, p.Peer, "hg_safe", table, "a", 0, 3)
	insertPart(t, p.Peer, "hg_safe", table, "a", 100, 2)
	insertPart(t, p.Peer, "hg_safe", table, "b", 200, 4)
	parts := partsOf(t, p.Peer, "hg_safe", table)
	scans := scanOf(t, p.Peer, "hg_safe", table, schema)
	n, err := rand.Int(rand.Reader, big.NewInt(1_000_000_000))
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	owner := 1_000_000_000 + n.Uint64() // a fresh owner-<id>/ prefix per run
	bucket, err := objstore.ParseBucket(strings.TrimRight(s3.Endpoint, "/") + "/" + s3.Bucket)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	creds := objstore.Credentials{AccessKeyID: s3.AccessKeyID, SecretAccessKey: s3.Secret}
	started := time.Now().UTC()
	name := objstore.BackupName(started, objstore.BackupFull)
	mustExec(t, p.Peer, objstore.BackupSQL(bucket, owner, name, "", creds))
	index := objstore.BackupIndex{
		Format: objstore.BackupIndexFormat, NetworkID: "sources-test", OwnerIndexerID: owner, Name: name, Kind: objstore.BackupFull,
		ChainLength: 1, StartedAt: started.Format(time.RFC3339), FinishedAt: time.Now().UTC().Format(time.RFC3339),
		SnapshotID: "0x" + strings.Repeat("ab", 32), Entry: replay.TrackFrontier{IndexerID: owner, SafeBlockSeq: 1, AppliedPromotionSeq: 1},
		Tables: []objstore.BackupIndexTable{{PhysicalTable: table, TableID: schema.TableID}},
	}
	byRows := map[uint64]partRow{}
	for _, part := range parts {
		partition := "p_a"
		if part.Rows == 4 {
			partition = "p_b"
		}
		byRows[part.Rows] = part
		index.Tables[0].Parts = append(index.Tables[0].Parts, objstore.BackupIndexPart{Name: part.Name, PartitionID: partition, PhysHash: part.Hash, Rows: part.Rows})
	}
	body, err := json.Marshal(index)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	mustExec(t, p.Peer, "INSERT INTO FUNCTION s3("+literal(bucket.IndexURL(owner, name))+", "+literal(s3.AccessKeyID)+", "+literal(s3.Secret)+", 'RawBLOB') SELECT "+literal(string(body)))

	stage := "hg_rstage_" + sfx
	member := memberUser(t, p, stage, "", nil, "GRANT READ ON S3 TO %s")
	cfg := RestoreConfig{Endpoint: s3.Endpoint, Bucket: s3.Bucket, AccessKeyID: s3.AccessKeyID, Secret: s3.Secret}
	source := NewRestore(member, cfg, owner)
	needed := byRows[3]
	need := Need{TableKey: schema.TableID, Table: table, PartitionID: "p_a", PartName: needed.Name, PartPhysHash: needed.Hash, PartRowLtHash: scans[needed.Name].RowLtHash, RowCount: 3}

	scratch := newScratch(t, member, stage, "member-test_"+sfx+"_1", schema)
	res := source.Fetch(context.Background(), need, schema, scratch)
	if res.Outcome != OutcomeFetched || res.Err != nil || res.Source != SourceRestore {
		t.Fatalf("Fetch = %+v, want fetched from restore", res)
	}
	requireOnePart(t, member, res, scratch, schema, need.PartRowLtHash, 3)
	if got := tablesIn(t, p.Member, stage); !slices.Equal(got, []string{scratch.Table}) {
		t.Fatalf("%s holds %v after the restore, want only the scratch (no %s_r)", stage, got, scratch.Table)
	}

	unlisted := need
	unlisted.PartPhysHash = strings.Repeat("0", 32)
	scratch2 := newScratch(t, member, stage, "member-test_"+sfx+"_2", schema)
	if res := source.Fetch(context.Background(), unlisted, schema, scratch2); res.Outcome != OutcomeMissed || res.Err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("Fetch of a need no backup lists = %+v, want missed", res)
	}
	if got := partsOf(t, p.Member, stage, scratch2.Table); len(got) != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("a missed restore wrote %+v", got)
	}

	// An object store that refuses connections: the server would retry the
	// index read 500 times; the read's deadline (IndexTimeout) ends it, a
	// refused fetch.
	down := NewRestore(member, RestoreConfig{Endpoint: "http://" + p.PeerHost + ":1", Bucket: s3.Bucket, AccessKeyID: s3.AccessKeyID, Secret: s3.Secret}, owner)
	down.IndexTimeout = 5 * time.Second
	scratch3 := newScratch(t, member, stage, "member-test_"+sfx+"_3", schema)
	began := time.Now()
	res = down.Fetch(context.Background(), need, schema, scratch3)
	took := time.Since(began)
	if res.Outcome != OutcomeRefused || res.Err == nil || took > down.IndexTimeout+20*time.Second {
		t.Fatalf("Fetch from an endpoint that refuses connections = %+v after %s, want refused within the index read's deadline of %s", res, took, down.IndexTimeout)
	}
	if !strings.Contains(res.Err.Error(), "read the backup indexes of indexer") {
		t.Fatalf("the refusal %v does not name the index read", res.Err)
	}
	if strings.Contains(res.Err.Error(), s3.Secret) || strings.Contains(res.Err.Error(), s3.AccessKeyID) {
		t.Fatalf("the restore error carries the key: %v", res.Err)
	}
	if parts := partsOf(t, p.Member, stage, scratch3.Table); len(parts) != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("a refused restore wrote %+v", parts)
	}
	t.Logf("endpoint refusing connections: %s after %s: %v", res.Outcome, took.Round(time.Millisecond), res.Err)
}
```

- [ ] **Step 6: Implement the shared types and the outcome mapping**

Create `member/sources/source.go`:

```go
// Package sources fills one scratch table of a member's hg_rstage database
// with the bytes of one manifest or candidate part (housegate spec 2026-10-14
// §8.6): the owner pull from the owner's hg_safe, the unsafe pulls from the
// owner's own hg_unsafe (the shadow verifier) or a network verifier's
// hg_unsafe (the peer unsafe pull), and the restore of the owner's verified
// object-store backup.
//
// No transport is trusted. A source only writes into the scratch it is given
// and reports what the scratch holds afterwards; the install gate
// (member/install around member/gate) scans and classifies it. A source never
// retries: a missed, refused or unreachable fetch returns at once, so the
// caller moves to its next source and defers a part no source delivers (plan
// S3-C2 K35).
//
// posture.go holds the member's startup probes: remote() must be read-only for
// its user, and its ClickHouse must enforce the engine fence.
package sources

import (
	"context"
	"errors"
	"fmt"
	"regexp"
	"strings"
	"time"

	clickhouse "github.com/ClickHouse/clickhouse-go/v2"

	"github.com/housegate/housegate/pkg/replay"
	"github.com/housegate/housegate/pkg/replay/payloadexec"

	"github.com/sentioxyz/arbiter-core"
	"github.com/sentioxyz/arbiter-core/dataplane/chparts"
	"github.com/sentioxyz/arbiter-core/dataplane/ddl"
)

// Outcome is how one fetch ended (metric label outcome).
type Outcome string

const (
	// OutcomeFetched: the source wrote into the scratch. Result.Parts names
	// what the scratch holds now, which may be nothing (the part was renamed
	// or cleaned between the lookup and the pull: the gate's rename race).
	OutcomeFetched Outcome = "fetched"
	// OutcomeMissed: the source does not hold the part. Nothing was written.
	OutcomeMissed Outcome = "missed"
	// OutcomeRefused: ClickHouse refused the fetch (memory limit, too many
	// simultaneous queries, timeout), or it failed for any other reason.
	OutcomeRefused Outcome = "refused"
	// OutcomeUnreachable: the source's ClickHouse could not be reached.
	OutcomeUnreachable Outcome = "unreachable"
)

// Outcomes lists every outcome, so a stats map can export each one with zeros.
func Outcomes() []Outcome {
	return []Outcome{OutcomeFetched, OutcomeMissed, OutcomeRefused, OutcomeUnreachable}
}

// Source names, the metric label source.
const (
	SourceOwnerPull       = "owner_pull"
	SourcePeerUnsafePull  = "peer_unsafe_pull"
	SourceRestore         = "restore"
	SourceOwnerUnsafePull = "owner_unsafe_pull"
)

// SourceNames lists every source name, so a stats map can export each one with
// zeros.
func SourceNames() []string {
	return []string{SourceOwnerPull, SourcePeerUnsafePull, SourceRestore, SourceOwnerUnsafePull}
}

// Need is one part to fetch: a manifest part (replay.PartManifestEntry) or a
// candidate part (arbiter.CandidatePart). TableKey is the logical table id
// (<database>.<table>); Table is the owner-side physical name
// (ddl.CHTableName). PartName is informational: a pull resolves the current
// name on the owner, because a REPLACE PARTITION renames parts and keeps
// their hash_of_all_files.
type Need struct {
	TableKey, Table, PartitionID, PartName, PartPhysHash, PartRowLtHash string
	RowCount                                                            uint64
}

// NeedOfManifestPart is the need of one part a manifest lists.
func NeedOfManifestPart(p replay.PartManifestEntry) Need {
	return Need{
		TableKey: p.TableID, Table: ddl.CHTableName(p.TableID), PartitionID: p.PartitionID,
		PartName: p.PartName, PartPhysHash: p.PartPhysHash, PartRowLtHash: p.PartRowLtHash, RowCount: p.RowCount,
	}
}

// NeedOfCandidatePart is the need of one candidate part a block's statement
// names.
func NeedOfCandidatePart(c arbiter.CandidatePart) Need {
	return Need{
		TableKey: c.TableID, Table: ddl.CHTableName(c.TableID), PartitionID: c.PartitionID,
		PartName: c.PartName, PartPhysHash: c.PartPhysHash, PartRowLtHash: c.PartRowLtHash, RowCount: c.RowCount,
	}
}

// Scratch is one scratch table on the member's ClickHouse (hg_rstage).
type Scratch struct {
	Database, Table string
}

func (s Scratch) qualified() string { return ident(s.Database) + "." + ident(s.Table) }

// Result is what one fetch did. Parts names the active parts of the scratch
// after a fetched outcome. Err is set on every refused or unreachable fetch;
// such a fetch may have left rows of a partial insert in the scratch, so the
// caller gives its next source a fresh scratch. A missed fetch wrote nothing.
type Result struct {
	Source  string
	Outcome Outcome
	Parts   []string
	Err     error
}

// Source fetches one needed part into a scratch.
type Source interface {
	Name() string
	Fetch(ctx context.Context, need Need, schema payloadexec.TableSchema, scratch Scratch) Result
}

// NoSplitSettings are the settings under which INSERT ... SELECT writes a
// source part of rows rows as one part (housegate spec 2026-10-14 §2,
// mechanics M6): one insert block of at least rows rows, no byte bound, one
// reading and one inserting thread.
func NoSplitSettings(rows uint64) clickhouse.Settings {
	return clickhouse.Settings{
		"min_insert_block_size_rows":  max(rows, 1),
		"min_insert_block_size_bytes": 0,
		"max_threads":                 1,
		"max_insert_threads":          1,
	}
}

// ClickHouse error codes the outcomes and the posture probes read.
const (
	codeTimeoutExceeded            int32 = 159
	codeTooManySimultaneousQueries int32 = 202
	codeSocketTimeout              int32 = 209
	codeNetworkError               int32 = 210
	codeMemoryLimitExceeded        int32 = 241
	codeAllConnectionTriesFailed   int32 = 279
	codeAccessDenied               int32 = 497
	// codeNoRemoteShardAvailable is what remote() answers when it cannot
	// fetch the remote table's structure: on 25.8 and 26.3 for an
	// unreachable server, and also for a table the reachable server lacks
	// (measured; plan S3-C2 Appendix B).
	codeNoRemoteShardAvailable int32 = 519
)

// outcomeOf maps a failed fetch to its outcome (plan S3-C2 K35): a refusal by
// a ClickHouse limit is refused, a connection failure unreachable, anything
// else refused.
func outcomeOf(err error) Outcome {
	var exception *clickhouse.Exception
	if errors.As(err, &exception) {
		switch exception.Code {
		case codeMemoryLimitExceeded, codeTooManySimultaneousQueries, codeTimeoutExceeded:
			return OutcomeRefused
		case codeNetworkError, codeSocketTimeout, codeAllConnectionTriesFailed, codeNoRemoteShardAvailable:
			return OutcomeUnreachable
		}
	}
	return OutcomeRefused
}

func failure(res Result, step string, err error) Result {
	res.Outcome = outcomeOf(err)
	res.Parts = nil
	res.Err = fmt.Errorf("sources: %s: %s: %w", res.Source, step, err)
	return res
}

// identifierRE is the form of a named collection, which remote() takes bare.
var identifierRE = regexp.MustCompile(`^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*$`)

// ident backquotes an identifier with dataplane/ddl's rule.
func ident(id string) string {
	id = strings.ReplaceAll(id, `\`, `\\`)
	id = strings.ReplaceAll(id, "`", "``")
	return "`" + id + "`"
}

// literal quotes a string literal with dataplane/ddl's rule.
func literal(s string) string { return "'" + chparts.EscapeSQLString(s) + "'" }

func checkScratch(s Scratch) error {
	if s.Database == "" || s.Table == "" {
		return fmt.Errorf("sources: scratch needs a database and a table, got %q.%q", s.Database, s.Table)
	}
	return nil
}

const scratchPartsQuery = "SELECT name FROM system.parts WHERE database = ? AND table = ? AND active ORDER BY name"

// scratchParts lists the active parts of a member table by name.
func scratchParts(ctx context.Context, conn clickhouse.Conn, s Scratch) ([]string, error) {
	rows, err := conn.Query(ctx, scratchPartsQuery, s.Database, s.Table)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	defer rows.Close()
	var names []string
	for rows.Next() {
		var name string
		if err := rows.Scan(&name); err != nil {
			return nil, err
		}
		names = append(names, name)
	}
	return names, rows.Err()
}

// cleanupTimeout bounds the drop of a temporary table after its fetch.
const cleanupTimeout = time.Minute

// dropTemporary drops a temporary member table of one fetch (a fallback
// candidate or a restore target), also after ctx ended. A drop that fails
// leaves a table whose name starts with the scratch's, so the member's
// startup drop of its node-prefixed hg_rstage tables removes it.
func dropTemporary(ctx context.Context, conn clickhouse.Conn, s Scratch) {
	ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.WithoutCancel(ctx), cleanupTimeout)
	defer cancel()
	_ = conn.Exec(ctx, "DROP TABLE IF EXISTS "+s.qualified()+" SYNC")
}
```
