- [ ] **Step 7: Implement the remote pulls**

Create `member/sources/remote_pull.go`:

```go
package sources

import (
	"context"
	"fmt"
	"sync"

	clickhouse "github.com/ClickHouse/clickhouse-go/v2"

	"github.com/housegate/housegate/pkg/replay/chexec"
	"github.com/housegate/housegate/pkg/replay/payloadexec"

	"github.com/sentioxyz/arbiter-core/dataplane/chparts"
)

const (
	// DefaultMaxFallbackCandidates bounds the row-hash fallback of the owner
	// pull: at most this many parts of the needed partition and row count
	// are pulled by one Fetch.
	DefaultMaxFallbackCandidates = 8
	// NoFallback as MaxFallbackCandidates turns the row-hash fallback off.
	// The unsafe pulls use it: an hg_unsafe part is never rebuilt (merges
	// are pinned off and no REPLACE runs there), so a part whose
	// hash_of_all_files is gone was cleaned, and pulling other parts of the
	// same row count could only cost reads.
	NoFallback = -1
	// maxFallbackCursors bounds the fallback positions a RemotePull
	// remembers; beyond it they are forgotten, and each need's next fallback
	// starts from the first candidate of its partition again.
	maxFallbackCursors = 1024

	defaultSafeDatabase   = "hg_safe"
	defaultUnsafeDatabase = "hg_unsafe"
)

// RemotePull copies one part out of another ClickHouse into a scratch with
// INSERT ... SELECT FROM remote(<Collection>, ...) WHERE _part = <name> under
// NoSplitSettings (housegate spec 2026-10-14 §8.6). Collection is a named
// collection on the member's ClickHouse whose host, port, user and password
// are NOT OVERRIDABLE (contract §23.2), so no host, user or password ever
// appears in SQL. The part's current name is resolved on the source by
// hash_of_all_files (a REPLACE PARTITION renames parts and keeps the hash);
// when no active part has that hash, the owner pull falls back to the parts
// of the needed partition and row count (housegate spec 2026-10-14 §8.6),
// pulls each into its own fresh scratch <scratch>_c<k> and keeps the first
// whose scan is the needed row hash. The pull filters on _part only, never
// on the manifest's logical partition id, and only the system.parts columns
// the reader user is granted are named. The fallback scopes its listing to
// ClickHouse's partition_id of the need's partition, which the member's own
// server computes from the logical id with partitionId() (the reader may not
// read the partition column, and the logical id is not ClickHouse's), before
// it applies MaxFallbackCandidates; a Fetch that pulled a full window
// without keeping a part leaves a cursor, and the next Fetch of that need
// lists the candidates after it, so every candidate of the partition is
// pulled within a bounded number of fetches.
type RemotePull struct {
	Conn                  clickhouse.Conn
	SourceName            string
	Collection            string
	Database              string
	MaxFallbackCandidates int // 0: DefaultMaxFallbackCandidates; NoFallback: none

	// mu guards after: per need (fallbackKey), the name of the last
	// candidate a full fallback window pulled without keeping it.
	mu    sync.Mutex
	after map[string]string
}

// NewOwnerPull pulls from the owner's hg_safe (safeDatabase; "" is hg_safe).
func NewOwnerPull(conn clickhouse.Conn, collection, safeDatabase string) *RemotePull {
	if safeDatabase == "" {
		safeDatabase = defaultSafeDatabase
	}
	return &RemotePull{Conn: conn, SourceName: SourceOwnerPull, Collection: collection, Database: safeDatabase}
}

// NewOwnerUnsafePull pulls a candidate part from the owner's hg_unsafe
// (unsafeDatabase; "" is hg_unsafe), for the shadow verifier.
func NewOwnerUnsafePull(conn clickhouse.Conn, collection, unsafeDatabase string) *RemotePull {
	if unsafeDatabase == "" {
		unsafeDatabase = defaultUnsafeDatabase
	}
	return &RemotePull{Conn: conn, SourceName: SourceOwnerUnsafePull, Collection: collection, Database: unsafeDatabase, MaxFallbackCandidates: NoFallback}
}

// NewPeerUnsafePull pulls from a network verifier's hg_unsafe replica through
// its pool collection (si_peer_verifier_<n>).
func NewPeerUnsafePull(conn clickhouse.Conn, collection string) *RemotePull {
	return &RemotePull{Conn: conn, SourceName: SourcePeerUnsafePull, Collection: collection, Database: defaultUnsafeDatabase, MaxFallbackCandidates: NoFallback}
}

// Name is the source's metric label.
func (p *RemotePull) Name() string { return p.SourceName }

// Fetch pulls need into scratch, an empty table of the copy's structure
// (ddl.ScratchIntent).
func (p *RemotePull) Fetch(ctx context.Context, need Need, schema payloadexec.TableSchema, scratch Scratch) Result {
	res := Result{Source: p.SourceName}
	if err := p.check(need, scratch); err != nil {
		res.Outcome, res.Err = OutcomeRefused, err
		return res
	}
	if need.PartPhysHash != "" {
		name, rows, found, err := p.resolveByHash(ctx, need)
		if err != nil {
			return failure(res, "resolve the part by hash_of_all_files", err)
		}
		if found {
			if err := p.pull(ctx, scratch, need.Table, name, rows); err != nil {
				return failure(res, "pull part "+name, err)
			}
			return p.fetched(ctx, res, scratch)
		}
	}
	limit := p.fallbackLimit()
	if limit == 0 || need.RowCount == 0 || need.PartRowLtHash == "" {
		res.Outcome = OutcomeMissed
		return res
	}
	partitionID, err := p.partitionIDOf(ctx, need, schema)
	if err != nil {
		return failure(res, "resolve the partition id of "+need.PartitionID, err)
	}
	key := fallbackKey(need, partitionID)
	candidates, err := p.candidatesByRows(ctx, need, partitionID, p.cursor(key), limit)
	if err != nil {
		return failure(res, "list the parts of the needed partition and row count", err)
	}
	for k, name := range candidates {
		candidate := Scratch{Database: scratch.Database, Table: fmt.Sprintf("%s_c%d", scratch.Table, k+1)}
		kept, err := p.tryCandidate(ctx, need, schema, scratch, candidate, name)
		if err != nil {
			return failure(res, "pull candidate part "+name, err)
		}
		if kept {
			p.setCursor(key, "")
			return p.fetched(ctx, res, scratch)
		}
	}
	p.setCursor(key, nextFallbackCursor(candidates, limit))
	res.Outcome = OutcomeMissed
	return res
}

// nextFallbackCursor is where the next fallback of a need lists from after a
// window of candidates that kept nothing: after its last name when the window
// was full, else (the partition's listing ended) from the first again.
func nextFallbackCursor(candidates []string, limit int) string {
	if len(candidates) < limit || len(candidates) == 0 {
		return ""
	}
	return candidates[len(candidates)-1]
}

// fallbackKey identifies one need's fallback: the physical table, ClickHouse's
// partition id, the row hash and the row count.
func fallbackKey(need Need, partitionID string) string {
	return fmt.Sprintf("%s\x00%s\x00%s\x00%d", need.Table, partitionID, need.PartRowLtHash, need.RowCount)
}

func (p *RemotePull) cursor(key string) string {
	p.mu.Lock()
	defer p.mu.Unlock()
	return p.after[key]
}

func (p *RemotePull) setCursor(key, after string) {
	p.mu.Lock()
	defer p.mu.Unlock()
	if after == "" {
		delete(p.after, key)
		return
	}
	if p.after == nil || len(p.after) >= maxFallbackCursors {
		p.after = map[string]string{}
	}
	p.after[key] = after
}

// partitionIDOf is ClickHouse's partition_id of the need's logical partition
// (chparts.LogicalPartitionID): "all" for an unpartitioned table; else
// partitionId() over the partition value, computed by the member's own
// server as every server computes it for a part (the partition key is one
// bare String column, ddl's partition freeze; measured equal to
// system.parts.partition_id on 25.8.28.1 and 26.3.51.7, Appendix B). The
// query reads no table, so it needs no grant.
func (p *RemotePull) partitionIDOf(ctx context.Context, need Need, schema payloadexec.TableSchema) (string, error) {
	value, err := chparts.QuotePartition(schema, need.PartitionID)
	if err != nil {
		return "", err
	}
	if schema.PartitionBy == "" {
		return "all", nil
	}
	rows, err := p.Conn.Query(ctx, partitionIDQuery(value))
	if err != nil {
		return "", err
	}
	defer rows.Close()
	if !rows.Next() {
		if err := rows.Err(); err != nil {
			return "", err
		}
		return "", fmt.Errorf("%s returned no row", partitionIDQuery(value))
	}
	var id string
	if err := rows.Scan(&id); err != nil {
		return "", err
	}
	return id, rows.Err()
}

func partitionIDQuery(quotedValue string) string {
	return "SELECT partitionId(" + quotedValue + ")"
}

func (p *RemotePull) check(need Need, scratch Scratch) error {
	if !identifierRE.MatchString(p.Collection) {
		return fmt.Errorf("sources: %s: collection %q must be one ClickHouse identifier ([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*)", p.SourceName, p.Collection)
	}
	if p.Database == "" || need.Table == "" {
		return fmt.Errorf("sources: %s: a pull needs a source database and table, got %q.%q", p.SourceName, p.Database, need.Table)
	}
	return checkScratch(scratch)
}

func (p *RemotePull) fallbackLimit() int {
	switch {
	case p.MaxFallbackCandidates == 0:
		return DefaultMaxFallbackCandidates
	case p.MaxFallbackCandidates < 0:
		return 0
	default:
		return p.MaxFallbackCandidates
	}
}

// partsTable is the source's system.parts through the collection.
func (p *RemotePull) partsTable() string {
	return "remote(" + ident(p.Collection) + ", database = 'system', table = 'parts')"
}

func (p *RemotePull) resolveQuery(need Need) string {
	return "SELECT name, rows FROM " + p.partsTable() +
		" WHERE database = " + literal(p.Database) + " AND table = " + literal(need.Table) +
		" AND active AND hash_of_all_files = " + literal(need.PartPhysHash)
}

// fallbackQuery lists, in name order, at most limit active parts of the
// source table in ClickHouse partition partitionID with the needed row
// count, after the part name after ("" lists from the first).
func (p *RemotePull) fallbackQuery(need Need, partitionID, after string, limit int) string {
	q := fmt.Sprintf("SELECT name FROM %s WHERE database = %s AND table = %s AND active AND partition_id = %s AND rows = %d",
		p.partsTable(), literal(p.Database), literal(need.Table), literal(partitionID), need.RowCount)
	if after != "" {
		q += " AND name > " + literal(after)
	}
	return q + fmt.Sprintf(" ORDER BY name LIMIT %d", limit)
}

func (p *RemotePull) pullQuery(into Scratch, table, part string) string {
	return "INSERT INTO " + into.qualified() + " SELECT * FROM remote(" + ident(p.Collection) +
		", database = " + literal(p.Database) + ", table = " + literal(table) + ") WHERE _part = " + literal(part)
}

// resolveByHash finds the active part of the source table whose
// hash_of_all_files is the need's; of resurrected equal-hash twins (equal
// bytes) it takes the smallest name.
func (p *RemotePull) resolveByHash(ctx context.Context, need Need) (string, uint64, bool, error) {
	rows, err := p.Conn.Query(ctx, p.resolveQuery(need))
	if err != nil {
		return "", 0, false, err
	}
	defer rows.Close()
	var (
		name  string
		count uint64
		found bool
	)
	for rows.Next() {
		var n string
		var r uint64
		if err := rows.Scan(&n, &r); err != nil {
			return "", 0, false, err
		}
		if !found || n < name {
			name, count, found = n, r, true
		}
	}
	return name, count, found, rows.Err()
}

func (p *RemotePull) candidatesByRows(ctx context.Context, need Need, partitionID, after string, limit int) ([]string, error) {
	rows, err := p.Conn.Query(ctx, p.fallbackQuery(need, partitionID, after, limit))
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	defer rows.Close()
	var names []string
	for rows.Next() {
		var n string
		if err := rows.Scan(&n); err != nil {
			return nil, err
		}
		names = append(names, n)
	}
	return names, rows.Err()
}

func (p *RemotePull) pull(ctx context.Context, into Scratch, table, part string, rows uint64) error {
	ctx = clickhouse.Context(ctx, clickhouse.WithSettings(NoSplitSettings(rows)))
	return p.Conn.Exec(ctx, p.pullQuery(into, table, part))
}

// tryCandidate pulls one fallback candidate into its own fresh scratch
// (created AS the scratch, so it has the copy's structure, settings and
// storage policy) and, when its one part is the needed row hash and row
// count, attaches it into the scratch, keeping the pulled bytes.
func (p *RemotePull) tryCandidate(ctx context.Context, need Need, schema payloadexec.TableSchema, scratch, candidate Scratch, name string) (bool, error) {
	defer dropTemporary(ctx, p.Conn, candidate)
	if err := p.Conn.Exec(ctx, "CREATE TABLE "+candidate.qualified()+" AS "+scratch.qualified()); err != nil {
		return false, err
	}
	if err := p.pull(ctx, candidate, need.Table, name, need.RowCount); err != nil {
		return false, err
	}
	scans, err := chexec.ScanAllParts(ctx, p.Conn, candidate.Database+"."+candidate.Table, schema)
	if err != nil {
		return false, err
	}
	if len(scans) != 1 || scans[0].RowLtHash != need.PartRowLtHash || scans[0].RowCount != need.RowCount {
		return false, nil
	}
	var partitionID string
	if err := p.Conn.QueryRow(ctx, "SELECT partition_id FROM system.parts WHERE database = ? AND table = ? AND name = ? AND active",
		candidate.Database, candidate.Table, scans[0].PartName).Scan(&partitionID); err != nil {
		return false, err
	}
	err = p.Conn.Exec(ctx, "ALTER TABLE "+scratch.qualified()+" ATTACH PARTITION ID "+literal(partitionID)+" FROM "+candidate.qualified())
	return err == nil, err
}

func (p *RemotePull) fetched(ctx context.Context, res Result, scratch Scratch) Result {
	parts, err := scratchParts(ctx, p.Conn, scratch)
	if err != nil {
		return failure(res, "list the scratch parts", err)
	}
	res.Outcome, res.Parts = OutcomeFetched, parts
	return res
}
```

- [ ] **Step 8: Implement the object-store restore**

Create `member/sources/restore.go`:

```go
package sources

import (
	"context"
	"errors"
	"fmt"
	"log/slog"
	"strings"
	"time"

	clickhouse "github.com/ClickHouse/clickhouse-go/v2"

	"github.com/housegate/housegate/pkg/replay/payloadexec"

	"github.com/sentioxyz/arbiter-core/dataplane/objstore"
)

const redacted = "[redacted]"

// RestoreIndexTimeout is the default deadline of the index read. ClickHouse
// 26.3 defaults s3_retry_attempts to 500, so an object store that refuses
// connections keeps the read retrying for many minutes (measured), and
// objstore.ReadIndexes replaces the context's query settings with its own, so
// the setting cannot be lowered for it. A context deadline survives:
// clickhouse-go sends it as max_execution_time, which stops the server's
// retries too, and the fetch is refused at the deadline (plan S3-C2 K35). The
// RESTORE keeps the caller's context: once the index read succeeded the
// store is reachable, and a partition restore may be long.
const RestoreIndexTimeout = 2 * time.Minute

// RestoreConfig is the member's read-only view of the per-owner backups of
// Plan S3-C1: Endpoint is http(s)://<host>[:port], Bucket the bucket name.
// The key pair comes only from the member's environment
// (STORAGE_INTEGRITY_MEMBER_RESTORE_ACCESS_KEY_ID and
// STORAGE_INTEGRITY_MEMBER_RESTORE_SECRET, contract §24.2); String, GoString
// and LogValue never print either part of it.
type RestoreConfig struct {
	Endpoint, Bucket, AccessKeyID, Secret string
}

func (c RestoreConfig) String() string {
	return fmt.Sprintf("RestoreConfig{Endpoint: %q, Bucket: %q, AccessKeyID: %s, Secret: %s}", c.Endpoint, c.Bucket, redacted, redacted)
}

// GoString keeps %#v from printing the keys.
func (c RestoreConfig) GoString() string { return c.String() }

func (c RestoreConfig) LogValue() slog.Value {
	return slog.GroupValue(
		slog.String("endpoint", c.Endpoint), slog.String("bucket", c.Bucket),
		slog.String("access_key_id", redacted), slog.String("secret", redacted))
}

// RestoreSource restores a needed part from the owner's newest verified
// backup (housegate spec 2026-10-14 §8.6, plan S3-C1 contract §17): it reads
// the index objects under owner-<owner>/, picks the newest backup whose index
// lists a part of the needed physical table with the needed
// hash_of_all_files, restores that table's partition with objstore's
// RESTORE ... AS <scratch>_r PARTITIONS ... FROM S3(...) (the member's READ ON
// S3, K33), copies the needed part into the scratch with a local no-split
// INSERT ... SELECT ... WHERE _part = <name>, and drops <scratch>_r. RESTORE
// renames parts and keeps their hash_of_all_files (measured), so the part is
// found in <scratch>_r by its hash; copying it, rather than attaching it,
// keeps the scratch's own storage policy for ATTACH PARTITION ... FROM into
// the copy, and row hashes are content hashes, so the copy keeps the needed
// one. Parts of the restored partition that the need does not name never
// reach the scratch. A need that no backup lists is missed. The RESTORE runs
// synchronously: objstore's asynchronous restore polls system.backups, which
// the member's user may not read.
type RestoreSource struct {
	// IndexTimeout is the deadline of the index read; 0 is
	// RestoreIndexTimeout.
	IndexTimeout time.Duration

	conn  clickhouse.Conn
	cfg   RestoreConfig
	owner uint64
}

// NewRestore restores from the backups of owner (its indexer id).
func NewRestore(conn clickhouse.Conn, cfg RestoreConfig, owner uint64) *RestoreSource {
	return &RestoreSource{conn: conn, cfg: cfg, owner: owner}
}

// Name is the source's metric label.
func (r *RestoreSource) Name() string { return SourceRestore }

func (r *RestoreSource) String() string {
	return fmt.Sprintf("RestoreSource{owner: %d, config: %s}", r.owner, r.cfg)
}

// GoString keeps %#v from printing the keys.
func (r *RestoreSource) GoString() string { return r.String() }

func (r *RestoreSource) LogValue() slog.Value {
	return slog.GroupValue(slog.Uint64("owner", r.owner), slog.Any("config", r.cfg))
}

// Fetch restores need into scratch. No error it returns carries a statement
// (the restore and index statements hold the key pair), and scrub removes
// either part of the key from any server message that echoes one.
func (r *RestoreSource) Fetch(ctx context.Context, need Need, schema payloadexec.TableSchema, scratch Scratch) Result {
	res := Result{Source: SourceRestore}
	if err := checkScratch(scratch); err != nil {
		res.Outcome, res.Err = OutcomeRefused, err
		return res
	}
	if need.Table == "" || need.PartPhysHash == "" {
		res.Outcome = OutcomeMissed
		return res
	}
	bucket, err := objstore.ParseBucket(strings.TrimRight(r.cfg.Endpoint, "/") + "/" + r.cfg.Bucket)
	if err != nil {
		return r.scrub(failure(res, "the restore bucket", err))
	}
	creds := objstore.Credentials{AccessKeyID: r.cfg.AccessKeyID, SecretAccessKey: r.cfg.Secret}
	timeout := r.IndexTimeout
	if timeout <= 0 {
		timeout = RestoreIndexTimeout
	}
	indexCtx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(ctx, timeout)
	indexes, err := objstore.ReadIndexes(indexCtx, r.conn, bucket, r.owner, creds)
	cancel()
	if err != nil {
		return r.scrub(failure(res, fmt.Sprintf("read the backup indexes of indexer %d", r.owner), err))
	}
	backup, ok := r.newestListing(indexes, need)
	if !ok {
		res.Outcome = OutcomeMissed
		return res
	}
	clause, err := objstore.PartitionClause(schema, need.PartitionID)
	if err != nil {
		return r.scrub(failure(res, "the restore partition", err))
	}
	staged := Scratch{Database: scratch.Database, Table: scratch.Table + "_r"}
	dropTemporary(ctx, r.conn, staged)
	defer dropTemporary(ctx, r.conn, staged)
	restore := objstore.RestoreSQL(bucket, r.owner, backup, need.Table, clause,
		objstore.Scratch{Database: staged.Database, Table: staged.Table}, creds)
	if err := r.conn.Exec(ctx, restore); err != nil {
		return r.scrub(failure(res, fmt.Sprintf("restore %s partition %s from backup %s", need.Table, need.PartitionID, backup), err))
	}
	name, rows, found, err := r.restoredPart(ctx, staged, need.PartPhysHash)
	if err != nil {
		return r.scrub(failure(res, "find the restored part", err))
	}
	if !found {
		res.Outcome = OutcomeMissed
		return res
	}
	copyPart := "INSERT INTO " + scratch.qualified() + " SELECT * FROM " + staged.qualified() + " WHERE _part = " + literal(name)
	if err := r.conn.Exec(clickhouse.Context(ctx, clickhouse.WithSettings(NoSplitSettings(rows))), copyPart); err != nil {
		return r.scrub(failure(res, "copy the restored part "+name, err))
	}
	parts, err := scratchParts(ctx, r.conn, scratch)
	if err != nil {
		return r.scrub(failure(res, "list the scratch parts", err))
	}
	res.Outcome, res.Parts = OutcomeFetched, parts
	return res
}

// newestListing is the newest backup of the owner whose index lists a part of
// need's physical table with need's hash_of_all_files. Backup names start
// with their UTC start time, and objstore.ReadIndexes sorts by name.
func (r *RestoreSource) newestListing(indexes []objstore.BackupIndex, need Need) (string, bool) {
	for i := len(indexes) - 1; i >= 0; i-- {
		idx := indexes[i]
		if idx.OwnerIndexerID != r.owner {
			continue
		}
		for _, t := range idx.Tables {
			if t.PhysicalTable != need.Table {
				continue
			}
			for _, part := range t.Parts {
				if part.PhysHash == need.PartPhysHash {
					return idx.Name, true
				}
			}
		}
	}
	return "", false
}

func (r *RestoreSource) restoredPart(ctx context.Context, staged Scratch, physHash string) (string, uint64, bool, error) {
	rows, err := r.conn.Query(ctx, "SELECT name, rows FROM system.parts WHERE database = ? AND table = ? AND active AND hash_of_all_files = ? ORDER BY name LIMIT 1",
		staged.Database, staged.Table, physHash)
	if err != nil {
		return "", 0, false, err
	}
	defer rows.Close()
	if !rows.Next() {
		return "", 0, false, rows.Err()
	}
	var name string
	var count uint64
	if err := rows.Scan(&name, &count); err != nil {
		return "", 0, false, err
	}
	return name, count, true, rows.Err()
}

// scrub replaces each part of the restore key in res.Err's text with
// [redacted]. The outcome was taken from the original error first; the
// scrubbed error does not unwrap to it, so no caller can print the original
// server message through errors.As.
func (r *RestoreSource) scrub(res Result) Result {
	if res.Err == nil {
		return res
	}
	text := res.Err.Error()
	for _, key := range []string{r.cfg.Secret, r.cfg.AccessKeyID} {
		if key != "" {
			text = strings.ReplaceAll(text, key, redacted)
		}
	}
	if text != res.Err.Error() {
		res.Err = errors.New(text)
	}
	return res
}
```

- [ ] **Step 9: Implement the posture probes**

Create `member/sources/posture.go`:

```go
package sources

import (
	"context"
	"errors"
	"fmt"
	"strings"

	clickhouse "github.com/ClickHouse/clickhouse-go/v2"
)

// The member's startup posture probes (housegate spec 2026-10-14 §8.2, §8.6):
// the role refuses to start unless remote() is read-only for its user and its
// ClickHouse enforces access_control_improvements.table_engines_require_grant.
// The behavioural probes are what the role relies on; system.grants is read
// as a second opinion and only where the user may read it.

var (
	ErrRemoteWritable   = errors.New("sources: this user can write through remote()")
	ErrEngineFenceOff   = errors.New("sources: the engine fence is off")
	ErrGrantsUnreadable = errors.New("sources: system.grants is not readable by this user")
)

// refusal is an error whose text is exactly its message and which wraps a
// sentinel, so the contract's refusal texts stay verbatim.
type refusal struct {
	msg      string
	sentinel error
}

func (e *refusal) Error() string { return e.msg }
func (e *refusal) Unwrap() error { return e.sentinel }

// remoteWriteProbeTable is the table the remote() write probe names; the
// probe is refused before any connection, so it never exists anywhere.
const remoteWriteProbeTable = "si_member_write_probe"

// CheckRemoteIsReadOnly proves that this user cannot write through remote():
// INSERT INTO FUNCTION remote(<collection>, ...) must be refused locally with
// ACCESS_DENIED for WRITE ON REMOTE. ClickHouse checks that grant before it
// connects (measured on 25.8 and 26.3), so the probe writes nothing and works
// while the collection's server is down. A refusal that does not name WRITE
// ON REMOTE (the remote server refusing a write that left the member) counts
// as writable.
func CheckRemoteIsReadOnly(ctx context.Context, conn clickhouse.Conn, collection string) error {
	if !identifierRE.MatchString(collection) {
		return fmt.Errorf("sources: collection %q must be one ClickHouse identifier ([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*)", collection)
	}
	err := conn.Exec(ctx, "INSERT INTO FUNCTION remote("+ident(collection)+", database = 'hg_safe', table = "+literal(remoteWriteProbeTable)+") SELECT 1")
	if refusedFor(err, "WRITE ON REMOTE") {
		return nil
	}
	return &refusal{
		msg:      fmt.Sprintf("sources: INSERT INTO FUNCTION remote(%s) was not refused with ACCESS_DENIED (got %v): WRITE ON REMOTE must be absent", collection, err),
		sentinel: ErrRemoteWritable,
	}
}

// CheckEngineFence proves that this user's ClickHouse enforces the engine
// fence: CREATE TABLE <stageDB>.<probeTable> (x UInt8) ENGINE = Log must be
// refused with ACCESS_DENIED for TABLE ENGINE ON Log (no member user is
// granted Log). A leftover probe table is dropped first. When ClickHouse
// creates the table, the probe drops it again and the fence is off. Any other
// failure (no CREATE TABLE right in stageDB, no such database) is returned as
// it is: the probe proved nothing.
func CheckEngineFence(ctx context.Context, conn clickhouse.Conn, stageDB, probeTable string) error {
	probe := Scratch{Database: stageDB, Table: probeTable}
	if err := checkScratch(probe); err != nil {
		return err
	}
	if err := conn.Exec(ctx, "DROP TABLE IF EXISTS "+probe.qualified()+" SYNC"); err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("sources: drop a leftover engine fence probe %s.%s: %w", stageDB, probeTable, err)
	}
	err := conn.Exec(ctx, "CREATE TABLE "+probe.qualified()+" (x UInt8) ENGINE = Log")
	switch {
	case err == nil:
		dropTemporary(ctx, conn, probe)
		return &refusal{
			msg:      "sources: ClickHouse accepted ENGINE = Log for this user: access_control_improvements.table_engines_require_grant is off or the user holds every engine",
			sentinel: ErrEngineFenceOff,
		}
	case refusedFor(err, "TABLE ENGINE ON Log"):
		return nil
	default:
		return fmt.Errorf("sources: the engine fence probe CREATE TABLE %s.%s ... ENGINE = Log failed without the TABLE ENGINE refusal: %w", stageDB, probeTable, err)
	}
}

// refusedFor reports whether err is ACCESS_DENIED naming grant.
func refusedFor(err error, grant string) bool {
	var exception *clickhouse.Exception
	return errors.As(err, &exception) && exception.Code == codeAccessDenied && strings.Contains(exception.Message, grant)
}

// Grant is one row of system.grants. ClickHouse 25.8 and 26.3 render a
// source grant (READ or WRITE ON <source>) with database and table NULL and
// the source in access_object ("" for ON *), and a partial revoke as a row
// with is_partial_revoke set (measured; plan S3-C2 Appendix B), so READ ON
// REMOTE and READ ON S3 differ only in AccessObject.
type Grant struct {
	AccessType, Database, Table string
	AccessObject                string
	PartialRevoke               bool
}

// readOwnGrantsQuery reads this user's own grant rows; never SHOW GRANTS.
const readOwnGrantsQuery = "SELECT access_type, database, table, access_object, is_partial_revoke FROM system.grants WHERE user_name = currentUser()"

// ReadOwnGrants reads this user's grants from system.grants. A user without
// SELECT on system.grants (the stock server configuration requires the grant
// for system tables, and the member's grants of contract §23.2 do not hold
// it) gets an error wrapping ErrGrantsUnreadable; the role then relies on the
// behavioural probes alone and exports the fact. Grants through roles are not
// read.
func ReadOwnGrants(ctx context.Context, conn clickhouse.Conn) ([]Grant, error) {
	rows, err := conn.Query(ctx, readOwnGrantsQuery)
	if err != nil {
		var exception *clickhouse.Exception
		if errors.As(err, &exception) && exception.Code == codeAccessDenied {
			return nil, fmt.Errorf("%w: %v", ErrGrantsUnreadable, err)
		}
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("sources: read system.grants: %w", err)
	}
	defer rows.Close()
	var out []Grant
	for rows.Next() {
		var (
			g               Grant
			database, table *string
			partial         uint8
		)
		if err := rows.Scan(&g.AccessType, &database, &table, &g.AccessObject, &partial); err != nil {
			return nil, fmt.Errorf("sources: read system.grants: %w", err)
		}
		if database != nil {
			g.Database = *database
		}
		if table != nil {
			g.Table = *table
		}
		g.PartialRevoke = partial != 0
		out = append(out, g)
	}
	if err := rows.Err(); err != nil {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("sources: read system.grants: %w", err)
	}
	return out, nil
}

// CheckRemoteGrants requires READ ON REMOTE and no WRITE ON REMOTE in grants.
// ClickHouse renders READ ON REMOTE as (READ, REMOTE), READ ON * as (READ,
// ""), the legacy REMOTE ON *.* as both (READ, REMOTE) and (WRITE, REMOTE),
// SOURCES ON *.* as (READ, "") and (WRITE, ""), ALL as (ALL, ""), and a
// REVOKE WRITE ON REMOTE under WRITE ON * as a partial-revoke row (WRITE,
// REMOTE).
func CheckRemoteGrants(grants []Grant) error {
	if sourceRight(grants, "WRITE", "REMOTE") {
		return errors.New("sources: system.grants shows WRITE ON REMOTE for this user")
	}
	if !sourceRight(grants, "READ", "REMOTE") {
		return errors.New("sources: system.grants shows no READ ON REMOTE for this user")
	}
	return nil
}

// sourceRight reports whether grants give right (READ or WRITE) on source.
func sourceRight(grants []Grant, right, source string) bool {
	granted, revoked := false, false
	for _, g := range grants {
		if g.Database != "" || g.Table != "" {
			continue
		}
		onSource := g.AccessObject == "" || g.AccessObject == source
		if g.PartialRevoke {
			if (g.AccessType == right || g.AccessType == "ALL") && onSource {
				revoked = true
			}
			continue
		}
		if g.AccessType == "ALL" || (g.AccessType == right && onSource) {
			granted = true
		}
	}
	return granted && !revoked
}
```

The block pulls `clickhouse/clickhouse-server:25.8`, `clickhouse/clickhouse-server:26.3.37.3` and `bitnamilegacy/minio:2024.12.18-debian-12-r1@sha256:c0ede65eb88e47138470202c517bacf55ab3c27df848030b7b46e69d34b7d192` (Plan S3-C1's MinIO pin, Notes) from Docker Hub when they are not present locally: that download needs explicit user confirmation in chat before running. It runs as `bash -s` whatever shell runs the command, starts throwaway containers on one Docker network and removes everything it started on exit. The first run is CI's `integration-clickhouse` shape (two unfenced 25.8 servers whose `default` has Plan S3-A Task 4's CI password); the second is the member's server (a fenced 26.3.37.3 member with contract §23.4's access-control file, an unfenced 26.3.37.3 owner, MinIO). Expected, in order: `25.8.<patch>`, `//member/sources:sources_test PASSED`, `25.8: 18 passed, 1 skipped, 0 failed` (the restore test skips without an object store); `26.3.37.3`, `//member/sources:sources_test PASSED`, `26.3: 19 passed, 0 skipped, 0 failed`; then the measurement lines of the second run, each cut at 160 characters, among them `127.0.0.1:<member port>: fenced true, CheckEngineFence = <nil>`, `127.0.0.1:<peer port>: fenced false, CheckEngineFence = sources: ClickHouse accepted ENGINE = Log for this user: …`, `memory refusal: sources: owner_pull: pull part …: code: 241, …`, `owner_pull unreachable: code 519`, `peer_unsafe_pull unreachable: code 519` and `endpoint refusing connections: refused after <about 5>s: sources: restore: read the backup indexes of indexer <n>: objstore: read the indexes of indexer <n>: context deadline exceeded`. Go prints the PASS lines only under `-test.v`, and a filter or gate that matched nothing would pass silently, hence the counts. Stop and ask before changing code if: the unreachable code is not one of 519, 279, 210 or 209 (the mapping of K35 would have to change); the fenced server reports `fenced false` (the access-control file did not load); the memory refusal is not 241; the index read of the endpoint that refuses connections outlives its 5 s deadline (then the deadline no longer bounds the server's retries); or the restore leaves `<scratch>_r` behind or copies more than the needed part.

## Task 32: arbiter-core — `member/install`, the install gate executor (S3-C2)

Spec §8.5–§8.7 and §8.1's free-space stop, as clarifications K35 and K36 resolve them, with contract §22.2–§22.3's names: the si-member brings every ready copy of every owner in its scope to the validated manifest the feed accepted, only with parts that manifest lists, through Plan S3-C1's pure `member/gate`. Each needed part is fetched into its own fresh scratch table `<node_id>_<boot_nonce>_<n>` of `hg_rstage` from the owner's byte sources in order (while the owner bootstraps, each copy's first part tries the restore first: the P1 backups are the bootstrap source), scanned and classified (kept, rename race, split, doubled, Foreign), checked arithmetically (Σ(L) + Σ(kept) = R and the partition set) and installed with `ATTACH PARTITION … FROM`; a Diverged partition is rebuilt with `DROP PARTITION` followed by `ATTACH PARTITION … FROM`, never with the replacing statement. The installer journals what every copy holds per owner, recovers a part attached before the journal write, audits the copies at startup, after every ClickHouse restart and on a slow self-audit cadence (equal-hash twins dropped with a local `DROP PART`), drops the node's stale scratch tables at startup, pauses installs above the member disk budget, and quarantines a table whose scratch held a foreign part until an operator clears it offline. The package is consumed by Task 33's shadow (`ScratchPrefix`, the startup drop of its `…r` tables), Task 34's `member.Role` (startup steps 7–9: `DropStaleScratch`, `Audit`, `Apply`, the restart watcher and the self-audit ticker), Task 35's `si-member clear-foreign` and metrics, Task 36's kill-mid-stream test (`Deps.AfterAttach`), Plan S3-C4's serving lease (`Deps.BeforeInstall`, `Tables`) and Plan S3-E1's hardlink source (another `sources.Source` in front of the owner pull).

Notes:
- **One owner pass (spec §8.5 steps 1–7, contract §22.3).** `Apply` serves the owners of the ready copies and the owners the journal already holds (an owner without a copy is never journaled, which is what Task 34's readiness expects), ascending. It skips an owner whose journaled entry is ahead of its entry in `u` (next-but-one note, review fix 245-5), and an owner whose journal is at `u.SnapshotID` with every ready copy journaled at its incarnation, without a Diverged partition, an unjournaled part or a quarantine. Otherwise, per ready copy in table-key order: reconcile the copy with `system.parts` (next note), plan every partition the manifest, the journal or the copy knows with `gate.PlanPartition` over (M, R, L), L the journal's row hashes for the partition, fetch each needed part (one fresh scratch per fetch, `ddl.ScratchIntent`) through `Deps.Sources(owner)` in order (the bootstrap probe below aside) and classify it; then verify every copy (closure, placement, partition set); then commit every copy (`BeforeInstall` once per database before its first change, a repair's `DROP PARTITION`, one `ATTACH PARTITION … FROM` per scratch, `AfterAttach` after each); then one journal write holds every copy's parts and the owner's new entry (`u.SnapshotID`, `u.Entries[owner]`). A partition the manifest does not list has the zero root (`SumPartRowLtHashes(nil)`), so a journaled part there makes it Diverged and its repair is a `DROP PARTITION` alone; the manifest's partition set is the set of partitions it lists parts in. A copy whose table the manifest does not list (an incarnation not yet in a table set) must stay empty; one it lists must carry the manifest's `schema_hash` (`TableSchemaHash(NetworkID, copy.Schema)`), else the owner's pass fails with the schema-hash refusal.
- **An owner's copies move together (refines contract §22.3, Appendix B).** The journal holds one (snapshot, entry) per owner and no snapshot per table (§22.2 fixes the shape), and Plan S3-C4 serves a database only while every table of it equals the owner's entry, so a table committed alone would be ahead of the entry `TableState` reports for it. Nothing of an owner therefore changes before every ready copy of it verified, and one deferred part delays the owner's other tables; this is the contract's "an owner's journal entry advances only once every ready copy of that owner closes", applied to the parts as well. A failure after the first change (an `ATTACH` error, `AfterAttach`, a crash) leaves parts the journal does not list; `TableState.Diverged` and `Stats.AuditClean` report them until a pass adopts them.
- **A journal entry never goes back (review fix 245-5).** Owners move independently: each owner's pass commits and journals on its own, so a pass toward `u` that fails for one owner (its repair has no source, say) leaves the others at `u`, and `Apply` returns the joined error while they stay committed. An update offered after that may be older than an owner's journal (before the fix, Task 34's copy watch re-applied the last update whose `Apply` had succeeded); planned against it, the owner's newer parts would be outside the older manifest, so its partitions would be marked Diverged and rebuilt with `DROP PARTITION`, dropping valid newer parts and taking its journal back. So, before it reads, marks or drops anything for an owner, `Apply` compares the owner's entry in `u` with the journaled entry by Task 29's rule for an entry that goes back (either `SafeBlockSeq` or `AppliedPromotionSeq` lower): an owner whose journaled entry is ahead is skipped (`ownerAhead`; warn `install: the update is behind the owner's journal; the owner keeps its copies`), with no Diverged mark, no statement on its copies and no journal write, and the other owners' passes run as usual. An equal entry is not ahead: an owner's tables change only with its entry (`replay.TrackFrontier`), so a pass between two manifests of one entry changes no part. Task 34's copy watch re-applies the newest update the feed offered, so this check only guards against an update that is behind; the K36 adoption of parts a failed pass attached needs that newest target too, because only it still needs their row hashes. `TestApplyNeverTakesAnOwnerBackAfterAPartialPass` runs the case: owner 0 committed at s2 while owner 2's repair failed, then s1 offered again leaves owner 0's parts and entry as they are, and s2 offered again repairs owner 2. With Task 34's target the skip never fires on the arbiter's chain: an owner's journal entry is only ever set from an update the feed offered, the target is the newest offered one, and entries never go back along the chain (Task 29's rule), so no owner is ahead of it, and a role restart starts from a manifest every peer's journal names or from the watermark. Were an older update offered to an owner that is ahead and has a Diverged partition or an unjournaled part, that owner keeps them and `NeedsPass` keeps holding: each re-apply of the same update skips it again (one warn line per pass, no statement on its copies) until an update at or past its entry arrives, so the repair waits for the newest update and never runs against an older one.
- **Reconciliation and recovery (spec §8.7, K36).** Per copy, a journaled part whose name is gone or whose `hash_of_all_files` or rows changed marks its partition Diverged; the parts the journal does not list are scanned by name (`chexec.ScanParts`, one query, never a full scan), one equal in (row hash, `hash_of_all_files`) to a present journaled part is a twin and is dropped with `ALTER TABLE <ReplicaDB>.<copy> DROP PART '<name>'` (after `BeforeInstall`), of unjournaled twins the smallest name stays, and what remains is a candidate. The journal names no in-flight target, so K36's "journaled target manifest" is the manifest of the next `Apply`: an audit only counts the candidates (the copy is unclean), and `Apply` adopts each candidate whose row hash the target still needs (M − L, once per occurrence) or marks its partition Diverged. `Apply` reconciles each copy it touches too (one `system.parts` read per copy and pass), so a journal behind its copy never makes a pass attach a part twice; adoptions are journaled only with the pass, Diverged marks at once.
- **Diverged repair.** A Diverged partition is rebuilt from every part the manifest lists for it, each in its own scratch; after the verification, `ALTER TABLE <ReplicaDB>.<copy> DROP PARTITION <p>` (only when the copy has a part in p) and one `ALTER TABLE <ReplicaDB>.<copy> ATTACH PARTITION <p> FROM <StageDB>.<scratch>` per scratch; the other partitions keep their parts. The replacing statement is never issued: `TestInstallNeverIssuesReplacePartition` reads the package's sources (the `go_test` carries them as `data`), and every ClickHouse-gated test's `recordingConn` fails the test on it and on any `OPTIMIZE`, `TRUNCATE` or `SYSTEM` statement (Global Constraints). Measured while drafting on `clickhouse/clickhouse-server:26.3` (26.3.51.7): a MergeTree table of two good parts and one foreign part, repaired by the replacing statement from a two-part scratch, held 5 rows after `SYSTEM KILL` and the restart, and the same repair with `DROP PARTITION` and `ATTACH PARTITION … FROM` kept 2 (Appendix B, mechanics M3 and M4); `TestInstallDivergedRepairSurvivesAReloadInsideTheOutdatedWindow` measures the member's own path, on 26.3.37.3 in CI.
- **Bootstrap restore probe (spec §8.6: the P1 backups are the bootstrap source; review fix 245-4).** While an owner's journal holds no entry for it (`SnapshotID` empty: its copies are filled for the first time), the first fetch of each of its copies tries the source named `restore` right before the one named `owner_pull` (`restoreBeforeOwnerPull`: any source in front of the owner pull, such as Plan S3-E1's hard-link source, stays in front; without a restore source nothing changes), once per copy and process, also when the pass fails after it and runs again; every other part, and every part once the owner is journaled, keeps the P2 order. The probe installs that part from the newest backup that lists it and proves the member's restore path (its key, `READ ON S3`, the bucket) on every bootstrap, so Plan S3-C3's bootstrap shows installs from the backups beside the owner pull's; it costs one partition restore per copy, because Task 31's restore copies one needed part per `RESTORE` and restoring every part of a bootstrap would restore each partition once per part. A probe that misses, is refused or unreachable is counted and moves to the next source like any fetch.
- **Scratch classification and fallback (spec §8.5 step 4, K35).** A pull is classified with `Single` set to the need's (row hash, rows); the source named `restore` in restore mode (`Single` nil): the needed parts stay and every other part is dropped inside the scratch with `ALTER TABLE <StageDB>.<scratch> DROP PART '<name>'`, and a restore that keeps nothing counts as `missed`. `rename_race` and `doubled` drop the scratch and retry once from a clean one, then move on; `split` moves to the next source at once; `missed`, `refused` and `unreachable` (and a `fetched` result with `Err` set, counted `refused`) move on and are never retried within the pass. A part no source delivered is deferred, in memory, per (owner, table, partition, row hash), 1 m doubling to 30 m; until the deadline no source runs for it and the owner's pass fails at once with `ErrNoSourceSucceeded`; a restart retries at once. Every attempt counts one outcome in `Stats.Outcomes`; `Stats.Installs` counts the kept parts a committed pass installed, per source.
- **The closure is over what the scratches hold.** `verify` lists every scratch again; a scratch that no longer holds exactly its kept parts (name, `hash_of_all_files`, rows) is scanned again and the closure is computed over its content, so a scratch changed after its classification fails Σ(L) + Σ(kept) = R and nothing is attached (`TestInstallClosureFailureInstallsNothing` changes one through the unexported `beforeVerify` seam; with a correct gate the arithmetic cannot fail otherwise). A kept part that ClickHouse placed in another partition than the manifest lists fails the partition-set check, because `ATTACH PARTITION` of the listed partition would attach nothing.
- **Foreign (K36).** A Foreign classification journals the table `foreign` with its `foreign_scratch` (the `StageDB` table name, kept for forensics; `DropStaleScratch` keeps it) and fails the pass with §22.3's text. The quarantine belongs to the table key whatever its incarnation: every later pass of that owner refuses at once with the clear-foreign hint and fetches nothing, the audits skip the table, and the owner's entry stays where it is (every ready copy must close) until an operator runs `sentio-node si-member clear-foreign --table <db.table>` with the si-member stopped. `ClearForeign` takes the state directory's `LOCK` with a non-blocking `flock` (the running role holds it, contract §23.1), clears the mark and the scratch name, and marks every partition the table's journal lists Diverged: the next start drops the scratch, and the next pass rebuilds those partitions through the gate, trusting none of the copy's parts.
- **Audits (spec §8.7).** `Audit` with `startup` or `clickhouse_restart` makes `Stats.AuditClean` false until it completes; it reconciles every ready copy (quarantined tables skipped) without adopting. `self_audit` also scans every journaled, non-Diverged partition in full with `chparts.PartitionContentScan` and marks one whose journaled part's row hash changed; it runs at most once per half `SelfAuditInterval` (Task 34 ticks at the interval, so every tick runs, and a caller cannot loop the full scan). A startup or restart audit that failed leaves installs waiting: `Apply` runs it first. An audit covers the copies that are ready when it runs; the copyset may make a copy ready later (its first pass after the audit, a copy it could not create at first, a new incarnation), and such a copy is unaudited until `Apply` audits it under the same trigger before its pass (`auditUncovered`, review fix 245-1), so a copy the copyset created again empty while the journal still lists its parts is compared with its journal, marked Diverged and rebuilt instead of being skipped as current. `NeedsPass` reports what a pass of the newest update would do without a new manifest (a pending audit, an unaudited copy, a Diverged partition, an unjournaled part, outside an owner with a quarantined table); Task 34's copy watch re-applies the newest update the feed offered while it holds (review fixes 245-2 and 245-5). Task 34 drives `clickhouse_restart` from its `chrestart.Watcher`'s `OnRestart` and `self_audit` from its ticker; `TestAuditRerunsWhenClickHouseUptimeRegresses` wires a real `Watcher` to an uptime the test moves. `AuditClean` is true once an audit completed since the start or the last restart, every ready copy was audited since then, and no ready copy has a Diverged partition or an unjournaled part; a quarantine is reported apart (`TableState.Foreign`).
- **Disk budget (K35).** Before each pass's first fetch `Apply` reads `SELECT sum(bytes_on_disk) FROM system.parts WHERE database IN ('<ReplicaDB>', '<StageDB>')` (every part, active or not, the shadow's and other nodes' scratch included); at or above `StopInstallsRatio × DiskBudgetBytes` it returns `ErrInstallsPaused` with §22.3's text and changes nothing, while `Audit` and the shadow continue. `Stats.DiskUsedBytes` and `InstallsPaused` keep the last reading. The code default stays 0.8; Plan S3-C3 configures 0.5 over the member disk's total on devnet2 (D28), and `TestInstallsPauseAboveTheDiskBudget` runs exactly that ratio with the use at the threshold (installs pause at it) and the same budget at the default (installs run), so a pause that ignored the configured ratio, or paused only above it, fails.
- **Startup drop and names (spec §8.5 last paragraph).** `DropStaleScratch` drops every `StageDB` table that starts with `NodePrefix(NodeID)` except a journaled `foreign_scratch`: the install scratch of every earlier boot, Task 31's restore (`…_r`) and fallback tables, and Task 33's `…_r…` replay and candidate scratch. The role calls it at startup step (7), before the audit and before anything of this boot creates a scratch. A node id holds no underscore (K29), so `member-a_` never matches `member-ab_…`. A boot nonce is 8 lowercase hex characters from `crypto/rand`; the install scratch counter starts at 1 per process.
- **Reach and grants.** ClickHouse only, as `si_member`, within contract §23.2: `CREATE TABLE`, `DROP TABLE`, `ALTER … DROP PART` and `SELECT` on `hg_rstage` (the sources `INSERT` there); `ATTACH PARTITION … FROM` (`SELECT` on the scratch, `ALTER DELETE` and `INSERT` on the copy), `DROP PARTITION` and `DROP PART` (`ALTER DELETE`) and `SELECT` on `hg_replica`; `SELECT` on `system.parts` and `system.tables`. It never names `hg_safe`, `hg_unsafe`, `hg_promote` or `hg_member_unsafe`, and makes no RPC: no consensus format, no Raft-reachable call (contract §20.1).
- **State directory.** The journal is written atomically after each change (temp file, `Sync`, rename, directory `Sync`: the `arbiter-core:snode/state.go:674-721` pattern, `persistLocked` and `persistStateLocked` at `cfd4f42`; `:583-635` at `8f0bc43`); `New` reads it, refuses one of another node, and needs `StateDir` to exist (Task 34 creates it and holds `LOCK`). The journal keeps the entry of a copy the copyset dropped and ignores it (`Tables`, `Stats` and `ownerCurrent` read only entries that match a ready copy's incarnation and name), so `copyset.Deps.Dropped` needs nothing from the installer; a later incarnation's copy starts a fresh entry under the same key unless the key is quarantined.
- **CI.** The ClickHouse-gated tests join the existing `integration-clickhouse` job (ClickHouse 25.8 and, from Plan S3-A Task 4, `CH_USER` / `CH_PASSWORD` through `chtest.Open`); each test works in its own databases `t32_<8 hex>_replica`, `_rstage` and `_owner` (the owner database stands in for the owner's `hg_safe`, so the scripted sources pull with a local `INSERT … SELECT … WHERE _part`), so they share the server with the other targets safely. The restart test restarts its server, so it runs only in Plan S3-A's runner, against node B, after the SNode restart test and gated on its own `--- PASS:` line: in CI's `clickhouse-mechanics` job and Cut Release's `validate ClickHouse mechanics` step on `26.3.37.3`. Steps 13 and 14 run all of them locally on both versions.
- **No PR here.** Tasks 29–34 share the branch `urwt/claude/multi-source-s3c2`; Task 34 opens the one PR and releases `CORE_TAG_P2`. This task records nothing in the ledger.
- **Commit identity (user rule).** Task 29 Step 1 gave the worktree its own identity `poetry <chen@sentio.xyz>` (the global `uranuswch@gmail.com` must never author or co-author a commit: GitHub would add it as a co-author of the squash merge); Step 1 checks it before anything is written, every commit block prints the new commit's author, and Step 18 checks every commit of the branch. package install

```go
import (

const testNetwork = "s3c2-install-test"

// requireCH opens CH_ADDR (default 127.0.0.1:9000) through chtest once
// ARBITER_CH_INTEGRATION=1 is set, as the other ClickHouse-gated packages do.
func requireCH(t *testing.T) clickhouse.Conn {
	t.Helper()
	if os.Getenv("ARBITER_CH_INTEGRATION") != "1" {
		t.Skip("set ARBITER_CH_INTEGRATION=1 (and run ClickHouse on CH_ADDR or 127.0.0.1:9000) to run")
	}
	addr := os.Getenv("CH_ADDR")
	if addr == "" {
		addr = "127.0.0.1:9000"
	}
	return chtest.Open(t, addr)
}

// recordingConn records every statement the installer executes and fails the
// test on a replacing partition statement, an OPTIMIZE, a TRUNCATE or a
// SYSTEM statement, none of which the installer may issue.
type recordingConn struct {
	clickhouse.Conn
	t     *testing.T
	mu    sync.Mutex
	execs []string
}

func (c *recordingConn) Exec(ctx context.Context, query string, args ...any) error {
	c.mu.Lock()
	c.execs = append(c.execs, query)
	c.mu.Unlock()
	upper := strings.ToUpper(strings.TrimSpace(query))
	if strings.Contains(upper, "REPLACE PARTITION") || strings.HasPrefix(upper, "OPTIMIZE") || strings.HasPrefix(upper, "TRUNCATE") || strings.HasPrefix(upper, "SYSTEM") {
		c.t.Errorf("the installer issued a statement it never may: %s", query)
	}
	return c.Conn.Exec(ctx, query, args...)
}

// alters returns, in order, the ALTER TABLE statements since the last reset.
func (c *recordingConn) alters() []string {
	c.mu.Lock()
	defer c.mu.Unlock()
	var out []string
	for _, q := range c.execs {
		if strings.HasPrefix(q, "ALTER TABLE") {
			out = append(out, q)
		}
	}
	return out
}

func (c *recordingConn) reset() {
	c.mu.Lock()
	c.execs = nil
	c.mu.Unlock()
}

// fakeCopies is a fixed copy set.
type fakeCopies struct {
	mu   sync.Mutex
	list []copyset.Copy
}

func (f *fakeCopies) Copies() []copyset.Copy {
	f.mu.Lock()
	defer f.mu.Unlock()
	return slices.Clone(f.list)
}

func (f *fakeCopies) Copy(tableKey string) (copyset.Copy, bool) {
	f.mu.Lock()
	defer f.mu.Unlock()
	for _, c := range f.list {
		if c.TableKey == tableKey {
			return c, true
		}
	}
	return copyset.Copy{}, false
}

// row is one row of a test table: its partition (column day) and value.
type row struct {
	day string
	v   uint64
}

// fixture is one member ClickHouse with an owner database standing in for
// the owners' hg_safe, a copy set, sources per owner, a clock and a state
// directory that survives a member restart (newInstaller again).
type fixture struct {
	t        *testing.T
	raw      clickhouse.Conn
	conn     *recordingConn
	pinned   ddl.MemberPinned
	ownerDB  string
	stateDir string
	copies   *fakeCopies

	mu      sync.Mutex
	now     time.Time
	sources map[uint64][]sources.Source
}

func newFixture(t *testing.T, raw clickhouse.Conn) *fixture {
	t.Helper()
	var b [4]byte
	if _, err := rand.Read(b[:]); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	prefix := "t32_" + hex.EncodeToString(b[:])
	f := &fixture{
		t: t, raw: raw, conn: &recordingConn{Conn: raw, t: t},
		pinned:   ddl.MemberPinned{MemberUnsafeDB: prefix + "_munsafe", ReplicaDB: prefix + "_replica", StageDB: prefix + "_rstage", NodeID: "member-a"},
		ownerDB:  prefix + "_owner",
		stateDir: t.TempDir(),
		copies:   &fakeCopies{},
		now:      time.Date(2026, 10, 15, 12, 0, 0, 0, time.UTC),
		sources:  map[uint64][]sources.Source{},
	}
	ctx := context.Background()
	if err := ddl.EnsureMemberDatabases(ctx, raw, f.pinned); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	f.exec("CREATE DATABASE IF NOT EXISTS " + quoteIdent(f.ownerDB))
	t.Cleanup(func() {
		for _, db := range []string{f.pinned.ReplicaDB, f.pinned.StageDB, f.ownerDB} {
			_ = raw.Exec(context.Background(), "DROP DATABASE IF EXISTS "+quoteIdent(db)+" SYNC")
		}
	})
	return f
}

func (f *fixture) exec(query string) {
	f.t.Helper()
	if err := f.raw.Exec(context.Background(), query); err != nil {
		f.t.Fatalf("%s: %v", query, err)
	}
}

func (f *fixture) clock() time.Time {
	f.mu.Lock()
	defer f.mu.Unlock()
	return f.now
}

func (f *fixture) advance(d time.Duration) {
	f.mu.Lock()
	f.now = f.now.Add(d)
	f.mu.Unlock()
}

// tableManifest describes what the owner's table holds now.
func (f *fixture) tableManifest(c copyset.Copy) replay.TableManifest {
	f.t.Helper()

	table := ddl.CHTableName(c.TableKey)
	parts, err := chparts.ActiveParts(ctx, f.raw, f.ownerDB, table)
	if err != nil {
		f.t.Fatal(err)
	}
	scans, err := chexec.ScanAllParts(ctx, f.raw, f.ownerDB+"."+table, c.Schema)
	if err != nil {
		f.t.Fatal(err)
	}
	hashOf := map[string]chexec.PartScanResult{}
	for _, s := range scans {
		hashOf[s.PartName] = s
	}
	tm := replay.TableManifest{TableID: c.TableKey, SchemaHash: payloadexec.TableSchemaHash(testNetwork, c.Schema)}
	byPartition := map[string][]string{}
	for _, p := range parts {
		id := chparts.LogicalPartitionID(c.Schema, p)
		s := hashOf[p.Name]
		tm.ActiveParts = append(tm.ActiveParts, replay.PartManifestEntry{
			TableID: c.TableKey, PartitionID: id, PartName: p.Name, PartPhysHash: p.PhysHash, PartRowLtHash: s.RowLtHash, RowCount: s.RowCount, Bytes: p.Bytes,
		})
		byPartition[id] = append(byPartition[id], s.RowLtHash)
	}
	for _, id := range slices.Sorted(maps.Keys(byPartition)) {
		root, err := payloadexec.SumPartRowLtHashes(byPartition[id])
		if err != nil {
			f.t.Fatal(err)
		}
		tm.PartitionRoots = append(tm.PartitionRoots, replay.PartitionCommitment{TableID: c.TableKey, PartitionID: id, Root: root})
	}
	return tm
}

// pullTo copies the owner's part with need's hash_of_all_files into scratch
// times times, each in its own INSERT; zero copies nothing.
func (f *fixture) pullTo(ctx context.Context, need sources.Need, scratch sources.Scratch, times int) sources.Result {
	var name string
	q := "SELECT name FROM system.parts WHERE database = ? AND table = ? AND active AND hash_of_all_files = ?"
	if err := f.raw.QueryRow(ctx, q, f.ownerDB, need.Table, need.PartPhysHash).Scan(&name); err != nil {
		return sources.Result{Outcome: sources.OutcomeMissed}
	}
	for range times {
		insert := fmt.Sprintf("INSERT INTO %s SELECT * FROM %s WHERE _part = %s", qualified(scratch.Database, scratch.Table), qualified(f.ownerDB, need.Table), quoteLiteral(name))
		settings := clickhouse.Settings{"min_insert_block_size_rows": max(need.RowCount, 1), "min_insert_block_size_bytes": 0, "max_threads": 1, "max_insert_threads": 1}
		if err := f.raw.Exec(clickhouse.Context(ctx, clickhouse.WithSettings(settings)), insert); err != nil {
			return sources.Result{Outcome: sources.OutcomeRefused, Err: err}
		}
	}
	return sources.Result{Outcome: sources.OutcomeFetched}
}

// splitTo copies the owner's part row by row, one INSERT per row.
func (f *fixture) splitTo(ctx context.Context, need sources.Need, scratch sources.Scratch) sources.Result {
	q := fmt.Sprintf("SELECT toString(%s), day, v FROM %s WHERE _part IN (SELECT name FROM system.parts WHERE database = ? AND table = ? AND active AND hash_of_all_files = ?)",
		quoteIdent(ddl.RowIDColumn), qualified(f.ownerDB, need.Table))
	rows, err := f.raw.Query(ctx, q, f.ownerDB, need.Table, need.PartPhysHash)
	if err != nil {
		return sources.Result{Outcome: sources.OutcomeRefused, Err: err}
	}
	var all []row
	for rows.Next() {
		var id string
		var r row
		if err := rows.Scan(&id, &r.day, &r.v); err != nil {
			rows.Close()
			return sources.Result{Outcome: sources.OutcomeRefused, Err: err}
		}
		all = append(all, r)
	}
	rows.Close()
	for _, r := range all {
		f.insertInto(scratch.Database, scratch.Table, r)
	}
	return sources.Result{Outcome: sources.OutcomeFetched}
}

// fetchFunc is one scripted Fetch.
type fetchFunc func(ctx context.Context, need sources.Need, scratch sources.Scratch) sources.Result

// scripted is a source whose n-th Fetch runs steps[n] (the last step once
// they run out) and that records the parts it was asked for.
type scripted struct {
	name  string
	mu    sync.Mutex
	steps []fetchFunc
	asked []string
}

func (s *scripted) Name() string { return s.name }

func (s *scripted) Fetch(ctx context.Context, need sources.Need, _ payloadexec.TableSchema, scratch sources.Scratch) sources.Result {
	s.mu.Lock()
	n := len(s.asked)
	s.asked = append(s.asked, need.PartName)
	step := s.steps[min(n, len(s.steps)-1)]
	s.mu.Unlock()
	res := step(ctx, need, scratch)
	res.Source = s.name
	return res
}

func (s *scripted) calls() int {
	s.mu.Lock()
	defer s.mu.Unlock()
	return len(s.asked)
}

func (f *fixture) pull(times int) fetchFunc {
	return func(ctx context.Context, need sources.Need, scratch sources.Scratch) sources.Result {
		return f.pullTo(ctx, need, scratch, times)
	}
}

func (f *fixture) split() fetchFunc {
	return func(ctx context.Context, need sources.Need, scratch sources.Scratch) sources.Result {
		return f.splitTo(ctx, need, scratch)
	}
}

// foreign writes a row the manifest does not list into the scratch.
func (f *fixture) foreign(r row) fetchFunc {
	return func(ctx context.Context, need sources.Need, scratch sources.Scratch) sources.Result {
		f.insertInto(scratch.Database, scratch.Table, r)
		return sources.Result{Outcome: sources.OutcomeFetched}
	}
}

// restoreWithExtra is a restore whose backup is ahead of publication: the
// needed part and one more part.
func (f *fixture) restoreWithExtra(extra row) fetchFunc {
	return func(ctx context.Context, need sources.Need, scratch sources.Scratch) sources.Result {
		res := f.pullTo(ctx, need, scratch, 1)
		f.insertInto(scratch.Database, scratch.Table, extra)
		return res
	}
}

func outcome(o sources.Outcome, err error) fetchFunc {
	return func(context.Context, sources.Need, sources.Scratch) sources.Result {
		return sources.Result{Outcome: o, Err: err}
	}
}

var errMemoryLimit = errors.New("code: 241, message: (total) memory limit exceeded")

func (f *fixture) source(name string, steps ...fetchFunc) *scripted {
	return &scripted{name: name, steps: steps}
}

func requireRefusal(t *testing.T, err error, kind error, text string) {
	t.Helper()
	if !errors.Is(err, kind) {
		t.Fatalf("err = %v, want one wrapping %v", err, kind)
	}
	if !strings.Contains(err.Error(), text) {
		t.Fatalf("err = %q, want it to contain %q", err, text)
	}
}
```

```go
		t.Fatalf("foreign outcomes = %d, want 1", s.Outcomes[OutcomeForeign])
	}
	requireRefusal(t, inst.Apply(context.Background(), s1), ErrForeign, "clear it offline with sentio-node si-member clear-foreign --table dex.swaps")
	if bad.calls() != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("the source ran %d times, want 1: a quarantined table fetches nothing", bad.calls())
	}
	inst = f.newInstaller(nil)
	f.start(inst)
	if left := f.stageTables(); !slices.Equal(left, []string{tj.ForeignScratch}) {
		t.Fatalf("stage tables after a restart = %v, want the kept scratch %s", left, tj.ForeignScratch)
	}
	if err := ClearForeign(f.stateDir, "dex.swaps"); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	f.setSources(0, f.source("owner_pull", f.pull(1)))
	inst = f.newInstaller(nil)
	f.start(inst)
	if left := f.stageTables(); len(left) != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("stage tables after clear-foreign and a restart = %v, want none", left)
	}
	f.mustApply(inst, s1)
	f.requireCopyEqualsManifest(c, s1)
}

// TestInstallRenameRaceRetriesOnceFromACleanScratch: a pull that finds no rows
// is retried once from a clean scratch; a second empty pull moves to the next
// source (spec §8.5 step 4).
func TestInstallRenameRaceRetriesOnceFromACleanScratch(t *testing.T) {
	f := newFixture(t, requireCH(t))
	c := f.table(0, "dex.swaps", 3, false)
	empty := outcome(sources.OutcomeFetched, nil)
	first := f.source("owner_pull", empty, f.pull(1))
	f.setSources(0, first)
	inst := f.newInstaller(nil)
	f.start(inst)
	f.promote(c, row{"", 1})
	s1 := f.update("s1", 10, c)
	f.mustApply(inst, s1)
	f.requireCopyEqualsManifest(c, s1)
	if first.calls() != 2 {
		t.Fatalf("owner pull ran %d times, want 2 (one retry)", first.calls())
	}
	if s := inst.Stats(); s.Outcomes[OutcomeRenameRace] != 1 || s.Outcomes[OutcomeKept] != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("outcomes = %v, want one rename_race and one kept", s.Outcomes)
	}

	f.promote(c, row{"", 2})
	s2 := f.update("s2", 11, c)
	again := f.source("owner_pull", empty)
	next := f.source("peer_unsafe_pull", f.pull(1))
	f.setSources(0, again, next)
	f.mustApply(inst, s2)
	f.requireCopyEqualsManifest(c, s2)
	if again.calls() != 2 || next.calls() != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("calls = %d and %d, want 2 (one retry) then 1", again.calls(), next.calls())
	}
	if s := inst.Stats(); s.Installs["peer_unsafe_pull"] != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("installs = %v, want one from peer_unsafe_pull", s.Installs)
	}
}

// TestInstallSplitFallsBackToTheNextSource: a pull that arrives as parts
// summing to the needed part is not retried; the next source delivers it.
func TestInstallSplitFallsBackToTheNextSource(t *testing.T) {
	f := newFixture(t, requireCH(t))
	c := f.table(0, "dex.swaps", 3, false)
	splitting := f.source("owner_pull", f.split())
	next := f.source("peer_unsafe_pull", f.pull(1))
	f.setSources(0, splitting, next)
	inst := f.newInstaller(nil)
	f.start(inst)
	f.promote(c, row{"", 1}, row{"", 2})
	s1 := f.update("s1", 10, c)
	f.mustApply(inst, s1)
	f.requireCopyEqualsManifest(c, s1)
	if splitting.calls() != 1 || next.calls() != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("calls = %d and %d, want 1 and 1", splitting.calls(), next.calls())
	}
	if s := inst.Stats(); s.Outcomes[OutcomeSplit] != 1 || s.Installs["peer_unsafe_pull"] != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("stats = %+v, want one split and one peer_unsafe_pull install", s)
	}
	if parts := f.copyParts(c); len(parts) != 1 || parts[0].Rows != 2 {
		t.Fatalf("copy parts = %+v, want one part of 2 rows", parts)
	}
}
```
