```go
// TestInstallRefusedPullFallsBackToRestoreAndDefers: a pull refused by the
// memory limit is not retried and the restore delivers the part, dropping
// the backup's extra part inside the scratch; a part no source delivers is
// deferred from 1m doubling, and no source runs before the deadline (K35).
func TestInstallRefusedPullFallsBackToRestoreAndDefers(t *testing.T) {
	f := newFixture(t, requireCH(t))
	c := f.table(0, "dex.swaps", 3, false)
	refused := f.source("owner_pull", outcome(sources.OutcomeRefused, errMemoryLimit))
	restore := f.source("restore", f.restoreWithExtra(row{"", 55}))
	f.setSources(0, refused, restore)
	inst := f.newInstaller(nil)
	f.start(inst)
	// The owner is journaled first (its table empty at s0), so s1 is no
	// bootstrap and the sources run in the P2 order; the bootstrap's restore
	// probe is TestInstallBootstrapProbesTheRestoreOncePerCopy's.
	f.mustApply(inst, f.update("s0", 9, c))
	f.promote(c, row{"", 1})
	s1 := f.update("s1", 10, c)
	f.conn.reset()
	f.mustApply(inst, s1)
	f.requireCopyEqualsManifest(c, s1)
	if refused.calls() != 1 || restore.calls() != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("calls = %d and %d, want 1 and 1", refused.calls(), restore.calls())
	}
	dropped := 0
	for _, q := range f.conn.alters() {
		if strings.HasPrefix(q, "ALTER TABLE `"+f.pinned.StageDB+"`.`member-a_") && strings.Contains(q, " DROP PART '") {
			dropped++
		}
	}
	if dropped != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("scratch DROP PART statements = %d, want 1 for the backup's extra part (%q)", dropped, f.conn.alters())
	}
	if s := inst.Stats(); s.Outcomes[OutcomeRefused] != 1 || s.Installs["restore"] != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("stats = %+v, want one refused and one restore install", s)
	}

	f.promote(c, row{"", 2})
	s2 := f.update("s2", 11, c)
	missed := f.source("restore", outcome(sources.OutcomeMissed, nil))
	f.setSources(0, refused, missed)
	t0 := f.clock()
	err := inst.Apply(context.Background(), s2)
	requireRefusal(t, err, ErrNoSourceSucceeded, "of dex.swaps ([owner_pull: refused (code: 241, message: (total) memory limit exceeded) restore: missed]); deferred until "+t0.Add(time.Minute).Format(time.RFC3339))
	requireRefusal(t, inst.Apply(context.Background(), s2), ErrNoSourceSucceeded, "deferred until "+t0.Add(time.Minute).Format(time.RFC3339))
	if refused.calls() != 2 || missed.calls() != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("calls = %d and %d, want 2 and 1: no source runs before the deadline", refused.calls(), missed.calls())
	}
	f.advance(61 * time.Second)
	requireRefusal(t, inst.Apply(context.Background(), s2), ErrNoSourceSucceeded, "deferred until "+t0.Add(61*time.Second+2*time.Minute).Format(time.RFC3339))
	if refused.calls() != 3 {
		t.Fatalf("owner pull ran %d times, want 3 after the deadline", refused.calls())
	}
	if j, _ := inst.Entry(0); j.SnapshotID != "s1" {
		t.Fatalf("Entry(0) = %s, want s1 while the part is deferred", j.SnapshotID)
	}
}

// TestInstallBootstrapProbesTheRestoreOncePerCopy (housegate spec 2026-10-14
// §8.6, the P1 backups are the bootstrap source; Plan S3-C2 review fix 245-4):
// while an owner has no journaled entry, the first part each of its copies
// fetches tries the restore before the owner pull, once per copy and process;
// every other part, and every part of a journaled owner, keeps the P2 order. A
// probe that misses costs that attempt, and a pass that fails after it does not
// probe again when it runs anew.
func TestInstallBootstrapProbesTheRestoreOncePerCopy(t *testing.T) {
	f := newFixture(t, requireCH(t))
	pools := f.table(0, "dex.pools", 4, false)
	swaps := f.table(0, "dex.swaps", 3, false)
	pull := f.source("owner_pull", f.pull(1))
	restore := f.source("restore", f.pull(1))
	f.setSources(0, pull, restore)
	inst := f.newInstaller(nil)
	f.start(inst)
	f.promote(pools, row{"", 1})
	f.promote(swaps, row{"", 2})
	f.promote(swaps, row{"", 3})
	s1 := f.update("s1", 10, pools, swaps)
	f.mustApply(inst, s1)
	f.requireCopyEqualsManifest(pools, s1)
	f.requireCopyEqualsManifest(swaps, s1)
	if restore.calls() != 2 || pull.calls() != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("calls: restore %d, owner pull %d; want 2 and 1 (each copy's first part from the restore, the rest by owner pull)", restore.calls(), pull.calls())
	}
	if s := inst.Stats(); s.Installs["restore"] != 2 || s.Installs["owner_pull"] != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("installs = %v, want 2 from the restore and 1 by owner pull", s.Installs)
	}

	// The owner is journaled now: its next part keeps the P2 order.
	f.promote(swaps, row{"", 4})
	s2 := f.update("s2", 11, pools, swaps)
	f.mustApply(inst, s2)
	f.requireCopyEqualsManifest(swaps, s2)
	if restore.calls() != 2 || pull.calls() != 2 {
		t.Fatalf("calls after s2: restore %d, owner pull %d; want 2 and 2", restore.calls(), pull.calls())
	}

	// Owner 2's backups hold nothing and its owner pull misses once: the
	// probe costs one restore attempt, the pass fails and defers the part,
	// and its next run takes both parts by owner pull without probing again.
	mints := f.table(2, "nft.mints", 5, false)
	pull2 := f.source("owner_pull", outcome(sources.OutcomeMissed, nil), f.pull(1))
	restore2 := f.source("restore", outcome(sources.OutcomeMissed, nil))
	f.setSources(2, pull2, restore2)
	f.promote(mints, row{"", 5})
	f.promote(mints, row{"", 6})
	s3 := f.update("s3", 12, pools, swaps, mints)
	requireRefusal(t, inst.Apply(context.Background(), s3), ErrNoSourceSucceeded, "of nft.mints ([restore: missed owner_pull: missed])")
	f.advance(61 * time.Second)
	f.mustApply(inst, s3)
	f.requireCopyEqualsManifest(mints, s3)
	if restore2.calls() != 1 || pull2.calls() != 3 {
		t.Fatalf("owner 2 calls: restore %d, owner pull %d; want 1 and 3", restore2.calls(), pull2.calls())
	}
	if s := inst.Stats(); s.Installs["restore"] != 2 || s.Installs["owner_pull"] != 4 {
		t.Fatalf("installs = %v, want 2 from the restore and 4 by owner pull", s.Installs)
	}
}

// TestInstallJournalsTheEntryPerOwner: each owner's entry advances on its
// own, and an owner advances only when every copy of it closes, in one
// journal write with the copies' parts (spec §8.5 step 7).
func TestInstallJournalsTheEntryPerOwner(t *testing.T) {
	f := newFixture(t, requireCH(t))
	swaps := f.table(0, "dex.swaps", 3, false)
	mints := f.table(2, "nft.mints", 4, false)
	owners := f.table(2, "nft.owners", 5, false)
	f.setSources(0, f.source("owner_pull", f.pull(1)))
	f.setSources(2, f.source("owner_pull", f.pull(1)))
	inst := f.newInstaller(nil)
	f.start(inst)
	f.promote(swaps, row{"", 1})
	f.promote(mints, row{"", 2})
	f.promote(owners, row{"", 3})
	u := f.update("s1", 10, swaps, mints, owners)
	u.Entries[2] = frontier(2, 7)

	f.setSources(2, f.source("owner_pull", func(ctx context.Context, need sources.Need, scratch sources.Scratch) sources.Result {
		if need.TableKey == "nft.owners" {
			return sources.Result{Outcome: sources.OutcomeMissed}
		}
		return f.pullTo(ctx, need, scratch, 1)
	}))
	requireRefusal(t, inst.Apply(context.Background(), u), ErrNoSourceSucceeded, "of nft.owners")
	if j, ok := inst.Entry(0); !ok || j.SnapshotID != "s1" || j.Entry != frontier(0, 10) {
		t.Fatalf("Entry(0) = %+v %v, want s1 at 10", j, ok)
	}
	if _, ok := inst.Entry(2); ok {
		t.Fatal("owner 2 has an entry although nft.owners did not close")
	}
	if got := f.copyHashes(mints); len(got) != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("nft.mints holds %d parts, want none: an owner's copies move together", len(got))
	}

	b, err := os.ReadFile(filepath.Join(f.stateDir, JournalFile))
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	var raw map[string]any
	if err := json.Unmarshal(b, &raw); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	owner0 := raw["owners"].(map[string]any)["0"].(map[string]any)
	if raw["version"] != float64(1) || raw["node_id"] != "member-a" || owner0["snapshot_id"] != "s1" {
		t.Fatalf("journal file = %s", b)
	}
	entry := owner0["entry"].(map[string]any)
	part := owner0["tables"].(map[string]any)["dex.swaps"].(map[string]any)["parts"].([]any)[0].(map[string]any)
	for _, k := range []string{"indexer_id", "safe_block_seq", "applied_promotion_seq"} {
		if _, ok := entry[k]; !ok {
			t.Fatalf("journal entry lacks %s: %s", k, b)
		}
	}
	for _, k := range []string{"name", "partition_id", "part_row_lthash", "hash_of_all_files", "rows"} {
		if _, ok := part[k]; !ok {
			t.Fatalf("journal part lacks %s: %s", k, b)
		}
	}

	f.setSources(2, f.source("owner_pull", f.pull(1)))
	f.advance(time.Minute)
	f.mustApply(inst, u)
	if j, ok := inst.Entry(2); !ok || j.SnapshotID != "s1" || j.Entry != frontier(2, 7) || len(j.Tables) != 2 {
		t.Fatalf("Entry(2) = %+v %v, want s1 at 7 with both tables", j, ok)
	}
	f.requireCopyEqualsManifest(mints, u)
	f.requireCopyEqualsManifest(owners, u)
	reopened := f.newInstaller(nil)
	if j, _ := reopened.Entry(2); j.SnapshotID != "s1" {
		t.Fatalf("the reopened journal has owner 2 at %q", j.SnapshotID)
	}
}

// TestApplyNeverTakesAnOwnerBackAfterAPartialPass (Plan S3-C2 review fix 245-5):
// owners 0 and 2 are at s1, and a self-audit finds a journaled part of owner 2's
// copy gone. s2 advances owner 0's entry with a new part; its pass commits and
// journals owner 0 while owner 2's repair finds no source, so Apply fails. A
// copy-watch tick that re-applied s1, the last update that had succeeded, would
// rebuild owner 0's partition back to s1 and take its journal back; Apply skips
// an owner whose journaled entry is ahead of the update, so owner 0 keeps s2's
// entry and parts and no statement touches its copy. The tick the role makes
// now re-applies s2, the newest update the feed offered: owner 0 is current
// and owner 2 is repaired once its source answers.
func TestApplyNeverTakesAnOwnerBackAfterAPartialPass(t *testing.T) {
	ctx := context.Background()
	f := newFixture(t, requireCH(t))
	swaps := f.table(0, "dex.swaps", 3, false)
	mints := f.table(2, "nft.mints", 4, false)
	f.setSources(0, f.source("owner_pull", f.pull(1)))
	f.setSources(2, f.source("owner_pull", f.pull(1)))
	inst := f.newInstaller(nil)
	f.start(inst)
	f.promote(swaps, row{"", 1})
	f.promote(mints, row{"", 2})
	f.promote(mints, row{"", 3})
	s1 := f.update("s1", 10, swaps, mints)
	f.mustApply(inst, s1)

	f.exec("ALTER TABLE " + qualified(f.pinned.ReplicaDB, mints.Table) + " DROP PART '" + f.copyParts(mints)[0].Name + "'")
	if err := inst.Audit(ctx, TriggerSelfAudit); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("Audit(self_audit): %v", err)
	}
	f.promote(swaps, row{"", 4})
	s2 := f.update("s2", 12, swaps, mints)
	s2.Entries[2] = frontier(2, 10)
	f.setSources(2, f.source("owner_pull", outcome(sources.OutcomeUnreachable, nil)))
	requireRefusal(t, inst.Apply(ctx, s2), ErrNoSourceSucceeded, "of nft.mints")
	if j, _ := inst.Entry(0); j.SnapshotID != "s2" || j.Entry != frontier(0, 12) {
		t.Fatalf("Entry(0) = %s at %+v, want s2 at 12: owner 0's pass commits on its own", j.SnapshotID, j.Entry)
	}
	f.requireCopyEqualsManifest(swaps, s2)
	kept := partNames(f.copyParts(swaps))
	if !inst.NeedsPass() {
		t.Fatal("NeedsPass = false with owner 2's partition Diverged")
	}

	// The copy watch's tick before the fix: s1 again, owner 2 still unreachable.
	f.advance(time.Hour)
	f.conn.reset()
	requireRefusal(t, inst.Apply(ctx, s1), ErrNoSourceSucceeded, "of nft.mints")
	for _, q := range f.conn.alters() {
		if strings.Contains(q, "`"+swaps.Table+"`") {
			t.Fatalf("re-applying s1 changed owner 0's copy: %s", q)
		}
	}
	if j, _ := inst.Entry(0); j.SnapshotID != "s2" || j.Entry != frontier(0, 12) {
		t.Fatalf("Entry(0) = %s at %+v after s1 was offered again, want s2 at 12: a journal entry never goes back", j.SnapshotID, j.Entry)
	}
	if got := partNames(f.copyParts(swaps)); !slices.Equal(got, kept) {
		t.Fatalf("owner 0's copy holds %v after s1 was offered again, want s2's %v", got, kept)
	}
	f.requireCopyEqualsManifest(swaps, s2)

	// The copy watch's tick now: s2 again, owner 2's source answers.
	f.setSources(2, f.source("owner_pull", f.pull(1)))
	f.advance(time.Hour)
	f.conn.reset()
	f.mustApply(inst, s2)
	for _, q := range f.conn.alters() {
		if strings.Contains(q, "`"+swaps.Table+"`") {
			t.Fatalf("re-applying s2 changed owner 0's copy, which is at s2: %s", q)
		}
	}
	if got := partNames(f.copyParts(swaps)); !slices.Equal(got, kept) {
		t.Fatalf("owner 0's copy holds %v after s2 was offered again, want %v", got, kept)
	}
	f.requireCopyEqualsManifest(mints, s2)
	if j, _ := inst.Entry(2); j.SnapshotID != "s2" || j.Entry != frontier(2, 10) {
		t.Fatalf("Entry(2) = %s at %+v, want s2 at 10 after the repair", j.SnapshotID, j.Entry)
	}
	if inst.NeedsPass() || !inst.Stats().AuditClean {
		t.Fatalf("NeedsPass %v, AuditClean %v after the repair; want false and true", inst.NeedsPass(), inst.Stats().AuditClean)
	}
}

// TestInstallRecoversAPartAttachedBeforeTheJournalWrite: a member stopped
// between ATTACH and the journal write leaves an unjournaled part; after the
// restart the startup audit holds the copy unclean and the next pass adopts
// the part, because the target manifest still needs its row hash, without
// fetching it again (K36).
func TestInstallRecoversAPartAttachedBeforeTheJournalWrite(t *testing.T) {
	f := newFixture(t, requireCH(t))
	c := f.table(0, "dex.swaps", 3, false)
	src := f.source("owner_pull", f.pull(1))
	f.setSources(0, src)
	crash := errors.New("stopped after the attach")
	inst := f.newInstaller(func(_ *Config, d *Deps) {
		d.AfterAttach = func(string, string) error { return crash }
	})
	f.start(inst)
	f.promote(c, row{"", 1})
	s1 := f.update("s1", 10, c)
	if err := inst.Apply(context.Background(), s1); !errors.Is(err, crash) {
		t.Fatalf("Apply = %v, want the injected stop", err)
	}
	if got := f.copyHashes(c); len(got) != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("copy holds %d parts after the stop, want the attached one", len(got))
	}
	if j, ok := inst.Entry(0); ok && len(j.Tables["dex.swaps"].Parts) != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("the journal lists %v although the member stopped before writing it", j.Tables["dex.swaps"].Parts)
	}

	inst = f.newInstaller(nil)
	f.start(inst)
	if inst.Stats().AuditClean || !inst.Tables(0)[0].Diverged {
		t.Fatal("the startup audit is clean although the copy holds an unjournaled part")
	}
	f.mustApply(inst, s1)
	f.requireCopyEqualsManifest(c, s1)
	if src.calls() != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("the owner pull ran %d times, want 1: the attached part is adopted, not fetched again", src.calls())
	}
	j, _ := inst.Entry(0)
	parts := f.copyParts(c)
	if len(j.Tables["dex.swaps"].Parts) != 1 || j.Tables["dex.swaps"].Parts[0].Name != parts[0].Name {
		t.Fatalf("journal parts = %+v, copy parts = %+v", j.Tables["dex.swaps"].Parts, parts)
	}
	if !inst.Stats().AuditClean {
		t.Fatal("the copy is not clean after the adoption")
	}
}

// TestInstallsPauseAboveTheDiskBudget: at or above the configured
// stop_installs_ratio of the disk budget, summed over every part of ReplicaDB
// and StageDB, Apply attaches nothing while audits continue (K35). The ratio is
// devnet2's 0.5 (decision D28), with the use exactly at the threshold; the same
// budget at the default 0.8 is not reached, and the pass installs.
func TestInstallsPauseAboveTheDiskBudget(t *testing.T) {
	f := newFixture(t, requireCH(t))
	c := f.table(0, "dex.swaps", 3, false)
	f.setSources(0, f.source("owner_pull", f.pull(1)))
	f.exec("CREATE TABLE " + qualified(f.pinned.StageDB, "member-b_0123abcd_1") + " (x UInt64) ENGINE = MergeTree ORDER BY x")
	f.exec("INSERT INTO " + qualified(f.pinned.StageDB, "member-b_0123abcd_1") + " VALUES (1)")
	var used uint64
	query := "SELECT sum(bytes_on_disk) FROM system.parts WHERE database IN (" + quoteLiteral(f.pinned.ReplicaDB) + ", " + quoteLiteral(f.pinned.StageDB) + ")"
	if err := f.raw.QueryRow(context.Background(), query).Scan(&used); err != nil || used == 0 {
		t.Fatalf("member disk use = %d (%v), want the other node's scratch part", used, err)
	}
	budget := 2 * used
	inst := f.newInstaller(func(cfg *Config, _ *Deps) { cfg.DiskBudgetBytes, cfg.StopInstallsRatio = budget, 0.5 })
	f.start(inst)
	f.promote(c, row{"", 1})
	s1 := f.update("s1", 10, c)
	f.conn.reset()
	err := inst.Apply(context.Background(), s1)
	requireRefusal(t, err, ErrInstallsPaused, fmt.Sprintf("install: member disk budget exceeded (%d of %d bytes); installs paused", used, budget))
	if alters := f.conn.alters(); len(alters) != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("ALTER statements while paused = %q", alters)
	}
	s := inst.Stats()
	if !s.InstallsPaused || s.DiskUsedBytes != used || s.DiskBudgetBytes != budget {
		t.Fatalf("stats = %+v, want installs paused at %d of %d bytes", s, used, budget)
	}
	if err := inst.Audit(context.Background(), TriggerStartup); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("an audit while installs are paused: %v", err)
	}
	inst = f.newInstaller(func(cfg *Config, _ *Deps) { cfg.DiskBudgetBytes = budget })
	f.start(inst)
	f.mustApply(inst, s1)
	f.requireCopyEqualsManifest(c, s1)
	if s := inst.Stats(); s.InstallsPaused || s.DiskUsedBytes != used {
		t.Fatalf("stats = %+v, want installs running at %d of %d bytes under the default ratio", s, used, budget)
	}
}
```

```go
// TestAStartWithACurrentJournalAuditsTheCopiesItFindsLater (Plan S3-C2 review
// fix 245-1): the member restarts with its journal at the watermark, and its
// copyset makes the copies ready only after the startup audit ran: one copy was
// lost and its first pass created it again empty, the other lost a journaled
// part. The audit covered neither, so the audit is unclean, both copies report
// Diverged and NeedsPass holds until Apply of the very manifest the journal is
// at audits them and rebuilds what they lost.
func TestAStartWithACurrentJournalAuditsTheCopiesItFindsLater(t *testing.T) {
	f := newFixture(t, requireCH(t))
	lost := f.table(0, "dex.swaps", 3, false)
	altered := f.table(0, "dex.pools", 4, false)
	f.setSources(0, f.source("owner_pull", f.pull(1)))
	inst := f.newInstaller(nil)
	f.start(inst)
	f.promote(lost, row{"", 1})
	f.promote(altered, row{"", 2})
	f.promote(altered, row{"", 3})
	s1 := f.update("s1", 10, lost, altered)
	f.mustApply(inst, s1)

	// While the member is down: one copy is gone (the copyset's first pass
	// creates it again, empty), the other loses a journaled part.
	f.exec("DROP TABLE " + qualified(f.pinned.ReplicaDB, lost.Table) + " SYNC")
	if err := ddl.EnsureCopy(context.Background(), f.raw, f.pinned, lost.Schema, lost.IncarnationSeq); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	f.exec("ALTER TABLE " + qualified(f.pinned.ReplicaDB, altered.Table) + " DROP PART '" + f.copyParts(altered)[0].Name + "'")

	// The new process audits while its copyset reports no ready copy yet.
	ready := f.copies.Copies()
	f.copies.mu.Lock()
	f.copies.list = nil
	f.copies.mu.Unlock()
	inst = f.newInstaller(nil)
	f.start(inst)
	if !inst.Stats().AuditClean {
		t.Fatalf("stats = %+v, want a clean audit while no copy is ready", inst.Stats())
	}
	f.copies.mu.Lock()
	f.copies.list = ready
	f.copies.mu.Unlock()
	if inst.Stats().AuditClean || !inst.NeedsPass() {
		t.Fatalf("AuditClean %v, NeedsPass %v with ready copies the audit never covered; want false and true", inst.Stats().AuditClean, inst.NeedsPass())
	}
	for _, st := range inst.Tables(0) {
		if !st.Diverged || st.SnapshotID != "s1" {
			t.Fatalf("Tables(0) = %+v, want every copy Diverged at s1 until it is audited", inst.Tables(0))
		}
	}
	f.mustApply(inst, s1)
	f.requireCopyEqualsManifest(lost, s1)
	f.requireCopyEqualsManifest(altered, s1)
	if s := inst.Stats(); !s.AuditClean || s.AuditRuns[TriggerStartup] != 1 || inst.NeedsPass() {
		t.Fatalf("stats = %+v, NeedsPass %v; want clean after the pass, one startup run and nothing left", s, inst.NeedsPass())
	}
}

// journal at the manifest and the copy set unchanged, a self-audit and then a

// uptimeConn answers chrestart's uptime probe from a start time the test
// moves; every other call reaches ClickHouse.
type uptimeConn struct {
	clickhouse.Conn
	started atomic.Int64 // unix nanoseconds
}

func (c *uptimeConn) QueryRow(ctx context.Context, query string, args ...any) driver.Row {
	if query == "SELECT toUInt64(uptime())" {
		return uptimeRow{uptime: uint64(time.Since(time.Unix(0, c.started.Load())) / time.Second)}
	}
	return c.Conn.QueryRow(ctx, query, args...)
}

type uptimeRow struct{ uptime uint64 }

func (r uptimeRow) Err() error { return nil }

func (r uptimeRow) Scan(dest ...any) error {
	*dest[0].(*uint64) = r.uptime
	return nil
}

func (r uptimeRow) ScanStruct(any) error { return nil }

// TestAuditRerunsWhenClickHouseUptimeRegresses: when the server's start time
// moves later (its uptime regressed), the watcher reruns the audit as
// clickhouse_restart; it finds what the restart changed, holds the audit
// unclean until the next pass repairs it, and Apply waits for a restart audit
// that failed.
func TestAuditRerunsWhenClickHouseUptimeRegresses(t *testing.T) {
	f := newFixture(t, requireCH(t))
	c := f.table(0, "dex.swaps", 3, false)
	f.setSources(0, f.source("owner_pull", f.pull(1)))
	inst := f.newInstaller(nil)
	f.start(inst)
	f.promote(c, row{"", 1})
	f.promote(c, row{"", 2})
	s1 := f.update("s1", 10, c)
	f.mustApply(inst, s1)

	probe := &uptimeConn{Conn: f.raw}
	probe.started.Store(time.Now().Add(-time.Hour).UnixNano())
	var mu sync.Mutex
	var audits []error
	done := make(chan struct{}, 1)
	w := &chrestart.Watcher{Interval: 50 * time.Millisecond, OnRestart: func(ctx context.Context, previous, current time.Time) {
		err := inst.Audit(ctx, TriggerClickHouseRestart)
		mu.Lock()
		audits = append(audits, err)
		mu.Unlock()
		done <- struct{}{}
	}}
	ctx, cancel := context.WithCancel(context.Background())
	stopped := make(chan struct{})
	go func() { defer close(stopped); w.Run(ctx, probe) }()
	defer func() { cancel(); <-stopped }()

	time.Sleep(200 * time.Millisecond)
	f.exec("ALTER TABLE " + qualified(f.pinned.ReplicaDB, c.Table) + " DROP PART '" + f.copyParts(c)[0].Name + "'")
	probe.started.Store(time.Now().UnixNano())
	select {
	case <-done:
	case <-time.After(30 * time.Second):
		t.Fatal("no audit ran after the start time moved")
	}
	mu.Lock()
	if len(audits) != 1 || audits[0] != nil {
		t.Fatalf("restart audits = %v, want one that succeeded", audits)
	}
	mu.Unlock()
	s := inst.Stats()
	if s.AuditRuns[TriggerClickHouseRestart] != 1 || s.AuditClean || s.DivergedPartitions[0] != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("stats = %+v, want one clickhouse_restart run, unclean, one Diverged partition", s)
	}
	f.mustApply(inst, s1)
	f.requireCopyEqualsManifest(c, s1)
	if !inst.Stats().AuditClean {
		t.Fatal("the audit is not clean after the repair")
	}

	// A restart audit that cannot complete leaves installs waiting for it:
	// Apply runs it again first.
	cancelled, cancelNow := context.WithCancel(context.Background())
	cancelNow()
	if err := inst.Audit(cancelled, TriggerClickHouseRestart); err == nil {
		t.Fatal("an audit on a cancelled context succeeded")
	}
	if inst.Stats().AuditClean {
		t.Fatal("the audit is clean although the restart audit did not complete")
	}
	f.mustApply(inst, s1)
	if s := inst.Stats(); !s.AuditClean || s.AuditRuns[TriggerClickHouseRestart] != 3 {
		t.Fatalf("stats = %+v, want Apply to have rerun the restart audit (3 runs) and be clean", s)
	}
}
```

```go
package install

import (
	"context"
	"os"
	"testing"
	"time"

	clickhouse "github.com/ClickHouse/clickhouse-go/v2"

	"github.com/sentioxyz/arbiter-core/dataplane/chrestart"
	"github.com/sentioxyz/arbiter-core/dataplane/chtest"
)

// requireRestartableCH returns a connection to CH_RESTART_ADDR: a ClickHouse
// whose container restarts itself (docker --restart always, fixed host port)
// and that no other test target shares (scripts/ci/clickhouse-mechanics.sh's
// node B).
func requireRestartableCH(t *testing.T) clickhouse.Conn {
	t.Helper()
	if os.Getenv("ARBITER_CH_RESTART") != "1" {
		t.Skip("set ARBITER_CH_RESTART=1 and CH_RESTART_ADDR (a ClickHouse whose container restarts itself) to run")
	}
	addr := os.Getenv("CH_RESTART_ADDR")
	if addr == "" {
		t.Fatal("ARBITER_CH_RESTART=1 requires CH_RESTART_ADDR")
	}
	return chtest.Open(t, addr)
}

// waitUptime waits until the server has been up for at least d, so that a
// restart moves its start time by more than chrestart's skew.
func waitUptime(t *testing.T, ctx context.Context, conn clickhouse.Conn, d time.Duration) {
	t.Helper()
	deadline := time.Now().Add(d + time.Minute)
	for {
		started, err := chrestart.StartedAt(ctx, conn, time.Now())
		if err == nil && time.Since(started) >= d {
			return
		}
		if time.Now().After(deadline) {
			t.Fatalf("server not up for %v after a minute (last error %v)", d, err)
		}
		time.Sleep(time.Second)
	}
}

// killClickHouse aborts the server with SYSTEM KILL, the abrupt restart that
// mechanics M3 pins as reactivating the parts a partition replacement retired,
// and waits until it answers again with a later start time.
func killClickHouse(t *testing.T, ctx context.Context, conn clickhouse.Conn) {
	t.Helper()
	before, err := chrestart.StartedAt(ctx, conn, time.Now())
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("start time before the kill: %v", err)
	}
	// The server dies while it answers, so the statement's own error is expected.
	_ = conn.Exec(ctx, "SYSTEM KILL")
	deadline := time.Now().Add(2 * time.Minute)
	for time.Now().Before(deadline) {
		time.Sleep(500 * time.Millisecond)
		probeCtx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(ctx, 5*time.Second)
		after, err := chrestart.StartedAt(probeCtx, conn, time.Now())
		cancel()
		if err == nil && after.After(before.Add(chrestart.DefaultRestartSkew)) {
			return
		}
	}
	t.Fatal("ClickHouse did not come back with a later start time within 2m: does its container run with --restart always?")
}

// TestInstallDivergedRepairSurvivesAReloadInsideTheOutdatedWindow: a Diverged
// partition repaired with DROP PARTITION and ATTACH PARTITION ... FROM stays
// repaired across an abrupt ClickHouse restart well inside old_parts_lifetime
// (480 s): the dropped foreign part does not come back and no twin appears,
// so the restart audit is clean and the next pass has nothing to do (spec §2,
// §8.5 step 2, §17 "Diverged repair with a reload inside the outdated
// window"; mechanics M4).
func TestInstallDivergedRepairSurvivesAReloadInsideTheOutdatedWindow(t *testing.T) {
	conn := requireRestartableCH(t)
	ctx := context.Background()
	f := newFixture(t, conn)
	c := f.table(0, "dex.swaps", 3, false)
	f.setSources(0, f.source("owner_pull", f.pull(1)))
	inst := f.newInstaller(nil)
	f.start(inst)
	f.promote(c, row{"", 1})
	f.promote(c, row{"", 2})
	s1 := f.update("s1", 10, c)
	f.mustApply(inst, s1)
	f.insertInto(f.pinned.ReplicaDB, c.Table, row{"", 77})

	inst = f.newInstaller(nil)
	f.start(inst)
	repairedAt := time.Now()
	f.mustApply(inst, s1)
	f.requireCopyEqualsManifest(c, s1)
	if s := inst.Stats(); s.DivergedPartitions[0] != 1 || !s.AuditClean {
		t.Fatalf("stats after the repair = %+v, want one Diverged partition, repaired", s)
	}
	repaired := f.copyParts(c)

	waitUptime(t, ctx, conn, 2*chrestart.DefaultRestartSkew)
	killClickHouse(t, ctx, conn)
	if since := time.Since(repairedAt); since >= 480*time.Second {
		t.Fatalf("the restart came %s after the repair, outside the outdated-part window", since)
	}
	f.requireCopyEqualsManifest(c, s1)
	if parts := f.copyParts(c); len(parts) != len(repaired) {
		t.Fatalf("copy parts after the restart = %+v, want the %d repaired ones", parts, len(repaired))
	}
	inst = f.newInstaller(nil)
	f.conn.reset()
	f.start(inst)
	if err := inst.Audit(ctx, TriggerClickHouseRestart); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if s := inst.Stats(); !s.AuditClean || s.AuditDroppedTwins != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("stats after the restart = %+v, want a clean audit with no twin", s)
	}
	f.mustApply(inst, s1)
	if alters := f.conn.alters(); len(alters) != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("ALTER statements after the restart = %q, want none", alters)
	}
	t.Logf("install: the Diverged repair survived a restart %s after it", time.Since(repairedAt).Round(time.Second))
}
```

```go
package install

// TestScratchNamesCarryTheNodeIDAndBootNonce: install scratch tables are
// <node_id>_<boot_nonce>_<n> (spec §8.5 step 3), every one starts with the
// node's and the boot's prefix, and a boot nonce is 8 fresh lowercase hex
// characters.
func TestScratchNamesCarryTheNodeIDAndBootNonce(t *testing.T) {
	if got := ScratchName("member-a", "0123abcd", 7); got != "member-a_0123abcd_7" {
		t.Fatalf("ScratchName = %q", got)
	}
	if got := ScratchPrefix("member-a", "0123abcd"); got != "member-a_0123abcd_" {
		t.Fatalf("ScratchPrefix = %q", got)
	}
	if got := NodePrefix("member-a"); got != "member-a_" {
		t.Fatalf("NodePrefix = %q", got)
	}
	name := ScratchName("member-c", "89abcdef", 12)
	if !strings.HasPrefix(name, NodePrefix("member-c")) || !strings.HasPrefix(name, ScratchPrefix("member-c", "89abcdef")) {
		t.Fatalf("%q lacks its node or boot prefix", name)
	}
	if strings.HasPrefix(ScratchName("member-ab", "89abcdef", 1), NodePrefix("member-a")) {
		t.Fatal("member-ab's scratch starts with member-a's prefix")
	}
	nonce := regexp.MustCompile(`^[0-9a-f]{8}$`)
	seen := map[string]bool{}
	for range 64 {
		n, err := NewBootNonce()
		if err != nil {
			t.Fatal(err)
		}
		if !nonce.MatchString(n) {
			t.Fatalf("boot nonce %q is not 8 lowercase hex characters", n)
		}
		seen[n] = true
	}
	if len(seen) < 60 {
		t.Fatalf("64 boot nonces gave only %d distinct values", len(seen))
	}
}
```

```go
package install

import (
	"errors"
	"os"
	"path/filepath"
	"slices"
	"syscall"
	"testing"
)

// TestClearForeignRefusesWhileTheStateDirIsLocked: clear-foreign is offline,
// so it refuses while a running si-member holds <state_dir>/LOCK; once the
// lock is free it lifts the quarantine and marks every partition the table
// lists Diverged, so the next start rebuilds the copy and drops the scratch.
func TestClearForeignRefusesWhileTheStateDirIsLocked(t *testing.T) {
	dir := t.TempDir()
	j := newJournal("member-a")
	j.owner(0).Tables["dex.swaps"] = &TableJournal{
		IncarnationSeq: 3, Copy: "dex__swaps__i3", Foreign: true, ForeignScratch: "member-a_0123abcd_7",
		Parts: []JournalPart{{Name: "all_1_1_0", PartitionID: "all"}, {Name: "p_x_2_2_0", PartitionID: "p_x"}},
	}
	j.owner(0).Tables["dex.pools"] = &TableJournal{IncarnationSeq: 4, Copy: "dex__pools__i4"}
	if err := writeJournal(filepath.Join(dir, JournalFile), j); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	lock, err := os.OpenFile(filepath.Join(dir, LockFile), os.O_RDWR|os.O_CREATE, 0o600)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if err := syscall.Flock(int(lock.Fd()), syscall.LOCK_EX|syscall.LOCK_NB); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	err = ClearForeign(dir, "dex.swaps")
	if !errors.Is(err, ErrStateDirLocked) || err.Error() != "install: state dir "+dir+" is locked by a running si-member" {
		t.Fatalf("ClearForeign under the lock = %v", err)
	}
	if err := syscall.Flock(int(lock.Fd()), syscall.LOCK_UN); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	_ = lock.Close()

	if err := ClearForeign(dir, "dex.pools"); err == nil || err.Error() != "install: dex.pools is not quarantined as foreign in "+filepath.Join(dir, JournalFile) {
		t.Fatalf("ClearForeign of a table that is not foreign = %v", err)
	}
	if err := ClearForeign(dir, "dex.swaps"); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	got, err := readJournal(filepath.Join(dir, JournalFile))
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	tj := got.Owners["0"].Tables["dex.swaps"]
	if tj.Foreign || tj.ForeignScratch != "" || !slices.Equal(tj.Diverged, []string{"all", "p_x"}) {
		t.Fatalf("journal after clear-foreign = %+v, want no quarantine and both partitions Diverged", tj)
	}
	if err := ClearForeign(t.TempDir(), "dex.swaps"); err == nil {
		t.Fatal("ClearForeign without a journal succeeded")
	}
}
```

```go
package install

import (
	"context"
	"os"
	"path/filepath"
	"regexp"
	"slices"
	"strings"
	"testing"
	"time"

	"github.com/housegate/housegate/pkg/replay/payloadexec"

	"github.com/sentioxyz/arbiter-core/member/sources"
)

type noCopies struct{}

func (noCopies) Copies() []copyset.Copy           { return nil }
func (noCopies) Copy(string) (copyset.Copy, bool) { return copyset.Copy{}, false }
func noSources(uint64) []sources.Source           { return nil }

// TestInstallNeverIssuesReplacePartition: no source file of the package
// renders a replacing partition statement (spec §8.5 step 2: a copy is
// repaired with DROP PARTITION and ATTACH PARTITION ... FROM), nor an
// OPTIMIZE, TRUNCATE or SYSTEM DROP REPLICA (Plan S3-C2 Global Constraints);
// every ClickHouse-gated test also fails on any of them through
// recordingConn.
func TestInstallNeverIssuesReplacePartition(t *testing.T) {
	files, err := filepath.Glob("*.go")
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	forbidden := regexp.MustCompile(`(?i)replace\s+partition|"REPLACE|\boptimize\s+table\b|\btruncate\s+table\b|\bsystem\s+drop\s+replica\b`)
	checked := 0
	for _, name := range files {
		if strings.HasSuffix(name, "_test.go") {
			continue
		}
		b, err := os.ReadFile(name)
		if err != nil {
			t.Fatal(err)
		}
		if loc := forbidden.FindIndex(b); loc != nil {
			t.Errorf("%s renders a replacing partition statement: %q", name, b[loc[0]:loc[1]])
		}
		checked++
	}
	if checked != 5 {
		t.Fatalf("checked %d source files, want the package's 5 (installer, journal, audit, scratch, foreign)", checked)
	}
}

// namedSource is a source that only has a name.
type namedSource string

func (n namedSource) Name() string { return string(n) }

func (namedSource) Fetch(context.Context, sources.Need, payloadexec.TableSchema, sources.Scratch) sources.Result {
	return sources.Result{}
}

// TestRestoreBeforeOwnerPullKeepsTheOtherSourcesInOrder: the bootstrap probe's
// order (Plan S3-C2 review fix 245-4) moves the restore right before the owner
// pull and changes nothing else; a source in front of the owner pull stays in
// front, and a list without a restore or without an owner pull, or with the
// restore already in front, is returned as it is.
func TestRestoreBeforeOwnerPullKeepsTheOtherSourcesInOrder(t *testing.T) {
	for _, tc := range []struct{ in, want []string }{
		{[]string{"owner_pull", "peer_unsafe_pull", "restore"}, []string{"restore", "owner_pull", "peer_unsafe_pull"}},
		{[]string{"member_unsafe_hardlink", "owner_pull", "peer_unsafe_pull", "restore"}, []string{"member_unsafe_hardlink", "restore", "owner_pull", "peer_unsafe_pull"}},
		{[]string{"owner_pull", "peer_unsafe_pull"}, []string{"owner_pull", "peer_unsafe_pull"}},
		{[]string{"peer_unsafe_pull", "restore"}, []string{"peer_unsafe_pull", "restore"}},
		{[]string{"restore", "owner_pull"}, []string{"restore", "owner_pull"}},
	} {
		in := make([]sources.Source, 0, len(tc.in))
		for _, name := range tc.in {
			in = append(in, namedSource(name))
		}
		var got []string
		for _, s := range restoreBeforeOwnerPull(in) {
			got = append(got, s.Name())
		}
		if !slices.Equal(got, tc.want) {
			t.Fatalf("restoreBeforeOwnerPull(%v) = %v, want %v", tc.in, got, tc.want)
		}
	}
}

// TestNewRefusesAnInvalidConfig: New refuses a configuration it cannot run
// with before it touches ClickHouse.
func TestNewRefusesAnInvalidConfig(t *testing.T) {
	dir := t.TempDir()
	good := Config{Pinned: ddl.DefaultMemberPinned("member-a", 0, ""), NetworkID: "n", StateDir: dir, BootNonce: "0123abcd", DiskBudgetBytes: 1}
	deps := Deps{Conn: &recordingConn{}, Copies: noCopies{}, Sources: noSources}
	if _, err := New(good, deps); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("New(good) = %v", err)
	}
	for _, tc := range []struct {
		name   string
		change func(*Config, *Deps)
		want   string
	}{
		{"node id", func(c *Config, _ *Deps) { c.Pinned.NodeID = "Member_A" }, `install: node id "Member_A" must match`},
		{"databases", func(c *Config, _ *Deps) { c.Pinned.StageDB = c.Pinned.ReplicaDB }, "install: Pinned needs distinct ReplicaDB and StageDB"},
		{"boot nonce", func(c *Config, _ *Deps) { c.BootNonce = "0123ABCD" }, `install: boot nonce "0123ABCD" must be 8 lowercase hex characters`},
		{"network", func(c *Config, _ *Deps) { c.NetworkID = "" }, "install: NetworkID and StateDir are required"},
		{"budget", func(c *Config, _ *Deps) { c.DiskBudgetBytes = 0 }, "install: disk budget is required"},
		{"ratio", func(c *Config, _ *Deps) { c.StopInstallsRatio = 1 }, "install: stop_installs_ratio must satisfy 0 < ratio < 1, got 1"},
		{"self-audit", func(c *Config, _ *Deps) { c.SelfAuditInterval = time.Minute }, "install: self_audit_interval must be at least 10m, got 1m0s"},
		{"deps", func(_ *Config, d *Deps) { d.Sources = nil }, "install: Deps needs Conn, Copies and Sources"},
		{"state dir", func(c *Config, _ *Deps) { c.StateDir = filepath.Join(dir, "missing") }, "install: state dir " + filepath.Join(dir, "missing") + " is not a directory"},
		{"journal node", func(c *Config, _ *Deps) {
			c.StateDir = t.TempDir()
			if err := writeJournal(filepath.Join(c.StateDir, JournalFile), newJournal("member-b")); err != nil {
				t.Fatal(err)
			}
		}, `belongs to node "member-b", not "member-a"`},
	} {
		t.Run(tc.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			cfg, d := good, deps
			tc.change(&cfg, &d)
			_, err := New(cfg, d)
			if err == nil || !strings.Contains(err.Error(), tc.want) {
				t.Fatalf("New = %v, want %q", err, tc.want)
			}
		})
	}
}
```

- [ ] **Step 7: Implement the journal**

Create `member/install/journal.go`:

```go
package install

import (
	"encoding/json"
	"errors"
	"fmt"
	"io/fs"
	"os"
	"path/filepath"
	"slices"
	"strconv"
	"strings"

	"github.com/housegate/housegate/pkg/replay"
)

// JournalFile is the installer's journal in Config.StateDir. Nothing but this
// package writes it; Plan S3-E1 keeps its own files beside it.
const JournalFile = "install-journal.json"

// journalVersion is the only Journal.Version this package reads and writes.
const journalVersion = 1

// Journal records what every copy holds (housegate spec 2026-10-14 §8.5 step
// 7): per owner, the manifest and track frontier its copies were last brought
// to together, and per table the parts installed into its copy.
type Journal struct {
	Version int                      `json:"version"` // 1
	NodeID  string                   `json:"node_id"`
	Owners  map[string]*OwnerJournal `json:"owners"` // key: decimal indexer id
}

// OwnerJournal is one owner's part of the journal. SnapshotID and Entry move
// together with every table of the owner, in one write, once every ready copy
// of the owner closed at that manifest.
type OwnerJournal struct {
	SnapshotID string                   `json:"snapshot_id"`
	Entry      replay.TrackFrontier     `json:"entry"`
	Tables     map[string]*TableJournal `json:"tables"` // key: <database>.<table>
}

// TableJournal is one copy: its incarnation, its physical name in ReplicaDB
// and the parts it holds. Diverged lists the partitions awaiting a rebuild
// (spec §8.5 step 2); Foreign quarantines the whole table (Plan S3-C2 K36)
// and ForeignScratch names the hg_rstage table kept for forensics.
type TableJournal struct {
	IncarnationSeq uint64        `json:"incarnation_seq"`
	Copy           string        `json:"copy"`
	Parts          []JournalPart `json:"parts"`
	Diverged       []string      `json:"diverged,omitempty"` // partition ids awaiting repair
	Foreign        bool          `json:"foreign,omitempty"`
	ForeignScratch string        `json:"foreign_scratch,omitempty"`
}

// JournalPart is one installed part, by its name in the copy.
type JournalPart struct {
	Name           string `json:"name"`
	PartitionID    string `json:"partition_id"`
	PartRowLtHash  string `json:"part_row_lthash"`
	HashOfAllFiles string `json:"hash_of_all_files"`
	Rows           uint64 `json:"rows"`
}

func newJournal(nodeID string) *Journal {
	return &Journal{Version: journalVersion, NodeID: nodeID, Owners: map[string]*OwnerJournal{}}
}

func ownerKey(owner uint64) string { return strconv.FormatUint(owner, 10) }

// readJournal reads path; a missing file is (nil, nil).
func readJournal(path string) (*Journal, error) {
	b, err := os.ReadFile(path)
	if errors.Is(err, fs.ErrNotExist) {
		return nil, nil
	}
	if err != nil {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("install: read journal %s: %w", path, err)
	}
	var j Journal
	if err := json.Unmarshal(b, &j); err != nil {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("install: journal %s: %w", path, err)
	}
	if j.Version != journalVersion {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("install: journal %s has version %d, want %d", path, j.Version, journalVersion)
	}
	if j.Owners == nil {
		j.Owners = map[string]*OwnerJournal{}
	}
	for key, oj := range j.Owners {
		if _, err := strconv.ParseUint(key, 10, 64); err != nil || oj == nil {
			return nil, fmt.Errorf("install: journal %s has a bad owner entry %q", path, key)
		}
		if oj.Tables == nil {
			oj.Tables = map[string]*TableJournal{}
		}
		for tableKey, tj := range oj.Tables {
			if tj == nil {
				return nil, fmt.Errorf("install: journal %s has an empty entry for table %s", path, tableKey)
			}
		}
	}
	return &j, nil
}

// writeJournal replaces path atomically: a temp file in the same directory,
// Sync, rename, directory Sync (the arbiter-core:snode/state.go pattern), so a
// crash leaves either the old or the new journal.
func writeJournal(path string, j *Journal) error {
	b, err := json.MarshalIndent(j, "", "  ")
	if err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("install: encode journal: %w", err)
	}
	dir := filepath.Dir(path)
	tmp, err := os.CreateTemp(dir, ".install-journal-*")
	if err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("install: write journal: %w", err)
	}
	defer func() { _ = os.Remove(tmp.Name()) }()
	if _, err := tmp.Write(b); err != nil {
		_ = tmp.Close()
		return fmt.Errorf("install: write journal: %w", err)
	}
	if err := tmp.Sync(); err != nil {
		_ = tmp.Close()
		return fmt.Errorf("install: sync journal: %w", err)
	}
	if err := tmp.Close(); err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("install: write journal: %w", err)
	}
	if err := os.Rename(tmp.Name(), path); err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("install: replace journal: %w", err)
	}
	d, err := os.Open(dir)
	if err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("install: sync state dir: %w", err)
	}
	defer d.Close()
	if err := d.Sync(); err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("install: sync state dir: %w", err)
	}
	return nil
}

func (j *Journal) clone() *Journal {
	out := &Journal{Version: j.Version, NodeID: j.NodeID, Owners: make(map[string]*OwnerJournal, len(j.Owners))}
	for key, oj := range j.Owners {
		out.Owners[key] = oj.clone()
	}
	return out
}

func (oj *OwnerJournal) clone() *OwnerJournal {
	out := &OwnerJournal{SnapshotID: oj.SnapshotID, Entry: oj.Entry, Tables: make(map[string]*TableJournal, len(oj.Tables))}
	for key, tj := range oj.Tables {
		out.Tables[key] = tj.clone()
	}
	return out
}

func (tj *TableJournal) clone() *TableJournal {
	out := *tj
	out.Parts = slices.Clone(tj.Parts)
	out.Diverged = slices.Clone(tj.Diverged)
	return &out
}

// owner returns the owner's journal, creating it.
func (j *Journal) owner(owner uint64) *OwnerJournal {
	oj := j.Owners[ownerKey(owner)]
	if oj == nil {
		oj = &OwnerJournal{Tables: map[string]*TableJournal{}}
		j.Owners[ownerKey(owner)] = oj
	}
	return oj
}

// partitionHashes is L of spec §8.5 step 1: the row hashes the journal lists
// for one partition, repeats kept.
func (tj *TableJournal) partitionHashes(partitionID string) []string {
	var out []string
	for _, p := range tj.Parts {
		if p.PartitionID == partitionID {
			out = append(out, p.PartRowLtHash)
		}
	}
	return out
}

// partitions lists, sorted, the partitions the journal lists parts of.
func (tj *TableJournal) partitions() []string {
	var out []string
	for _, p := range tj.Parts {
		out = append(out, p.PartitionID)
	}
	slices.Sort(out)
	return slices.Compact(out)
}

func (tj *TableJournal) isDiverged(partitionID string) bool {
	return slices.Contains(tj.Diverged, partitionID)
}

// markDiverged records partitionID as awaiting a rebuild; it reports whether
// the partition was not marked yet.
func (tj *TableJournal) markDiverged(partitionID string) bool {
	if tj.isDiverged(partitionID) {
		return false
	}
	tj.Diverged = append(tj.Diverged, partitionID)
	slices.Sort(tj.Diverged)
	return true
}

// setPartition makes parts the journaled content of partitionID and clears
// its Diverged mark.
func (tj *TableJournal) setPartition(partitionID string, parts []JournalPart) {
	tj.Parts = slices.DeleteFunc(tj.Parts, func(p JournalPart) bool { return p.PartitionID == partitionID })
	tj.Parts = append(tj.Parts, parts...)
	sortJournalParts(tj.Parts)
	tj.Diverged = slices.DeleteFunc(tj.Diverged, func(p string) bool { return p == partitionID })
}

func (tj *TableJournal) addParts(parts ...JournalPart) {
	tj.Parts = append(tj.Parts, parts...)
	sortJournalParts(tj.Parts)
}

func sortJournalParts(parts []JournalPart) {
	slices.SortFunc(parts, func(a, b JournalPart) int {
		if c := strings.Compare(a.PartitionID, b.PartitionID); c != 0 {
			return c
		}
		return strings.Compare(a.Name, b.Name)
	})
}
```

- [ ] **Step 8: Implement scratch names and the startup drop**

Create `member/install/scratch.go`:

```go
package install

import (
	"context"
	"crypto/rand"
	"encoding/hex"
	"fmt"
	"strconv"
	"strings"
	"time"

	"github.com/housegate/housegate/pkg/replay/payloadexec"

	"github.com/sentioxyz/arbiter-core/dataplane/ddl"
	"github.com/sentioxyz/arbiter-core/member/sources"
)

// scratchDropTimeout bounds the DROP TABLE of one scratch, which runs on a
// context of its own so a cancelled pass still removes what it created.
const scratchDropTimeout = 30 * time.Second

// NewBootNonce returns 8 lowercase hex characters from crypto/rand. The
// si-member draws a new one at every process start, so the scratch tables of
// one boot never share a name with those of an earlier one (housegate spec
// 2026-10-14 §8.5 step 3).
func NewBootNonce() (string, error) {
	var b [4]byte
	if _, err := rand.Read(b[:]); err != nil {
		return "", fmt.Errorf("install: draw the boot nonce: %w", err)
	}
	return hex.EncodeToString(b[:]), nil
}

// NodePrefix starts the name of every StageDB table of the member nodeID, of
// every boot: install, restore and replay scratch alike. A node id holds no
// underscore (Plan S3-C2 K29), so no other node's prefix starts with it.
func NodePrefix(nodeID string) string { return nodeID + "_" }

// ScratchPrefix starts the name of every StageDB table of one boot.
func ScratchPrefix(nodeID, bootNonce string) string { return nodeID + "_" + bootNonce + "_" }

// ScratchName is the n-th install scratch table of one boot,
// <node_id>_<boot_nonce>_<n> (spec §8.5 step 3).
func ScratchName(nodeID, bootNonce string, n uint64) string {
	return ScratchPrefix(nodeID, bootNonce) + strconv.FormatUint(n, 10)
}

// newScratch creates the next empty install scratch in StageDB with the
// copy's structure, settings and storage policy (ddl.ScratchIntent), so that
// ATTACH PARTITION ... FROM it into the copy is accepted.
func (i *Installer) newScratch(ctx context.Context, schema payloadexec.TableSchema) (sources.Scratch, error) {
	name := ScratchName(i.cfg.Pinned.NodeID, i.cfg.BootNonce, i.scratchN.Add(1))
	intent, err := ddl.ScratchIntent(i.cfg.Pinned, schema, name)
	if err != nil {
		return sources.Scratch{}, fmt.Errorf("install: scratch for %s: %w", schema.TableID, err)
	}
	if err := i.d.Conn.Exec(ctx, intent.SQL()); err != nil {
		return sources.Scratch{}, fmt.Errorf("install: create scratch %s.%s: %w", i.cfg.Pinned.StageDB, name, err)
	}
	return sources.Scratch{Database: i.cfg.Pinned.StageDB, Table: name}, nil
}

// dropScratch drops one scratch table. A failure is logged: the next start
// drops every table of this node's prefix anyway.
func (i *Installer) dropScratch(s sources.Scratch) {
	ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), scratchDropTimeout)
	defer cancel()
	if err := i.d.Conn.Exec(ctx, "DROP TABLE IF EXISTS "+qualified(s.Database, s.Table)+" SYNC"); err != nil {
		i.d.Logger.Warn("install: dropping a scratch table failed; the next start drops it", "scratch", s.Database+"."+s.Table, "err", err)
	}
}

// DropStaleScratch drops every StageDB table whose name starts with this
// node's prefix (spec §8.5, last paragraph): the install, restore and replay
// scratch of every earlier boot. It keeps only a scratch the journal holds as
// a table's foreign_scratch (Plan S3-C2 K36), which ClearForeign releases.
// The role calls it once at startup, before the startup audit and before
// anything of this boot creates a scratch.
func (i *Installer) DropStaleScratch(ctx context.Context) error {
	i.work.Lock()
	defer i.work.Unlock()
	prefix := NodePrefix(i.cfg.Pinned.NodeID)
	names, err := ddl.ListStageTables(ctx, i.d.Conn, i.cfg.Pinned, prefix)
	if err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("install: list the %s tables of %s: %w", i.cfg.Pinned.StageDB, prefix, err)
	}
	kept := i.foreignScratches()
	for _, name := range names {
		if !strings.HasPrefix(name, prefix) {
			continue
		}
		if kept[name] {
			i.d.Logger.Warn("install: keeping a foreign scratch for forensics", "scratch", i.cfg.Pinned.StageDB+"."+name)
			continue
		}
		if err := i.d.Conn.Exec(ctx, "DROP TABLE IF EXISTS "+qualified(i.cfg.Pinned.StageDB, name)+" SYNC"); err != nil {
			return fmt.Errorf("install: drop the stale scratch %s.%s: %w", i.cfg.Pinned.StageDB, name, err)
		}
		i.d.Logger.Info("install: dropped a stale scratch table", "scratch", i.cfg.Pinned.StageDB+"."+name)
	}
	return nil
}

func quoteIdent(id string) string {
	id = strings.ReplaceAll(id, `\`, `\\`)
	id = strings.ReplaceAll(id, "`", "``")
	return "`" + id + "`"
}

func qualified(database, table string) string { return quoteIdent(database) + "." + quoteIdent(table) }

func quoteLiteral(s string) string {
	s = strings.ReplaceAll(s, `\`, `\\`)
	s = strings.ReplaceAll(s, `'`, `\'`)
	return "'" + s + "'"
}
```

- [ ] **Step 9: Implement the offline quarantine release**

Create `member/install/foreign.go`:

```go
package install

import (
	"errors"
	"fmt"
	"maps"
	"os"
	"path/filepath"
	"slices"
	"sort"
	"syscall"
)

// LockFile is the si-member's state-directory lock (Plan S3-C2 contract
// §23.1, member.LockFile): the running role holds an exclusive flock on it,
// so ClearForeign, an offline command, refuses while the role runs.
const LockFile = "LOCK"

// ErrStateDirLocked reports that a running si-member holds the state
// directory's lock.
var ErrStateDirLocked = errors.New("install: state dir is locked")

// ClearForeign releases the local quarantine of one table (Plan S3-C2 K36),
// offline, for `sentio-node si-member clear-foreign --table <db.table>`. It
// takes the state directory's lock itself, so it refuses while an si-member
// runs on stateDir. The table's journal loses its foreign mark and its
// foreign_scratch, and every partition it lists is marked Diverged, so the
// next start drops the kept scratch (DropStaleScratch) and rebuilds the copy
// partition by partition through the gate (DROP PARTITION, then ATTACH
// PARTITION ... FROM fresh scratch), trusting none of its parts. tableKey is
// the logical <database>.<table>.
func ClearForeign(stateDir, tableKey string) error {
	unlock, err := lockStateDir(stateDir)
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	defer unlock()
	path := filepath.Join(stateDir, JournalFile)
	j, err := readJournal(path)
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	if j == nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("install: no install journal in %s", stateDir)
	}
	cleared := 0
	for _, owner := range slices.Sorted(maps.Keys(j.Owners)) {
		tj := j.Owners[owner].Tables[tableKey]
		if tj == nil || !tj.Foreign {
			continue
		}
		for _, p := range tj.partitions() {
			tj.markDiverged(p)
		}
		tj.Foreign, tj.ForeignScratch = false, ""
		cleared++
	}
	if cleared == 0 {
		return fmt.Errorf("install: %s is not quarantined as foreign in %s", tableKey, path)
	}
	return writeJournal(path, j)
}

// lockStateDir takes the exclusive, non-blocking flock that a running
// si-member holds on <stateDir>/LOCK.
func lockStateDir(stateDir string) (func(), error) {
	f, err := os.OpenFile(filepath.Join(stateDir, LockFile), os.O_RDWR|os.O_CREATE, 0o600)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("install: open the lock of state dir %s: %w", stateDir, err)
	}
	if err := syscall.Flock(int(f.Fd()), syscall.LOCK_EX|syscall.LOCK_NB); err != nil {
		_ = f.Close()
		if errors.Is(err, syscall.EWOULDBLOCK) {
			return nil, refuse(ErrStateDirLocked, "install: state dir %s is locked by a running si-member", stateDir)
		}
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("install: lock state dir %s: %w", stateDir, err)
	}
	return func() {
		_ = syscall.Flock(int(f.Fd()), syscall.LOCK_UN)
		_ = f.Close()
	}, nil
}

// foreignScratches lists the scratch tables the journal keeps for forensics.
func (i *Installer) foreignScratches() map[string]bool {
	i.mu.Lock()
	defer i.mu.Unlock()
	out := map[string]bool{}
	for _, oj := range i.journal.Owners {
		for _, tj := range oj.Tables {
			if tj.Foreign && tj.ForeignScratch != "" {
				out[tj.ForeignScratch] = true
			}
		}
	}
	return out
}

// foreignTables lists, sorted, the table keys of owner the journal holds
// quarantined, whatever incarnation they belonged to.
func (i *Installer) foreignTables(owner uint64) []string {
	i.mu.Lock()
	defer i.mu.Unlock()
	oj := i.journal.Owners[ownerKey(owner)]
	if oj == nil {
		return nil
	}
	var out []string
	for key, tj := range oj.Tables {
		if tj.Foreign {
			out = append(out, key)
		}
	}
	sort.Strings(out)
	return out
}
```
